The Operator charged the joint account $1,064,082.17 for 12,975.39 ft of 8.625, 44.00,Q125 size casing on MB-010. Upon reconciliation of the well only 11,347.38 ft were used in the well including thread loss leading to an overcharge of $133,509.37. This was the subject of Information Request 051 raised during fieldwork.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $133,509.37 for the overcharge plus 2.5% overhead for a credit of $136,847.10.

table_references.summary: The table contains six financial transactions, all occurring in either September or October 2021, each identified by a unique reference number ranging from 406135436 to 406149114. The transaction amounts range from approximately **$1,637** to nearly **$6,991**, with five transactions occurring in 09/21 and one in 10/21. The total combined amount across all transactions is approximately **$21,616**.

This table is an invoice reconciliation summary from a vendor (Corporation OF) covering transactions between August 2020 and February 2022, tracking footage and charges for what appears to be oil/gas well tubular goods or piping. The total amount charged across all invoices was **$1,032,422.54** for **11,537.61 feet** at an average price of **$89.48 per foot**, spanning 253 conditions. A reconciliation against well records revealed an overcharge of **288.9 feet**, resulting in a credit/charge to the joint account of **$25,849.14**, after accounting for thread loss (112.75 ft) and fabrication adjustments (-138.87 ft).

This table tracks pipe/tubing inventory charges from a vendor (Corporation OF), covering invoices dated between August 2020 and February 2022, detailing joint counts, footage, and amounts charged for various well projects. The total charged across 253 joints was **$1,032,422.54** at an average price of **$89.48 per foot** over **11,537.61 feet**, while actual footage set in the well was **11,274.86 feet** per iWells reporting. The table reconciles the billed amount against what was actually run in the well, accounting for thread loss and fabrication, resulting in a small overage of **11.1 feet** and a credit/charge to the joint account of **$996.07**.

This table contains procurement or inventory data linking pipe/casing specifications (CSG, 8.625" diameter, Q125RY grade with VAM thread connections) to allocation numbers and line item text. Each row references a specific material identifier (e.g., 4513509779, 4513685070) paired with goods receipt (GR) details including joint counts, material batch numbers, and order references. The Allocation Number and Line Item Text columns appear to contain identical values, suggesting they serve as duplicate reference keys for tracking these casing string components.

table_references.summary: This table contains casing string specifications for three sections of a wellbore: an **Intermediate Liner** (11.875" OD, set at 17,926 ft on 06/01/2022), a **Production Liner** (7.625" OD, set at 21,337 ft on 06/13/2022), and a **Tieback String** (10.750" OD, set at 17,794 ft on 06/21/2022). Each section lists its individual casing components with details including outer/inner diameter, weight (lb/ft), steel grade, length, and depth. Components across all three strings are primarily 71.80–39 lb/ft pipe in grades such as VM125HC, Q125, and P110, with specialized items like float collars, reamer shoes, centralizer subs, and swellpackers included at various depths.

table_references.summary: This table tracks invoices from **Tenaris Global Services** for tubular goods (casing/pipe), covering 7 invoices dated between April–June 2020 and one credit memo in April 2021, all at a consistent price of **$94.29 per foot**. The total charged across 156 joints (7,245.76 feet) amounts to **$683,202.62**, with 147 joints (6,742.44 feet) confirmed set in the well and 9 joints held in yard inventory. After accounting for thread loss and inventory, there is a minor overage of 23.9 feet, resulting in a **credit to the joint account of $2,253.02**.

020.description:
The Operator charged the joint account $1,529,879.60 for 14,214.47 ft of 8.625, 44.00,VM95H size casing on MB-017. Upon reconciliation of the well only 12,313.37 ft were used in the well, including thread loss, leading to an overcharge of $204,611.71. This was the subject of Information Request 064 which was raised during the fieldwork.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $204,611.71 for the overcharge plus 2.5% overhead for a credit of $209,727.00.

table_references.summary: The table contains **5 financial transactions** from **September and October 2021**, each with a corresponding reference number. Transaction amounts range from approximately **$8,325 to $85,811**, with the largest being $85,810.79 (Ref. 406135419) and the smallest being $8,325.31 (Ref. 406144824). The total combined value of all transactions is approximately **$163,767**.

This table tracks vendor invoices for tubular goods or pipe (measured in footage and joints), spanning from October 2019 to October 2021, with a mix of charges and credits. The total amount charged across all invoices is **$1,366,112.32** for **12,570.51 feet**, at an average price of **$108.68 per foot**. A reconciliation at the bottom compares billed footage against what was actually set in the well (12,215.66 ft), resulting in an overcharge of **232.7 feet**, with a credit/charge to the joint account of **$25,288.18**.

The Non-Operator has reviewed the reconciliation provided by the Operator and disagrees with it. The Operator has performed the reconciliation using JADE for P110 grade pipe, and the iWells documents show Q125 grade pipe. Meanwhile the Joint Account has been charged for both P110 and Q125 grades of pipe, but iWells shows that only Q125 was used.

The Non-Operator respectfully resubmits the reconciliation provided in February showing zero consumption of P110 pipe (since Q125 was used) and requests credit to the Joint Account of $235,094.41 including 2.5% OH. The file is titled "2021-103 Exc 23 C.US.MR2.PD.18.007.0942A MA24 Recon.xlsx".

Note please see exception 24 of this same audit covering a reconciliation of the Q125RY pipe that was used in the well.

replies.text:
The material in question pertains to 4,670.34 feet of casing (CSG), 7.625", 39.00 lb/ft, P110, VAM TOP HC, R3, SMLS, for which total charges amount to $229,365.42.

However, according to the IWell report, the actual material installed was 4,669.37 feet plus 2,917.24 feet totaling of 7,586.61 feet of CSG, 7.625", 39.00 lb/ft, Q125RY, VAM TOP HC, which was not charged. Given that Q125RY is a higher-grade material, its cost is likely greater than that of P110.

This discrepancy warrants further investigation. As a result, the credit claim of $235,094.41 is denied pending resolution of the material variance.

## Summary

This table presents a billing reconciliation for tubular goods (measured in footage/units), showing a total charge of **$765,491.54** across **14,048.77 feet/units** at an average price of **$54.49 per foot**. After accounting for footage set in the well (6,612.72 ft), thread loss (1%), and adjusted totals, a significant **credit of $411,626.77** (including 2.5% overhead) is determined to be owed back to the joint account. A key dispute note flags that the Operator improperly mixed incompatible coupling types (VAM-TOP and Wedge 667), which should not be reconciled together.

After accounting for footage actually set in the well (13,837.87 ft), thread loss (1%), and an adjustment, there was an overcharge of **72.52 feet**, resulting in a **total credit of $4,050.40** due back to the joint account, including a 2.5% overhead charge of $98.79.

This table contains well completion and casing assembly data for the **MARSA-24 well** (MC08070CS, permit #30287262), covering drilling operations between **November 2021 and September 2022**. It documents multiple installed casing components including a **7.625" UTB Tieback Assembly**, a **Scab Liner**, a **Production Liner at 21,705'**, and a **7.625"x9.875" Tieback String**, all using **7.625" casing (33.7–39 ppf)** in grades **Q125RY/P110** with Wedge 667/Varst1 connections. Key length values range from short pup joints (~10 ft) to major casing strings exceeding **13,800 ft**, with installation dates primarily in **March–April 2022** and **August 2022**.

The Joint Account was charged the following SIEP invoices per attached JADE: These items relate to IR# 38, 42, 43, and 45 raised during fieldwork.

| SIEP Invoice No.   | TOTAL SIEP invoice amt   | Claimed Amount   |
|--------------------|--------------------------|------------------|
| 6706060103         | $99,303.87               | $89,316.27       |
| 6706061380         | $20,237.66               | $15,423.66       |
| 6706064339         | $14,717.50               | $15,377.50       |
| 6706060777         | $16,539.20               | $15,170.00       |
| 6706060417         | $49,483.79               | $4,202.75        |
| Total              |                          | $ 139,490.18     |

SIEP invoice 6706060103 includes the following charges to the Joint Account:

- a. Reservoir Imaging invoice 1907 for $39,480: The attached invoice notes that this charge is for GREAT WHITE 4D Consultant services.
- b. P3 Global Personnel for $8,370.74: This is for services of HSE Rep Richard Ball. We are unable to find Richard Ball on the PoB list and therefore unable to ascertain that Mr. Ball worked on Mars property.
- c. EPI invoices for Geoff Smith's services for $41,465.53. We cannot find Geoff Smith on the PoB list. Furthermore, we noted that the timesheet submitted by Mr. Smith notes that he was on Mars/Perdido but entire amount was charged to Mars.

SIEP inv 6706061380 includes the following charges from Reservoir Imaging invoices 1914 and 1916 which are for James Harrison's Great White 4D Consultant Services.

- [ ]  Invoice 1914: $11,517.09

- [ ]  Invoice 1916: $ 3,906.57

SIEP inv 6706064339 includes $15,377.50 of personnel charges for Alejandro Pessano. We are unable to locate Mr. Pessano on the PoB and therefore unable to ascertain that he worked on the Mars property.

The Joint Account was charged $15,170.00 via SIEP Inv 6706060777. However, no 3rd party invoice was attached as backup for the SIEP invoice. The Operator's response to IR 43 failed to address whom this charge is for and why this amount is charged to Mars.

SIEP invoice 6706060417 includes $ $ 4,202.75 of William Leibold's charges that were for VITO. (see page 6 of attached invoice-- amounts highlighted).

Please credit the Joint account $ 139,490.18 plus 2.5% overhead for a total of $ 142,977.43 for the above miscoded and unsubstantiated costs charged to the Mars property.

037.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account (Mars/Olympus) $122,247.84 for "PSP Award" which appears to be stock or stock options purchased/awarded to certain individuals. This was the subject of Information Request 53.

This Performance Share Plan is considered an Incentive Compensation Plan, and these costs should be covered by overhead rates. These payments do not directly benefit joint property, and there are no predetermined operational metrics to earn these awards. Finally, this Shell share program, as identified in the whitepaper provided with Information Request 53, is not made available to all employees that work on joint property. MFI-19 (1986 Offshore Accounting Procedure - Joint Operations) states, "Costs which are primarily beneficial to the Operator should be excluded from employee benefits and treated as Overhead, for which the Operator is compensated under the provisions of Section III. Such costs to be borne by the Operator would include...safety awards, service awards and other special benefits available only to executives, certain employees or groups on a selective basis."

replies.text:
Credit Denied. The four software applications are required to meet safety reporting and regulatory requirements. These four software applications are not accounting, or administrative software applications as mentioned in COPAS MFI 44. Therefore, no credit is due to the Joint Account. The benefits and function of the four software applications are as follows:

Enablon BBS is an HSSE application (Health, Safety, Security, Environmental) used by all offshore staff and contractors to document Behavior-Based Safety observations. Observation data is used as leading indicators to increase safety and reduce incidents. Results are also used to meet safety reporting and regulatory requirements.

IntelaTrac application include Chemical Analysis, Preventive maintenance, Production monitoring,

Production tank levels, Production flow rates.

UTL (Universal Tag Locator) is a production/operations application used by offshore staff (e.g., Deck Operators, Maintenance, Technicians, Operations Supervisors, etc.) to document and share relevant Shift and Situational Awareness information (e.g., production, operations, maintenance, HSSE, alarms, etc.) across the entire facility. Data is integrated from multiple source systems. Results are also used for shift handover, situational awareness, optimized maintenance, increased availability, and reduced deferment.

Connected Field Worker (CFW) is a production/operations set of IT tools used by offshore staff (e.g., Deck Operators, Maintenance, Operations Supervisors, etc.) including On-deck wireless connectivity, Mobile Device Automated Support, MS Productivity Tools (e.g., MS Teams, Sharepoint), and SAP mobile tools (e.g., Work Request, Work Execution). The platform supports Operator Rounds, Virtual Inspections, Over-the-shoulder Coaching, Commissioning & startup activities, etc., resulting in increased situational awareness, optimized maintenance, increased availability, and reduced deferment.

The Operator's mention of the activities being for "maintenance planning, scheduling activities, or preventative maintenance" follow the February 2019 Letter Agreement, Section 3.3

## 3. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration

OTL is chargeable by the Operator to the joint account for planners, schedulers, and plan execution supporters working on facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities.

The costs in question cannot, however, be classified as OTL as they do not meet the definition of "Technical Employee" as contemplated by the February 2019 Letter Agreement:

## 2. Definition of"Technical Employees"

"Technical Employees" shall mean those employees, having special and specific engineering, geological, geophysical technical or operational skills (including planners, schedulers and execution support for facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities), and whose function in Joint Operations (as defined in the Mars UOA) is providing services for the benefit of the Joint Property (as defined in the Mars UOA).

The Definition does not mention any aspect related to IT skills. Therefore full credit remains due.

## Credit Denied:

Established in 2011, the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) is the lead agency in the United States Department of Interior in charge of improving safety and ensuring environmental protection relating to the offshore energy industry. This was in response to the Minerals Management Service (MMS) regulatory failure related to the Deepwater Horizon oil spill in 2010. The BSEE established a performance-based approach to integrating and managing offshore operations known as Safety and Environmental Management System (SEMS). Within SEMS there are various Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) that require an Operator to follow and adhere to. Examples of the more common CFR's are as follows:

- CFR 250.1910 - What safety and environmental information is required?
- CFR 250.1913 - What criteria for operating procedures must my SEMS program meet?
- CFR 250.1916 - What criteria for mechanical integrity must my SEMS program meet?

The Operator incurs various costs in order to comply with the aforementioned government mandates as part of the operations of the Joint Venture. Therefore, these costs should be charged to the Joint Account and shared with the Co-Owner(s).

To have information of association of personnel name to dollars charged to the Joint Account, how much did the Joint Account pay for X individual, what job were they working on and a dollar cost breakdown per employee are audit tasks or reviews that should have been performed by the auditor during the field audit.

Unfortunately, based on the support provided with this exception, the auditor did not do any of recommended steps to review these payroll charges. 050.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $96,661.94 for P&T charges as noted in the attached JADE. This was raised in information Request 113. The Operator indicated that these charges were for an individual Fan Shejun who was covering activities conducted by the Metocean team as noted below:

Metocean data is critical for decision making when conducting weather sensitive activities; therefore, routine inspections and planned maintenance shall be performed. Fan Shejun covers the activities that will be conducted by the Metocean Team under the Gulf of Mexico. Metocean Monitoring and Operational Support (MMOS) program. The work will focus on operational support, data utilization, instrumentation specialty engineering, and technology awareness. These activities are needed to enable life extension programs, efficient operations, safe platform operations, and quick post-storm recovery to production.

Upon reviewing the 2018 Settlement Agreement Exhibit "C" Section 3. OTL-Chargeable Activities, the above costs do not appear to be 1. Regulatory Activity, 2. Feasibility and Project Studies, or 3. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration".

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $96,661.94 plus 13% Overhead for the Affiliate Labor not in compliance with the Settlement Agreement.

Credit Denied. The two cost centers; CC 101039 and CC 101013 in question are Mars Operation Home cost centers. Please see the attached staff listing file for employee information that charged to these two Mars home cost centers. All the employees in these two CC are directly employed on the Mars in the conduct of Mars Joint Operation. Per Mars UOA, Exhibit C, II Direct Charges, 2. labor (see below), these payroll costs are directly chargeable to the Joint account.

## II. DIRECT CHARGES

Operator shall charge the Joint Account with the following items:

1. Rentals and Royalties

Lease rentals and royalties paid by Operator for the Joint Operations.

## 2. Labor

- (2) Salaries and wages of Operator's employees directly employed on Shore Base Facilities or other Offshore Facilities serving the Joint Property if such costs are not charged under Paragraph 7 of this Section II.
- A. (1) Salaries and wages of Operator's field employees directly employed on the Joint Property in the conduct of Joint Operations.
- (3) Salaries of First Level Supervisors in the field.
- (4) Salaries and wages of Technicaļ Employees directly employed on the Joint Property if such charges are excluded from the Overhead rates.
- B. Operator's cost of holiday, vacation, sickness and disability benefits and other customary allowances paid to employees whose salaries and wages are chargeable to the Joint Account under Paragraph 2A of this Section II. Such costs under this Paragraph 2B may be charged on a "when and as paid basis" or by "percentage assessment" on the amount of salaries and wages chargeable to the Joint Account under Paragraph2A of this Section II. If percentage assessment is used, the rate shall be based on the Operator's cost experience.
- (5) Salaries and wages of Technical Employees either temporarily or permanently assigned to and directly employed in the operation of the Joint Property if such charges are excluded from the overhead rates.
- C. Expenditures or contributions made pursuant to assessments imposed by governmental authority which are applicable to Operator's costs chargeable to the Joint Account under Paragraphs 2A and 2B of this Section II.
- D. Personal Expenses of those employees whose salaries and wages are chargeable to the Joint Account under Paragraph 2A of this Section II.

## 3. Employee Benefits

Operator's current costs of established plans for employees' group life insurance, hospitalization, pension, retirement, stock purchase, thrift, bonus, and other benefit plans of a like narure, applicable to Operator's labor cost chargeable to the Joint Account under Paragraphs 2A and 2B of this Section II shall be Operator's actual cost not to exceed the percent most recently recommended by the Council of Petroleum Accountants Societies.

Partial credit of $5,639.95 for Lott, Warren has been granted under SAP Doc. 132877113. The remainder credit of $145,491.49 plus overhead $18,913.89 totaling $164,405.18 have been denied.

1. Flores, Carl; Global Assist and Assure Lead, credit claim of $59,149.69 plus overhead.

According to the 2020 staff listing, personnel including Daphane Maxon, Scott M. Chiasson, Loren V. Stagner, and John Andrew Harrison provided by the non-operator had no direct reports. Therefore, they do not meet the criteria for first-level supervision as claimed by the co-owner. As their actual supervisor, Carl Flores is considered the first-level supervisor, and his time is directly chargeable to the joint account. Accordingly, the credit claim of $59,149.69 plus overhead is denied.

2. Gregersen, Casey; Wells Competitive Intelligence Engineer, credit claim of $21,230.77 plus

overhead.

According to the 2020 staff listing, the position text of Gregersen is Wells Competitive Intelligence Engineer. Assist and assure coach is not an administrative role. The OTL is in well safety deepwater organization and is responsible the activities in project delivery were in compliance with BSEE regulatory safety required by 30 CFR 250.1910 - 1933. Per the February 2019 Letter Agreement, Attachment 1, 3.1, the OTL's cost is chargeable to the Joint Account directly.

3. Guo Wenni, Senior Development Planner, credit claim of $1,323.75 plus overhead.

The OTL supported the project activity of Mars Hazard analysis required by 30 CFR 250.1911. had been granted and posted. Per the February 2019 Letter Agreement, Attachment 1, 3.1, the OTL's cost is chargeable to the Joint Account directly.

4. Hicks, Stacie, Data Reporting Technician, credit claim of $32,605.14 plus overhead.

The OTL supported the projects and activities related to Mars Well/Facility Operation and Olympus Operation and Maintenance. He monitored data from drilling, production, maintained records for environmental monitoring and safety compliance and ensure alignment with BSEE regulations (§ 250.186 - Reporting Information and Forms, § 250.187 - Incident Reporting Requirements, § 250.188 - Specific Incidents to Report, § 250.189 - 190 - Notification and Written Report Requirements). Per the February 2019 Letter Agreement, Attachment 1, 3.1, and 3.3, the OTL's cost is chargeable to the Joint Account directly.

5. Lott, Warren, credit claim of $5,639.95 plus overhead had been granted and posted under SAP document no. 132877113.
6. Maxon, Daphane; Assist and Assure Coach, credit claim of $25,542.19 plus overhead.

Assist and assure coach is not an administrative role. The OTL is in well safety deepwater organization and is responsible the activities in project delivery were in compliance with BSEE regulatory safety required by 30 CFR 250.1910 - 1933. With regards to Mr. Flores: Per the Operator's audit 2024NOV\_E101 exception #59, team leadership is considered non-billable. Therefore the Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account for his time as he was a team leader, to ensure consistent treatment across the companies. Credit remains due: $59,149.69

With regards to Mr. Gregersen, the Operator has stated that the is a "Wells Competitive Intelligence Engineer". This in no way benefits the Joint Account. Competitive Intelligence is a corporate activity that each company does for themselves individually and not the Joint Account. Full credit remains due: $21,230.77

With regards to Mr. Guo: This person is a planner, who is not working on Well Maintenance, Facility Maintenance, nor Turnaround as required by the February 2019 Letter Agreement. Accordingly, their time is not chargeable. Full credit remains due: $1,323.75

With regards to Ms. Hicks: The type of Data Reporting performed by Ms. Hicks is not a CFR requirement, rather it is considered administrative in nature, and also specifically called out as Non-Billable under the "regulatory/permitting" sections of the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement and therefore not chargeable. Full credit remains due $32,605.14

For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include procurement, administration, accounting and auditing, pipeline nominations and scheduling, human resources, management, supervision (excluding first level supervision of operational staff which is billable), legal services, handling taxation matters,permitting/regulatory work, land and division order services. Overhead charges are compensation for all costs and expenses associated with such functions, including the salaries or wages plus applicable payroll burdens, benefits, and personal expenses of personnel performing such functions, as well as their office and other support costs.

With regards to Ms. Maxon: Coaching is administrative in nature. It is not considered technical labor per the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement and therefore is not chargeable to the Joint Account. Full credit remains due: $25,542.19

Total Credit due: $139,851.54 plus 13% overhead for a total credit of $158,032.24.

The Operator charged the Joint Account $169,828.36 for Harvey Gulf International invoice #16672 in the amount of $93,612.61 and invoice #16886 in the amount of $76,215.75 as according to the provided JADE lines. Upon review, the following discrepancies were found:

* Invoice #16672: The vendor transposed the allocation basis resulting in heavier allocations on Olympus vs. Ursa. This was the subject of Information Request #075 which was raised during the fieldwork.
* Invoice #16886: The vendor allocated 100% of the charges to Mars A, but supporting location papers from the invoice reference Ursa only. This was the subject of Information Request #080 which was raised during the fieldwork.

A copy of the invoices, the JADE lines, SAP screenshots and a reconciliation template provided by the Operator for Invoice #16672 is attached.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $163,015.97 (Invoice #16672: credit $93,612.61 to reverse the incorrect allocation; recharge $6,812.39 for the correct allocation; resulting in a net credit of $86,800.22; Invoice #16886: net credit $76,215.75) for the incorrect allocations plus 2.5% overhead for a credit of $167,091.37

The Auditor also could not validate Helicopter allocations from Shell Pipelines per information provided on IR 018 since helicopter activity is also for 2019 and did not have sufficient support.

The Joint Account was charged a total of $2,157,797.62 in Logistics Services-- Marine from WBS O.US.175.MAR.PLF.71300. We were unable to open many of the attached backups to the monthly Journal entries.

For one that we were able to open, we found the following explanation on the attached backup for the monthly Supply Boat charge:

"Each Month on full operations 175K is transferred from Drilling projects to Production for their share of Marine charges. This portion is for Well A-8 Drill\_NW#30282909\_01-01 to 01-31-2020"

There is no further explanation as to the basis of this monthly $175,000 charge to the WBS element.

This is the subject of IR # 82 during fieldwork.

Please credit the Joint Account $1,927,800 (($175,000x12) X 91.8% portion of WBS element allocated to Mars) plus overhead of $250,614 for a total of $2,178,414 for these unexplained allocated costs to the joint account.

replies.text:
Credit denied. The process works that all marine logistics is initially billed to drilling since drilling is absorbing 100% of rig fuel cost incurred supporting the TLP Operations. And then an allocation for an amount of $175K is charged to Production Operations and Projects. The $175K represents legitimate cost for the Production Operation. There is no overcharging the Joint Account for Overhead.

If this billing process is to have the marine logistics initially charged to Production Operation and then make an allocation to drilling projects. Then the overhead over /under charging will not even be raised as an issue. However, due to most of the marine logistics cost is for drilling, it is not a preferred method to bill production operation first.

In conclusion, the $175K represents legitimate cost for production operation. There is no overcharging the Joint Account for Overhead. Additionally, overhead adjustment was not included in the original claim. Credit is denied.

063.short_description: MB-001 Materials Not Ran in Well
063.description:
The Operator charged the joint account $1,916,337.16 for various materials on well MB-001. A review of the schematic report indicates these materials were not ran in the well. This was the subject of Information Request 092. The Operators response indicated that 49XXXXX documents are accrual/ reversal entries that have been offset to "zero". A review of the JADE indicates that 49XXXXXX (WA document type) documents are material transfers, moving the materials from one well and charging it to a different well. 064.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $18,357.93 for salaries, benefits, burden and overhead according to the provided JADE lines. This was the subject of Information Request 128. Upon review, the employees noted on the JADE lines were all charging less than one day per month to a Major Construction project. This is contrary to the Statement of Clarification and Intent, and also the Shell/BP Agreed Ways of working outlined in email from Azza Fawzi at Shell dated 3/26/2021 to Eric Donaldson at BP.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $18,357.93 including Overhead for the labor not chargeable.

The Joint Account was allocated a total of $5,382,966.15 in Contract Services from WBS O.US.175.MAR.PLF.71300. (see attached JADE)

A review of the ledger of WBS O.US.175.MAR.PLF.71300 shows that there is a total charge of $2,060.537.07 for Manpower Svcs.

We examined the following charges to Manpower Svcs in WBS O.US.175.MAR.PLF.71300:

As noted on the table above, a number of line items did not have invoices attached. Instead, only timesheets, which show time worked but not amount charged, were included as backup for the Manpower Svcs charges. Furthermore, upon cross-referencing the timesheets/invoices with the PoB, we noted the following:

- [ ]  Robert LaValley -- not found in PoB

- [ ]  Rickey McCants -- either not found in PoB during time charged or PoB indicates he was at URSA

- [ ]  Peter Lima -- not found in PoB

- [ ]  Nelson Caraballo -- PoB does not indicate he is at Mars during time charged

- [ ]  Michael Nettles -- no timesheet or invoice attached, only email approvals (attached). PoB does not indicate he worked at Mars during 2020.

This exception is the subject of IR #s 94 and 103 during fieldwork.

Since we are unable to ascertain that the above contract labor were performing services for Mars for the time charged, please credit the Joint Account $240,135.03 ($261,585 x 91.8% allocated to Joint acct) plus 13% Overhead for a total of $271,352.58.

066.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $1,039,794.13 for several marine invoices as according to the provided JADE lines. Upon review, the vendor did not reference Mars/Olympus in the working papers yet allocated costs to these properties. This was noted when the auditor reviewed the Voyage Reports and compared them to the vendor invoices, and found discrepancies. In some cases, Mars/Olympus is also not referenced in the allocation provided by the vendor. This was the subject of Information Requests #111 & #115 which was raised during the fieldwork. The Operator did not satisfy the inquiry in the Information Request and only provided that the vendors made mistakes.

A copy of the invoices which include the Voyage Reports, SAP screenshots & the JADE lines have been provided to show that the vendor did not specify the locations of the services rendered in their invoices and supporting work papers.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $1,039,794.13 for the lack of evidence that the services provided by the vendor(s) were for Mars/Olympus, plus 2.5% overhead for a credit of $1,065,788.98.

Credit denied. The charges of supply boat service in questions are from vendors of Otto Candies, Tidewater Maine, Jackson and Harvey Gulf International. In addition to download vendors' invoices from SAP, the auditor has been instructed to download the Marine Voyage Sheets from MyCM for their review of supply boat service charges. The Voyage Record of Marine Voyage Sheet is a real time input by Vessel Master.

Each file of Marine Voyage Sheet for vessel contains seven tabs; Voyage Record (A real time input by vessel master), cost allocation, Star Voyage Log, Star Cost Allocation, Fuel, Charge Code from business, Rig Fuel CC and is generated from GOLS Star Activity Tracker. The GOLS Star Activity Tracker is a real-time activity tracker updated by the vessel master.

With so much information such as invoices, Daily Master Log, Marine voyage Sheet; etc., the auditor has not yet provided any analysis to prove that the Joint Properties have been charged incorrectly. Therefore, no credit is due to the Joint Account.

Therefore, no credit is due to the Joint Account.

068.description:
The Operator moved charges from C.US.MAR.PD.16.002.0942A and C.US.WEB.PD.17.002.0943A to the joint account on WBS C.US.MMD.PD.19.004.0942A. The credit side of entry (from the well) could not be located on the JADE. The JIB indicates three entries for each amount, two debits and one credit, resulting in debit to the joint account. This was the subject of Information Request 079. The Operators response indicated that the WBSs are Long Lead Equipment and has been in Suspense from the year 2016 to till now.

Section II.4 of the Accounting Procedure states "Only such Material shall be purchased for or transferred to the Joint Property as may be required for immediate use and is reasonably practical and consistent with efficient and economical operations. The accumulation of surplus stocks shall be avoided." As these items were in a suspense account (2016-current), please provide support which demonstrates the direct benefit to the joint account or credit the joint account $399,127.17 plus overhead.

075.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $181,950.84 for Houma Distribution Center costs according to the attached JADE lines. These were the subject of Information Request 14 where the Operator explained that these costs were charged in accordance with the Mars UOA Section 7.B. which allows the Operator to charge company owned facilities and equipment at market rate less 20%.

7. Equipment and Facilities Furnished by Operator
- A. Operator shall charge the Joint Account for use of Operator-owned cquipment and facilities, including Shore Base and/ maintenance. repairs, other operating expense, insurance. taxes, depreciation and interest on gross investment less accumulated depreciation nottoexceed\_ eight percent (8 .%) per annum. In addition, for platforms only, the rate may include an element of the estimated cost of platform dismantlement. Such rates shall not exceed average commercial rates currently prevxiling in the immediate area of the Joint Properry.
3. immediate area of the Joint Property less twenty percent (20%). lor automotive equipment. Operator may elect to use rates published by the Perroleum Motor Transport Association.

The Operator did not provide an analysis of the market, nor did it show how the costs had been reduced by 20% from that market analysis. These costs are therefore not chargeable in accordance with Section 7.B. of the Mars UOA and should be credited to the Joint Account.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $181,950.84 for these costs.

Note: This Exception 075 is taken in parallel with Exception 076 which charges for the cost of Ownership and Operation in accordance with 7.A. of the Mars UOA. Either method is acceptable under the UOA, however not both. Therefore exception to both methods is taken until such time as the Operator determines which method they have chosen.

## IV. COSTS INCLUDED IN SHOREBASE OPERATIONS

Direct Operating Costs associated with the provision and operation of the types of facilities and services described in Sections II and III of this document would be included in the Shorebase Facility account. Care should be taken to exclude costs which may occur at a Shorebase Facility location or are allocated to a Shorebase from a higher organizational level, and that do not apply to Shorebase Facility operations (e.g., warehouse space, office space and operating costs for field operating personnel, warehousing personnel and other charges covered by overhead). Billable costs shall be based upon the provisions of the Accounting Procedure in effect covering the operations served.

In addition to the above Operating Costs, the Operator should recover cost of investment through a "rate to recover cost of ownership" charge which may be the same as the "Equipment and Facilities furnished by Operator" provision in the Accounting Procedure. For this purpose, all investments should be taken into account, including land, parking lots, etc. It may include construction overhead and on/off site technical labor according to the provisions of the Accounting Procedures in effect covering the operations served. The "rate to recover cost of ownership" should consist of the following:

Upon review, these costs appear to be the costs of Ownership and Operation which are in accordance with the Mars UOA Section 7.A.

7. Equipment and Facilities Furnished byOperator
- A. Operator shall charge the Joint Account for use of Operator-owned cquipment and facilities, including Shore Base and/ maintenance. repairs, other operating expense, insurance. taxes, depreciation and interest on gross investment less accumulated depreciation not to exceedeight percent( 8 %) per annum. In addition, for exceed average commecial rates currently prevuiling in the inmediate area of the Joint Property.
3. immediate atea of the Joint Property less twenty percent (20%). lor automotive equipment. Operator may elect to use rates published by the Perroleum Motor Transport Associarion.

On the response to Information Request 14, the Operator indicated that it was electing to use the Section 7.B. method (Market Rate less 20%) and therefore the costs of Ownership and Operation are not chargeable.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $461,843.48 plus 2.5% Overhead for costs not chargeable under Section 7.B of the Mars UOA.

Note: This Exception 76 is taken in parallel with Exception 75. According to the Mars UOA, Either the 7.A. or 7.B. method is acceptable, however not both. Exception is taken here until such time as the Operator determines which method they have chosen.

In August 2020, the Operator recognized an error was made converting from Lindros to PowerBI for their offshore billing, and issued a credit of $1,467,000.00 which corrects the billings in error up to December 2019. (see emails in file 129739711 Journal Entry) to Lindsay Adair, Tyler Bond at Shell dated 8/12/2020.

JADE for this specific concern for 2019 and 2020 is attached for the Operator's review.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account for $819,000 plus 13% OH for the IWOCs reel not used on the Joint Account.

37.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account (Mars/Olympus) $122,247.84 for "PSP Award" which appears to be stock or stock options purchased/awarded to certain individuals. This was the subject of Information Request 53.

This Performance Share Plan is considered an Incentive Compensation Plan, and these costs should be covered by overhead rates. These payments do not directly benefit joint property, and there are no predetermined operational metrics to earn these awards. Finally, this Shell share program, as identified in the whitepaper provided with Information Request 53, is not made available to all employees that work on joint property. MFI-19 (1986 Offshore Accounting Procedure - Joint Operations) states, "Costs which are primarily beneficial to the Operator should be excluded from employee benefits and treated as Overhead, for which the Operator is compensated under the provisions of Section III. Such costs to be borne by the Operator would include...safety awards, service awards and other special benefits available only to executives, certain employees or groups on a selective basis."

replies.text:
Credit Denied. The four software applications are required to meet safety reporting and regulatory requirements. These four software applications are not accounting, or administrative software applications as mentioned in COPAS MFI 44. Therefore, no credit is due to the Joint Account. The benefits and function of the four software applications are as follows:

Enablon BBS is an HSSE application (Health, Safety, Security, Environmental) used by all offshore staff and contractors to document Behavior-Based Safety observations. Observation data is used as leading indicators to increase safety and reduce incidents. Results are also used to meet safety reporting and regulatory requirements.

IntelaTrac application include Chemical Analysis, Preventive maintenance, Production monitoring, Production tank levels, Production flow rates.

UTL (Universal Tag Locator) is a production/operations application used by offshore staff (e.g., Deck Operators, Maintenance, Technicians, Operations Supervisors, etc.) to document and share relevant Shift and Situational Awareness information (e.g., production, operations, maintenance, HSSE, alarms, etc.) across the entire facility. Data is integrated from multiple source systems. Results are also used for shift handover, situational awareness, optimized maintenance, increased availability, and reduced deferment.

Connected Field Worker (CFW) is a production/operations set of IT tools used by offshore staff (e.g., Deck Operators, Maintenance, Operations Supervisors, etc.) including On-deck wireless connectivity, Mobile Device Automated Support, MS Productivity Tools (e.g., MS Teams, Sharepoint), and SAP mobile tools (e.g., Work Request, Work Execution). The platform supports Operator Rounds, Virtual Inspections, Over-the-shoulder Coaching, Commissioning & startup activities, etc., resulting in increased situational awareness, optimized maintenance, increased availability, and reduced deferment.

Most items are governed by regulatory sections such as **§250.1915 (Training)**, **§250.1920 (Auditing)**, and **§250.19 (Management of Change)**, or are noted as **directly billable under COPAS Model Form** guidelines.

The Operator's mention of the activities being for "maintenance planning, scheduling activities, or preventative maintenance" follow the February 2019 Letter Agreement, Section 3.3

## 3. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration

OTL is chargeable by the Operator to the joint account for planners, schedulers, and plan execution supporters working on facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities.

The costs in question cannot, however, be classified as OTL as they do not meet the definition of "Technical Employee" as contemplated by the February 2019 Letter Agreement:

## 2. Definition of "Technical Employees"

"Technical Employees" shall mean those employees, having special and specific engineering, geological, geophysical technical or operational skills (including planners, schedulers and execution support for facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities), and whose function in Joint Operations (as defined in the Mars UOA) is providing services for the benefit of the Joint Property (as defined in the Mars UOA).

The Definition does not mention any aspect related to IT skills. Therefore, full credit remains due.

The Operator is mis-reading the 2020 Mars Exception 003 supporting files. The "Exception JADE Lines" tab is the correct tab to use for that exception. Other tabs are included as proof of auditor's analysis and working papers. The total amount claimed in the exception, $514,023.49 is referenced at the bottom of that tab, Snip is below:

The individuals in the "All JADE Lines" tab who were not taken as exception in 2020 were charged to Major Construction projects where engineering, design, and drafting is chargeable under the Statement of Clarification and Intent. Their costs were therefore not questioned as part of that exception.

As the Operator has elected to revise the Overhead rate from Major Construction to Development, the categories of engineering, design, and drafting are no longer blanket chargeable as they now fall under the Mars UOA and the February 2019 Letter Agreement. As this OTL is no longer chargeable under the Statement of Clarification and intent, the Operator is requested to issue credit as requested.

Credit Denied:

Established in 2011, the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) is the lead agency in the United States Department of Interior in charge of improving safety and ensuring environmental protection relating to the offshore energy industry. This was in response to the Minerals

Management Service (MMS) regulatory failure related to the Deepwater Horizon oil spill in 2010. The BSEE established a performance-based approach to integrating and managing offshore operations known as Safety and Environmental Management System (SEMS). Within SEMS there are various Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) that require an Operator to follow and adhere to. Examples of the more common CFR's are as follows:

- CFR 250.1910 - What safety and environmental information is required?
- CFR 250.1913 - What criteria for operating procedures must my SEMS program meet?
- CFR 250.1916 - What criteria for mechanical integrity must my SEMS program meet?

The Operator incurs various costs in order to comply with the aforementioned government mandates as part of the operations of the Joint Venture. Therefore, these costs should be charged to the Joint Account and shared with the Co-Owner(s).

"OTL" shall mean actual costs incurred (including salaries and wages) for Technical Employees (as defined herein) and/or actual costs incurred for professional consultant services and contract services of technical personnel either temporarily or permanently assigned to and working for the principle benefit of the Joint Operations (as defined in the Applicable Operating Agreement) but located 'offsite' or off of the Joint Property (as defined in Applicable Operating Agreement), which are part of approved activities or activities conducted by the Operator which do not require vote or election (as defined in the Applicable Operating Agreement).

Full credit is denied.

To have information of association of personnel name to dollars charged to the Joint Account, how much did the Joint Account pay for X individual, what job were they working on and a dollar cost breakdown per employee are audit tasks or reviews that should have been performed by the auditor during the field audit.

Since auditor did not provide any kind of analysis, as a courtesy, the Operator had provided analysis at Cost center level and employees' name and job title from each cost center in Operator's earlier response. Based on the analysis at the cost center level, it shows the cost centers are all for the operation of the Joint properties and no administrative employees being charged to the Joint Accounts. Therefore, no credit is due to the Joint Accounts.

Credit Denied. The Grand Isle Shipyard (GIS) employees and contractors worked on the rig and platform. Below is a summary detailing the services provided by the GIS personnel and attached files for details.

- 1.Nicholas Hansen is a Technician 4 and works on 14/14 schedule. He worked on the removal of electrical LOTO to PBE-2303.
2. Perry Scioneaux is an electrician and performed inspection of the 3Y Hazloc electrical equipment.
3. The Crane Mechanic and Mars GIS construction crew performed their services on the H&P
- rig. Attached are two examples detailing contractors' name, job title, hours and activities worked.

58.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $169,828.36 for Harvey Gulf International invoice #16672 in the amount of $93,612.61 and invoice #16886 in the amount of $76,215.75 as according to the provided JADE lines. Upon review, the following discrepancies were found:

* Invoice #16672: The vendor transposed the allocation basis resulting in heavier allocations on Olympus vs. Ursa. This was the subject of Information Request #075 which was raised during the fieldwork.
* Invoice #16886: The vendor allocated 100% of the charges to Mars A, but supporting location papers from the invoice reference Ursa only. This was the subject of Information Request #080 which was raised during the fieldwork.

A copy of the invoices, the JADE lines, SAP screenshots and a reconciliation template provided by the Operator for Invoice #16672 is attached.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $163,015.97 (Invoice #16672: credit $93,612.61 to reverse the incorrect allocation; recharge $6,812.39 for the correct allocation; resulting in a net credit of $86,800.22; Invoice #16886: net credit $76,215.75) for the incorrect allocations plus 2.5% overhead for a credit of $167,091.37

The Joint Account was charged a total of $2,157,797.62 in Logistics Services-- Marine from WBS O.US.175.MAR.PLF.71300.

A review of the ledger of WBS O.US.175.MAR.PLF.71300 shows that there is a total charge of $2,149,510.93 for Supply Boats, mostly made up of monthly charges of $175,000. ($175k x 12=$2.1m)

We were unable to open many of the attached backups to the monthly Journal entries.

For one that we were able to open, we found the following explanation on the attached backup for the monthly Supply Boat charge:

"Each Month on full operations 175K is transferred from Drilling projects to Production for their share

of Marine charges. This portion is for Well A-8 Drill\_NW#30282909\_01-01 to 01-31-2020" There is no further explanation as to the basis of this monthly $175,000 charge to the WBS element.

This is the subject of IR # 82 during fieldwork.

Please credit the Joint Account $1,927,800 (($175,000x12) X 91.8% portion of WBS element allocated to Mars) plus overhead of $250,614 for a total of $2,178,414 for these unexplained allocated costs to the joint account.

Upon review of the additional information provided by the Operator, the costs in question are overcharging the Joint Account for Overhead.

During the year, the Operator has transferred approximately $4.1MM USD in cost from Capex to Opex, with a resultant overhead charge of around $441k USD. A supporting file is included with the response to show the Debits booked to the Opex AFEs and credits booked to Capex AFEs.

These transfers are unnecessary because the Operator allocates supply vessel costs directly to Capex or Opex AFEs as determined by the Operator's logistics group and so each respective category is correctly charged.

These transfers are excess overhead recovery and should be credited to the Joint Account. Credit Due $440,768.75 for the

replies.text:
Credit denied. The process works that all marine logistics is initially billed to drilling since drilling is absorbing 100% of rig fuel cost incurred supporting the TLP Operations. And then an allocation for an amount of $175K is charged to Production Operations and Projects. The $175K represents legitimate cost for the Production Operation. There is no overcharging the Joint Account for Overhead.

If this billing process is to have the marine logistics initially charged to Production Operation and then make an allocation to drilling projects. Then the overhead over /under charging will not even be raised as an issue. However, due to most of the marine logistics cost is for drilling, it is not a preferred method to bill production operation first.

In conclusion, the $175K represents legitimate cost for production operation. There is no overcharging the Joint Account for Overhead. Additionally, overhead adjustment was not included in the original claim. Credit is denied.

64.short_description: Major Construction Labor less than 8 Hours
64.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $18,357.93 for salaries, benefits, burden and overhead according to the provided JADE lines. This was the subject of Information Request 128. Upon review, the employees noted on the JADE lines were all charging less than one day per month to a Major Construction project. This is contrary to the Statement of Clarification and Intent, and also the Shell/BP Agreed Ways of working outlined in email from Azza Fawzi at Shell dated 3/26/2021 to Eric Donaldson at BP.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $18,357.93 including Overhead for the labor not chargeable

The Joint Account was allocated a total of $5,382,966.15 in Contract Services from WBS O.US.175.MAR.PLF.71300. (see attached JADE) A review of the ledger of WBS O.US.175.MAR.PLF.71300 shows that there is a total charge of $2,060.537.07 for Manpower Svcs.

We examined the following charges to Manpower Svcs in WBS O.US.175.MAR.PLF.71300:

As noted on the table above, a number of line items did not have invoices attached. Instead, only timesheets, which show time worked but not amount charged, were included as backup for the Manpower Svcs charges. Furthermore, upon cross-referencing the timesheets/invoices with the PoB, we noted the following:

- Robert LaValley -- not found in PoB
- Peter Lima -- not found in PoB
- Rickey McCants -- either not found in PoB during time charged or PoB indicates he was at URSA
- Nelson Caraballo -- PoB does not indicate he is at Mars during time charged
- Michael Nettles -- no timesheet or invoice attached, only email approvals (attached). PoB does not indicate he worked at Mars during 2020.

This exception is the subject of IR #s 94 and 103 during fieldwork.

Since we are unable to ascertain that the above contract labor were performing services for Mars for the time charged, please credit the Joint Account $240,135.03 ($261,585 x 91.8% allocated to Joint acct) plus 13% Overhead for a total of $271,352.58.

66.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $1,039,794.13 for several marine invoices as according to the provided JADE lines. Upon review, the vendor did not reference Mars/Olympus in the working papers yet allocated costs to these properties. This was noted when the auditor reviewed the Voyage Reports and compared them to the vendor invoices, and found discrepancies. In some cases, Mars/Olympus is also not referenced in the allocation provided by the vendor. This was the subject of Information Requests #111 & #115 which was raised during the fieldwork. The Operator did not satisfy the inquiry in the Information Request and only provided that the vendors made mistakes.

A copy of the invoices which include the Voyage Reports, SAP screenshots & the JADE lines have been provided to show that the vendor did not specify the locations of the services rendered in their invoices and supporting work papers.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $1,039,794.13 for the lack of evidence that the services provided by the vendor(s) were for Mars/Olympus, plus 2.5% overhead for a credit of $1,065,788.98

Credit denied. The charges of supply boat service in questions are from vendors of Otto Candies, Tidewater Maine, Jackson and Harvey Gulf International. These vendors except for Jackson have provided the voyage cost allocation sheet, Daily Master Log, Daily Vessel Log or Daily Billing Log and attached them in their billing/invoices. In addition to download vendors' invoices from SAP, the auditor has been instructed to download the Marine Voyage Sheets from MyCM for their review of supply boat service charges. The Voyage Record of Marine Voyage Sheet is a real time input by Vessel Master.

Each file of Marine Voyage Sheet for vessel contains seven tabs; Voyage Record (A real time input by vessel master), cost allocation, Star Voyage Log, Star Cost Allocation, Fuel, Charge Code from business, Rig Fuel CC and is generated from GOLS Star Activity Tracker. 68.short_description: C.US.MAR.PD.16.002.0942A and C.US.WEB.PD.17.002.0943A to Disposal Account
68.description:
The Operator moved charges from C.US.MAR.PD.16.002.0942A and C.US.WEB.PD.17.002.0943A to the joint account on WBS C.US.MMD.PD.19.004.0942A. The credit side of entry (from the well) could not be located on the JADE. The JIB indicates three entries for each amount, two debits and one credit, resulting in debit to the joint account. This was the subject of Information Request 079. The Operators response indicated that the WBSs are Long Lead Equipment and has been in Suspense from the year 2016 to till now.

Section II.4 of the Accounting Procedure states "Only such Material shall be purchased for or transferred to the Joint Property as may be required for immediate use and is reasonably practical and consistent with efficient and economical operations. The accumulation of surplus stocks shall be avoided." As these items were in a suspense account (2016-current), please provide support which demonstrates the direct benefit to the joint account or credit the joint account $399,127.17 plus overhead.

69.short_description: NCS Invoice for Mars/Perdido Charged only to Mars
69.description:
Joint Account was charged $56,000 via SIEP inv no. 6706060465. This is a recharge of NCS Subsea invoice #55. The NCS invoice indicated that this is for Project "815 Shell GoM Mars, Perdido" but the entire amount was charged to Mars. Operator was unable to explain why this charge was not split between Perdido and Mars except to say that per Shell contact, there was "no miscoding".

This was the subject of IR #62 during fieldwork.

Since a portion of NCS invoice noted above is marked as Perdido, please credit the Joint Account $28,000 ($56,000 x1/2) plus 2.5% overhead for a total of $28,700.

replies.text:

The NCS invoice is charged correctly to Mars. As referenced on the invoice, PO 4550182372 Line Item 00010 is related to Mars 4D Pcable processing and Line Item 00020 is related to Mars 3d Pcable processing. There were no charges listed on the invoice related to the Perdido project.

72.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $100,127.06 for RTOC costs according to the attached JADE lines. This was the subject of Information Request 133.

Upon review, the costs were duplicate because they charged the same time period twice.

The following are the duplicate pairs:

129291626 and 129291367 for January 2020 RTOC Staff

129291368 and 129291398 for Feb 1 through Feb 14 Cenergy contractors

129697490 and 129697491 for Jun 6 through Jun 19 Cenergy contractors

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $50,063.53 plus 2.5% overhead for a total credit of $51,315.12.

replies.text:
Credit denied. The claims of duplicate charges by the auditor were incorrect.

- Auditor claimed - 129291626 and 129291367 for January 2020 RTOC Staff - The charges posted under SAP Doc. 129291367 is for January 2020 and SAP Doc. no. 129291626 is for February 2020 business. replies.text:
Credit denied. The amount shown on semi-monthly time sheets provided by the auditor do not match to the charges posted under those SAP documents in question and do not tie to JADE. In other words, those semi-monthly time sheets provided by the auditor were not used as a basis for posting. They are not the supporting documents for the SAP documents.

The team lead of RTOC emailed two or more months of semi-monthly time sheets to JE preparer for the posting of RTOC charges. Instead of recreating supporting documents by splitting semi-monthly time sheets by month, the JE preparer simply attached the email with all the attachments received as the supporting document for the JE of both SAP documents. Therefore, the same semi-monthly time sheets could be appeared in multiple SAP documents. However, it does not mean the charges have been made duplicated or the charges for the same months have been posted twice.

We have traced and reconciled the charges in question from the semi-monthly time sheet to SAP JE posting and JADE lines, we found that the JE preparer had failed to update the description of the JE when he or she did the template upload. It had caused confusion for the auditor but there is no duplication of charges.

The file to show the reconciliation from JE of SAP document to Semi-monthly time sheet and JADE line for SAP document no. 129291626, 129291368, and 129697490 is the attached file for co-owner's review.

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

The Operator's maintains the position no duplication of charges exists. Attached is the analysis previously provided. According to the analysis, the RTOC expenses posted under six SAP documents in question are not duplicates. There is no evidence on the six invoices that time periods were duplicated.

The non-operator claims Document Pair 129291626/129291367 are both for January RTOC Allocations, however, failed to recognize the amount charged and charge code are different in these two documents. Document no. 129291626 is for RTOC expense from February 1st, 2020, to February 15th, 2020, and Document no. 129291367 is for RTOC expense from January 1st, 2020, to January 31st, 2020. Therefore, it is concluded the two documents are not for the same time periods.

The Non-Operator claims Document Pair 129291368/129291398 are both for Cenergy Allocations from February 1 to February 14. However, this claim is incorrect as the two documents are for different time periods. Document no. 129291368 is for RTOC charges of Cenergy contractors for the period from January 18, 2020, to January 31, 2020. Document no. 129291398 is for RTOC charges of Cenergy contractors for the period from February 1, 2020, to February 14, 2020. Therefore, it is concluded the two documents are not for the same time periods.

The Non-Operator claims both documents, 129697490 and 129697491, are for Cenergy Allocations between June 6 and June 19. However, the amount charged, and charge code are different in these two documents. Document no. 129697490 is for RTOC charges for Cenergy contractors for the period from May 23, 2020, to June 5, 2020. Document no. 129697491 is to post RTOC charges for Cenergy contractors for the period from June 6, 2020, to June 19, 2020. Therefore, it is concluded the two documents are for the same time periods.

75.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $181,950.84 for Houma Distribution Center costs according to the attached JADE lines. These were the subject of Information Request 14 where the Operator explained that these costs were charged in accordance with the Mars UOA Section 7.B. which allows the Operator to charge company owned facilities and equipment at market rate less 20%.

7. Equipment and Facilities Furnished by Operator

- A. Operstor shall charge the Joint Account for use of Operator-owned equipment and facilities, including Shore Base and, maintenance. repairs, other operating expense, insurance. taxes, depreciation and interest on gross investment les: accumulated depreciation not to exceed\_eight percent(— 8 %)per annum. In addition, fo exceed average commercial rates currently prevailing in the immediate area of the Joint Property.
2. immediate atea of the Joint Property less twenty percent (20%). lor automotive equipment, Operator may elecr to use rates published by the Perroleum Motor Transport Association.

The Operator did not provide an analysis of the market, nor did it show how the costs had been reduced by 20% from that market analysis. These costs are therefore not chargeable in accordance with Section 7.B. of the Mars UOA and should be credited to the Joint Account.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $181,950.84 for these costs.

Note: This Exception 075 is taken in parallel with Exception 076 which charges for the cost of Ownership and Operation in accordance with 7.A. of the Mars UOA. Either method is acceptable under the UOA, however not both. Therefore, exception to both methods is taken until such time as the Operator determines which method they have chosen.

Credit denied. The JADE lines in question were for allocation of Houma Marine Terminal operating cost (please see JADE file column #AB). The Marine operating terminal costs are allocated monthly to various properties based upon boat usages. It has been incurred regularly since marine terminal in operation and before the establishment of DC.

Houma DC costs are for storage or area cost for items not readily available from suppliers (Long lead time items), items requiring climate controlled environment, critical spares and equipment, and intervention equipment. Houma DC costs were allocated monthly to various properties based upon the square footage used in the location and the market rates less 20% per Section II Direct Charges paragraph 7.B. as addressed under exception no. 75.

Therefore, the allocation costs of storage or area of Houma DC and marine terminal operating costs are two separate allocations that are not duplications of costs. No credit is due to the Joint Account.

029.description:
PHA Fees

Various Invoices

The Operator billed Chevron $12,127,641.80 for Silvertip PHA fees for December 2018 to November 2020 production months. The PHA fees were recalculated by the Auditors taking into consideration several changes as outlined in the Tobago Interconnection Agreement effective August 1, 2019. Included in this agreement were changes to the Monthly Minimum Fee that are applied when the Infrastructure Access Fee (IAF) does not meet this level. These changes are outlined in section 3.5.2, Monthly Minimum Fee Associated with the Perdido Regional Host.

Finally, the Auditors also noted changes to the Firm Capacity Nominations, which are reviewed annually and agreed to by the partners.

Per the review, the changes discussed above were not consistently applied to all production months. A workbook was created and provided to Shell as part of Silvertip information request (IR) 17 to review. This IR remained open at the conclusion of fieldwork. During the review, the Auditor did take exception to a journal entry made in April 2020 to correct October 2018 PHA fees. Per documentation support for the October 2018 entry, all costs were appropriately billed on the initial entry, no adjustment was required.

The Operator is requested to provide additional documentation upon their review of the PHA fee IR or credit the Silvertip Joint Account $295,430.00 + TBD with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

The Joint Account was charged $410,346.72 on project code P.US.SIL.NF.17.011.7240A, 19>2017 RGS C-CIMV Replacement for work that appears to be applicable to Perdido instead of Silvertip. Furthermore, the Operator was unable to provide evidence that an AFE was submitted to Chevron for approval. The Joint Operating Agreement, Section 6.2 states,

'The Operator shall not make any single expenditure or undertake any project or Operation costing $250,000, or more, unless an Authorization for Expenditure (AFE) has either (1) been included in a proposal for an Operation and approved by the Participating Parties through their Election to participate in the Operation, or (2) received the approval of the Parties as a General Matter.'

replies.text:
As per the Systems Engineer, the C-CIMV (Chemical Injection Metering Valve) services the C-Caisson which produces Silvertip wells, therefore it's being charged to the Silvertip Joint Account.

The CIMV used to provide defoamer chemical to C-Caisson failed open making it impossible to adequately control defoamer rate to the caisson. The work covers the cost of the CIMV replacement and the RCFA which will be conducted to understand and mitigate the failure mechanism. The additional cost is to accommodate the install of C-CIMV including installation from a dedicated boat prior to the start-up of SA005 to minimize deferment associated without having defoamer deliverability.

Credit is denied.

replies.text:
As shown on the invoice, these charges are for maintenance of the Yokogawa control system (YCS) which is absolutely critical to be able to operate Perdido and is the entire interface that operations uses to control and maintain the process conditions within the optimal and safe operating ranges. We would not be able operate the YCS without maintaining security patches and upgraded versions through regular maintenance.

As per MFI-44, section II, C - "Software costs include - Support Costs - troubleshooting, upgrading, maintaining, and reconfiguring to accommodate physical changes to the wells and equipment over time." and "Examples of Computer Applications (Table 1)" these charges are direct billable. Credit is denied.

[table 8]

Credit is denied.

Scope of Work on PO

- 1) Technical Telephone Support 24/7/365 - DCS and SIS
- 2) Software Support Releases - Revision Upgrades/Patch Updates for CENTUM, ProSafe-RS, and PRM
- 3) Priority Response
- 4) Customer Information Portal
- 5) Security Information Service 6) GoM Fleet Manager

The Operator cites COPAS MFI 38 in its response. However, this same document states in its introduction (page 3): "The provisions in this MFI do not supersede or override the provisions of any accounting procedure that is part of an existing agreement. The joint operating agreement and accounting procedure for a particular property will always take precedence". Therefore, the Confidential Settlement Agreement between SOI and Chevron supersedes COPAS provisions.

Clause 3.7 of the Settlement Agreement specifically limit third-party storage charges to 6 months and states (emphasis added):

Third Party Storage, Warehouse Facilities - For approved projects, the labor and facilities costs and any consignment fee directly incurred for preservation, maintenance, and storage for jointly owned equipment or materials for Joint Operations may be charged to the Joint Account as a direct charge. The chargeable amounts are limited to periods of six (6) months or less occurring prior to execution of the project or as agreed to by the Parties. This time period is considered temporary staging for a specific project. replies.text:
Scott Armature stored critical equipment for motors in their climate controlled facility, and they are responsible for furnishing the VFD's (Variable Frequency Drivers) and motors when required that enable us to continue operations. They are also responsible for inspecting and maintaining this critical equipment in their facility. They are procuring business critical equipment, and without these services, it would not be possible to carry out safe and reliable operations and production at Perdido would be at risk. The items have very long lead times, typically around 25 weeks.

COPAS MFI 38 Materials Manual page 15 J. Maintenance and Preservation Costs states the following:

Warehouse operation, storage fees and maintenance expenses represent the operator's cost of storing (in a wholly owned warehouse) and handling material 1) may not be readily available in current market conditions for immediate use, 2) is frequently used, or 3) is otherwise held as surplus.

Services provided by 3rd parties for the co-owned material is not intended to be covered by the overhead rate.

Credit is denied.

The Operator cites COPAS MFI 38 in its response. However, this same document states in its introduction (page 3):"The provisions in this MFI do not supersede or override the provisions of any accounting procedure that is part of an existing agreement. The joint operating agreement and accounting procedure for a particular property will always take precedence". Therefore, the Confidential Settlement Agreement between SOI and Chevron supersedes COPAS provisions.

Clause 3.7 of the Settlement Agreement specifically limit third-party storage charges to 6 months and states (emphasis added):

Third Party Storage, Warehouse Facilities - For approved projects, the labor and facilities costs and any consignment fee directly incurred for preservation, maintenance, and storage for jointly owned equipment or materials for Joint Operations may be charged to the Joint Account as a direct charge. The chargeable amounts are limited to periods of six (6) months or less occurring prior to execution of the project or as agreed to by the Parties. This time period is considered temporary staging for a specific project. After use of the material or equipment for the Joint Operation is completed, the equipment or material storage costs will no longer be charged to the Joint Account unless the Parties have agreed in writing that the material or equipment is acritical spare.

Chevron is not disputing the criticality of the services provided. However, the Settlement Agreement requires that charges above six months be agreed in writing by the parties.

The claim is maintained. The Operator is requested to provide supporting documentation that the storage costs are in line with the terms of the agreement or credit the Joint Account $8,672.95 ($7,675.18 plus 13% overhead of $997.77) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

Part 1:

This part of the audit claim pertains to SIEP Time-writing on Electronic Submersible Pump (ESP) replacements based on the two WBS's of P.US.PER.EW.19.012.7240A and P.US.PER.EW.18.014.7240B. As these claims are related to Well Maintenance, they are direct chargeable as per the Billing Standards section 3.C Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration, "OTL is chargeable to the joint account for planners, schedulers, plan execution supporters and others working on drilling, completions, facility maintenance, well maintenance operations and turnaround activities whose function was previously performed offshore/onsite but have been relocated onshore but excluding any non-technical personnel engaged in dedicated administrative support of such activities." of the Settlement Agreement effective January 1, 2019.

Part 2:

This part of the claim is for SIEP Time-writing on 2019 Production Universe Support. As per the Engineer for this WBS of P.US.PER.EW.19.002.7241A, the work pertains to improvements to the production allocation method. This component is used for fulfilling our regulatory and compliance requirements where the data is submitted to BOEM.

Credit is denied.

The Operator cites COPAS MFI 38 in its response. However, this same document states in its introduction (page 3): "The provisions in this MFI do not supersede or override the provisions of any accounting procedure that is part of an existing agreement. The joint operating agreement and accounting procedure for a particular property will always take precedence". Therefore, the Confidential Settlement Agreement between SOI and Chevron supersedes COPAS provisions.

Clause 3.7 of the Settlement Agreement specifically limit third-party storage charges to 6 months and states (emphasis added):

Third Party Storage, Warehouse Facilities - For approved projects, the labor and facilities costs and any consignment fee directly incurred for preservation, maintenance, and storage for jointly owned equipment or materials for Joint Operations may be charged to the Joint Account as a direct charge. The chargeable amounts are limited to periods of six (6) months or less occurring prior to execution of the project or as agreed to by the Parties. This time period is considered temporary staging for a specific project. After use of the material or equipment for the Joint Operation is completed, the equipment or material storage costs will no longer be charged to the Joint Account unless the Parties have agreed in writing that the material or equipment is a critical spare.

The Confidential Agreement requires that charges above six months be agreed in writing by the parties. Therefore, the claim is maintained. The Operator is requested to provide supporting documentation that the storage costs are in line with the terms of the agreement or credit the Joint Account $2,857.99 ($2,529.20 plus 13% overhead of $328.79) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

## Description:

PHA Fees Various Invoices

The Operator billed Chevron $4,062,693.55 for Tobago PHA fees for December 2018 to November 2020 production months. The PHA fees were recalculated by the Auditors taking into consideration several changes as outlined in the Tobago Interconnection Agreement effective August 1, 2019. Included in this agreement were changes to the Monthly Minimum Fee that are applied when the Infrastructure Access Fee (IAF) does not meet this level. These changes are outlined in section 3.5.2, Monthly Minimum Fee Associated with the Perdido Regional Host.

Additionally, working interest was adjusted as both Shell and Chevron are carrying CNOOC's interest for a period of ten years, August 1, 2019 through December 31, 2029 (or the termination of the Interconnection Agreement).

Finally, the Auditors also noted changes to the Firm Capacity Nominations, which are reviewed annually and agreed to by the partners.

Per the review, the changes discussed above were not consistently applied to all production months. A workbook was created and provided to Shell as part of Silvertip information request (IR) 17 to review. This IR remained open at the conclusion of fieldwork. During the review, the Auditor did take exception to a journal entry made in April 2020 to correct October 2018 PHA fees. Per documentation support for the October 2018 entry, all costs were appropriately billed on the initial entry, no adjustment was required.

The Operator is requested to provide additional documentation upon their review of the PHA fee IR or credit the Silvertip Joint Account $199,950.00 + TBD with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.
