026.error_type: 17.4 Miscellaneous / Other Well and Facility Ope-3212773C00
026.description:
Information Request (IR): 135

Workpapers provided to the Operator detail credits to the Joint Account for Infrastructure Access Fees (IAF) in consideration for access to the Ursa TLP and the utilization of the Ursa TLP facilities, deck space, and services provided by the Ursa TLP owners for Kaikias production.

Article 4: Fees and Expenses of the Kaikias Production Handling Agreement states in 4.3.1(e), "Each of the IAF fees in 4.3.1 (a) through (d) shall be adjusted annually by the COPAS Adjustment Factor, with the first adjustment being on April 1, 2018 and on each subsequent April 1st."

The Operator failed to escalate the IAF fees due to the Joint Account for Kaikias production until May 2019 resulting in an under payment of fees to the Joint Account for April 2019. In response to Information Request 135, the Operator replied stating the escalation should be taken on the production month of April 1st not the calendar month. The auditor recognizes the difference in interpretation of Article 4; however, the adjustment should be effective on each April 1st and does not specify production periods. The requested correction is to be made to the Joint Account.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account.

Credit Due Joint Account $ 107,466.71

043.short_description: NGTII Rig Accumulators - Unwind Period and Coding Error
043.description:
Workpapers provided to the Operator detail charges for the Noble Globetrotter 2 (NG2) Unwind.

$6M was allocated to various AFEs from October 4, 2020 to December 31, 2020. These unwind charges were based on estimated charges of $21.3M for Mobilization and $11.1M for Upgrades and amortized based on a contract term of 18 months. During the audit, the Operator provided detail for actual charges of $21.5M for Mobilization and $12.2M for Upgrades. A review of these expenditures indicated the Mobilization pool should be reduced by $125k due to an overcharge of a Shell Trinidad and Tobago invoice, as shown on Information Request (IR) 140. Therefore, the Mobilization and Upgrade pool should be adjusted to the actual charges of $21.4M and $12.2M, respectively.

Additionally, the unwind charges were amortized based on a contract term of 18 months which ended January 29, 2021. However, the assignment of the NG2 rig from Shell EP Wells Equipment Services and Shell Offshore included two one year extensions, which would extend this contract to around the end of the original 10 year term with Noble Drilling. Since the mobilization to the Gulf of Mexico and the upgrades to the NG2 rig for the Gulf of Mexico are significant expenditures occurring at the end of the contract term, it would be reasonable to amortize these expenditures over the total term of the assignment, including the two one year extensions. Also the fact that the NG2 continued to drill wells for Shell Offshore in the Gulf of Mexico after the initial 18 month term ended on January 29, 2021 provides additional justification for amortizing the unwind expenditures over the total term of the contract.

Based on our calculations, increasing the Mobilization and Upgrade expenditures to actual expenses and increasing the amortization period by the two one year extension periods, results in adjusted unwind charges of $2.5M for the time the NG2 rig was on URSA properties from October 4, 2020 to December 31, 2020.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account.

Credit Due $ 3,560,826.30 + 2.5% Overhead $ 89,020.66

Credit Due Joint Account $ 3,649,846.96

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

The Mobilization pool was not overcharged $125K by a Shell Trinidad and Tobago invoice as referenced by the auditor. During the audit field work, in response to IR-140, it was explained that the charges were related to Drilling Supervisor Donald Clair. Mr. C lair's time from July 2019 to early October 2019 spent during the mobilization of the rig from the Black Seat to Brownsville, TX and at the shipyard preparing the rig for work readiness.

The mobilization and upgrade accumulators are amortized based on the 18 months contract term that ended on January 29,2021. This amortization period is reflective of the Operator's intent to contract the rig for 18 months. The contract terminated on January 29th, 2021, in accordance with the 18 months term.

052.description: Workpapers provided to the Operator detail 13% operating overhead charged to AFE P.US.URS.WN.19.002.7241, P9O2 Scale Squeeze. According to the Accounting Procedure attached to the Joint Interest Operating agreement, the overhead rate should have been billed at the development rate of 2.5%.

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

The Operator refers to the Daily Operation Reports (DOR) dated 9/25/2019 to 10/3/2019 furnished during the audit field work. The work for the Bullhead Scale Squeeze at the well began on 10/1/2019 and was completed on 10/3/2019. The work was performed and completed in less than 5 consecutive workdays. The other days were for transit, staging and preparation time.

The Section III, Paragraph 1 - Overhead, B.2 mentioned by the auditor does not provide further guidelines about the start date and the end date for this five (5) consecutive workdays or more rule. A good reference about this rule could

业

be found in the paragraph of Exhibit C, III Overhead, 1. Overhead - Drilling and Producing Operations, Paragraph A. Overhead - Fixed Rate Basis, (2) Application of Overhead - Fixed Rate Basis, (b) Charges for wells undergoing any type of workover or recompletion for a period of five (5) consecutive workdays or more shall be made at the drilling well rate. Such charges shall be applied for the period from date workover operations, with rig or other units used in workover, commence through date of rig or other unit release.

The Operator's practice of 5 consecutive workdays starts when the activity begins in the wellbore, 'on the well'. Prepping activity, transit and stand by time are excluded from the 5 consecutive 'on the well' workdays rule. This is the same response to the URSA Audit 2020SOV\_E111 Exception No. 2.

054.description:
Workpapers provided to the Operator detail charges for Harvey America voyage 20201642. The vessel Master's log indicates the majority of the voyage was spent at Mars (MC-807) with a brief trip to Ursa (12/6/2020 from 12:38 to 18:58). The STAR log indicates that 100% of the cost was charged to the Noble Globetrotter II (NGT2). Per the rig schedule, the NGT2 was located at Princess P011 at the time of this voyage.

Information Request (IR) 15 requested an explanation as to why Ursa was being charged when the majority of time was spent at MC-807. In response to IR15, the Operator stated that the voyage was charged 100% to the NGT2 (drilling at Princess P011) and that the vessel made a run to Ursa to load mud for the Noble Globetrotter II; however, the Operator did not explain why the vessel was charged 100% to the NGT2 when the majority of the time was spent at MC-807. The Operator is requested to provide additional information to support the charges. Pending receipt of additional support from the Operator and the opportunity to validate the support, Audit takes exception to the charge.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account.

Credit Due $ 223,479.17 + 2.5% Overhead $ 5,586.98 Credit Due Joint Account $ 229,066.15

replies.text:
Credit denied. The charges for Harvey America are 100% for Globetrotter 2 which was at Ursa/Princess P11 well. The Star Voyage Logs shows the vessel at Globetrotter 2. The vessel did make a short trip to the URSA TLP. and those charges were recorded to Globetrotter 2 as it was at their request for the trip.

The well location on the sea floor doesn't always match the surface location of the asset,. This could be the reason for the vessel Master's log showing the location as MC807. The boat's GPS location may have been in the Mars block, but the vessel was used to support the Globetrotter 2 rig which was at URSA/Princess P11.

055.description:
Workpapers provided to the Operator detail charges allocated for the Houma Distribution Center. Information Request (IR) 59 requested the Operator describe the nature of these costs. The Operator did not respond to IR59 prior to the end of field work. The costs being allocated from the Houma DC cost center (291080) are the costs Commensurate with Ownership and Operation (i.e. natural gas service at the building, catering costs, Wi-Fi hotspot charges, inventory tracking devices, etc.)

In response to Information Request (IR) 34, the Operator stated that the charges for depreciation in question were not for depreciation, but were for the Shell Gulf of Mexico Distribution Center (DC) located near Houma and that these charges were applied based on the average prevailing market rate in the area, minus 20% according to Section II.7.(b) of the Unit Operating Agreement.

According to the Ursa Unit Operating Agreement, Accounting Procedure Section II.7.(a) or (b), the Operator is permitted to charge either the costs of ownership and operation less depreciation, OR average prevailing commercial rate less 20%.

As the Operator has chosen to charge Market Rate less 20%, as documented in IR34, the charges allocated from the Houma DC cost center (charges subject of IR59) are not correct and should be credited to the Joint Account.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account.

Credit Due $ 121,484.16 + 2.5% Overhead $ 3,037.10

Credit Due Joint Account $ 124,521.26

replies.text:
Credit denied. The JADE lines in question were for allocation of Houma Marine Terminal operating cost. The Marine operating terminal costs are allocated monthly to various properties based upon boat usages. It has been incurred regularly since marine terminal in operation and before the establishment of Houma DC.

Houma DC costs are for storage or area cost for items not readily available from suppliers (Long lead time items), items requiring climate controlled environment, critical spares and equipment, and intervention equipment. Houma

业

DC costs were allocated monthly to various properties based upon the square footage used in the location and the market rates less 20% per Section II Direct Charges paragraph 7.B. as addressed under exception no. 6.

The Houma DC facility in question is a Shorebase Facility. MFI-19 defines " Shore Base Facilities shall mean onshore support facilities that during Joint Operations provide such services to the Joint Property as a receiving and transshipment point for Materials; debarkation point for drilling and production personnel and services; communication, scheduling and dispatching center; and other asso ciated functions benefiting the Joint Property.'

Therefore, the allocation costs of storage or area of Houma DC and marine terminal operating costs are two separate allocations that are not duplications of costs. No credit is due to the Joint Account.

02.description: The drilling and completion Cost Objects for Appomattox well AW006 were charged a daily rental rate for the Operator-owned capping stack. The total BEAT amount was allocated to the six Appomattox WBS based on the number of Proteus activity days during the first calendar quarter of 2019. The Operator's response to Information Request 45 indicated that the BEAT was based annual activity. During 2019, the Proteus also served locations other than Appomattox locations. In the auditor's opinion, since the BEAT is based on annual activity, the 2019 BEAT should have been allocated to all locations served by the Proteus during 2019. replies.text: Credit denied. BEAT tax is applicable for the time period from January 1 st , 2018, until April 15 th , 2019. As noted in screen shot below from ‘Contract Variation 3508-CVO-0063-00’ from the attached Transocean invoice, the charges are for BEAT incurred from January 1st, 2019, until April 15th, 2019 The BEAT incurred and charged to Appomattox is in the noted time frame that the Proteus rig was at Appomattox, as shown in screen shot below from attached Transocean invoice.

Credit denied. BEAT tax is applicable for the time period from January 1 st , 2018, until April 15 th , 2019. As noted in screen shot below from ‘Contract Variation 3508-CVO-0063-00’ from the attached Transocean invoice, the charges are for BEAT incurred from January 1st, 2019, until April 15th, 2019 The BEAT incurred and charged to Appomattox is in the noted time frame that the Proteus rig was at Appomattox, as shown in screen shot below from attached Transocean invoice.

CNOOC maintains the position that the Base Erosion Anti-Abuse Tax (BEAT) estimated by Transocean should not be charged to the Joint Account. BEAT is calculated at a federal tax level for all US business and does not directly increase the cost of performing drilling services. If BEAT is interpreted as a “Change in Tax Law” applicable to the contract provision (see contract excerpt below), the decrease in tax costs resulting from greatly reduced income tax rates would also be applicable. The allocation of BEAT only considers the increased cost of a change in tax law and ignores a significant reduction to costs from lower corporate income tax rates. The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 not only created the BEAT tax, but also decreased the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21%, among other changes. If corporate level taxes are deemed applicable, it is inconsistent to recover tax costs associated with BEAT, but not also adjust for other tax law changes that reduce costs for the contractor, Transocean. For example, the income tax rate decreases from 35% to 21% was not adjusted in favor of Shell (i.e., reduced day rate). Further analysis indicates the Proteus’ daily operating rate was not adjusted after the contract variation billing related to early 2019 operations. The effective operating day rate was maintained at $474,166 from May 2019 to May 2021. The contract provision (excerpt below) does not appear to be consistently applied over time. The calculation of BEAT tax Transocean provided only references Proteus and therefore, appears incomplete. Not only was the BEAT tax calculation based on a mid-year estimate, but the allocation to Proteus appears disproportionate based on Transocean’s fleet of drill ships. 1. Many tax assumptions and variables are examined to arrive at taxable income (the starting point of the BEAT calculation) and relying on an estimate at mid-year is not accurate. At a minimum, a true-up from the estimate to the actual BEAT incurred related to Proteus in 2019 is required. 2. Since BEAT is calculated at a federal level, additional support is needed to evaluate the reasonableness of the allocation of the tax. Per the 2019 Annual Report (Form 10k) filed by Transocean Ltd and Subsidiaries, no less than eight ultra-deepwater drill ships operated in the US Gulf of Mexico in 2019. Total tax paid related to BEAT was $21M. The estimated charge of $3.5M is higher than one would anticipate for 104 days of service for one drillship compared to the eight operating 365 days per year. Provided by Shell in response to Exception No 43:

As a follow up to Shell's previous responses, and to correct CNOOC's inaccurate understanding of the application of the change in tax law with respect to the rig contracts, Shell is not paying additional Transocean taxes. Instead, these additional charges are associated with an increase in cost relating to rig services as a result of the change in law (The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017). In addition, it should also be noted that a reduction in corporate income tax was also taken into account in determining what an appropriate change in cost should be based on the change in law. Separately, Shell, as a prudent operator, took action with the rig owner to mitigate the cost increase related to the change in law (entered in 1H 2019). Therefore, as the Operator, Shell charged the projects based on where the cost was incurred (at the activity/well level), in-line with the relevant Agreements.

This exception remains open. The Operator presents several reasons for denying this claim. First, the Operator’s assertion that MFI-19, Section II.2.C (Direct Charges - Labor) is a reason for denying this exception is incorrect. The Interpretative Section of MFI-19, Section II.2.C states “Since these costs are limited, being based upon a maximum amount earned by each employee and the maximum earnings may be different for each category of charge, the cost terminates at various times during the year for individual employees.” This item addresses those labor costs based upon the maximum amount earned by each employee, such as FICA and unemployment taxes, the cost incurred usually terminates at various times during the year for individual employees. This citation is not applicable to the audit exception. Secondly, the Operator’s states MFI-19 II.15 (Other Expenditures) applies since the costs are an expenditure “not covered or dealt with in the foregoing provisions of this Section II, or in Section III and which is of direct benefit to the Joint Property and is incurred by the Operator in the necessary and proper conduct of the Joint Operations.” The chargeability of Labor is addressed in Section II.2.A and offsite technical labor is specifically addressed in Section II.2.A(5). Therefore, Section II.15 does not apply since the Labor expenditure is already addressed in the Accounting Procedure. Thirdly, the Operator suggests those individuals supporting SEMS-related activities are directly billable to the joint account since they are directly employed in the operation of the joint property and fall under Section II - Direct Labor, of the Accounting Procedure. As shown below from Section II.B.2, Technical Labor, of *MFI – 21, Overhead Principles* , “in the operation of” means “offsite.” Technical Labor costs are classified as either "on-site" or "off-site." Either one or both may qualify as a Direct Charge or as Overhead depending upon the terms of the agreement. On-site Technical Labor includes Technical Personnel directly employed on the Joint Property, while off-site includes those not working on the Joint Property but directly employed in the operation of the Joint Property. Finally, we agree 2020 was an exceptional year because of COVID, with offshore operators experiencing many logistical challenges. As such, we understand the need to move many Appomattox personnel onshore to perform their operational or drilling related job functions. These previously onsite billable charges (i.e., directly employed on the Joint Property) would now be considered costs covered by overhead per the governing Accounting Procedure. Since the Operator intended to deviate from the terms of the Accounting Procedure, they should have secured approval from the non-Operator to directly charge the Joint Account for such costs. To the best of our knowledge, the Operator did not seek that approval.
Claim is pending discussions between the Shell and CNOOC commercial teams

This exception remains open as initially presented to the Operator. As Shell properly recognizes, the definition of "Employees" contained in Exhibit G of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement (Integrated Project Team and Technology Sharing) expressly defines "Employees" to include any individual under the employment of any Affiliate of any Party to the Operating Agreement. Therefore, any Employee of a Shell Affiliate that is a member of the Integrated Project Team, is considered an Employee of Shell. The Addendum to Exhibit C of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement expressly incorporates by reference the terms and conditions of Exhibit G (See Addendum to Exhibit C, p.1). Consequently, all wages paid to Shell Affiliates are chargeable in accordance with Section III, Paragraph 2.B. Moreover, there is a prior course of dealing between CNOOC and Shell regarding audit exceptions for employee charges of less than one day per month, which further supports CNOOC's position. As Shell is aware, a prior course of dealing is "a sequence of previous conduct between the parties to the agreement," which can provide "a common basis of understanding for interpreting their expressions and other conduct" (RESTATEMENT (SECOND) OF CONTRACTS § 223, 1981). Given Shell's longstanding approval of CNOOC's interpretation requiring salaries of Shell's Affiliates to be subject to the time requirement of Section III, Paragraph 2.B(a), the parties have established a course of dealing regarding the interpretation of the Joint Operating Agreement concerning the subject audit exception.

Credit denied. There is no change in the Operator’s stance regarding the JOA interpretation pertaining to IPT. 46.description: The Operator charged various Appomattox drilling and completion AFE's a total of $5,022,341.24 for rental of an Operator-owned capping stack as shown on the attached JADE Detail. The auditor's review of those charges showed the Appomattox wells were billed $25,624.19 per day for the rental of the capping stack, the same daily rate charged in the 2020 audit (Shell Audit No. 2020SOV_E112 - Exception No. 27). Information Request (IR) No. 22 from the 2020 Appomattox audit asked the Operator to explain and provide support for the calculation of the daily rate and to explain how the Operator determines which well to charge. The IR No. 22 response provided the requested rate calculation documentation, which showed the rate calculation included a 1.5% Louisiana property tax component, but it didn't address the well charge determination criteria. In the auditor's opinion, the inclusion of a Louisiana property tax component in the Capping Stack rental calculation is not correct since the capping stack is stored and maintained in Aberdeen Scotland as stated in the previous response to IR No. 22. The Operator is requested to correct the rental rate calculation, to make appropriate adjustments and to respond to the question about how the determination is made concerning which well(s) should be charged for the rental. Credit of $227,725.20 is requested for the incorrect equipment rental rate plus 2.5% Development Overhead.

replies.text: Credit denied. The Capping Stack is considered as major equipment. A market rate analysis was conducted by the business in 2018 to determine the day rates and interest rates . Since there has not been any new general assumptions since, the day rates and interest rates have stayed static. As noted in the 2022 audit, Information Request #38… The ownership of the Capping Stack has been transferred to Marine Well Containment Company (MWCC) in 2021. Prior to 2021, It was stored in the MWCC facility in Ingleside, Texas. MWCC also oversees the quarterly function testing for Shell. The Capping Stack is considered as major equipment; hence market factors have been considered in arriving at the day rate. The daily rate for the Capping Stack is $25,624 per day and there have been no rate adjustments since 2019. The rate is calculated based on the below. The is $25,624 /day charge is compared to the internal market analysis done by the business. The daily rental rate of $25,624.19 (which was the day rate in 2019) was applied since it is lower than the Shell Suggested Rate of $30,378.08 (see screen shot of table below). The property tax rate of 1.5% is indeed correct for the Louisiana property tax; however, the Texas property rate is 2.5% and this rate should have been applied instead. For this claim, the Operator has decided not to do a retroactive adjustment for the difference in the property tax rates.

47.description: The Operator charged WBS C.US.APT.PD.17.006.0943C $3,300,000.00 for rental of an Operator owned Open Water Intervention Riser System (OWIRS) as shown on the attached JADE Detail. The auditor's review of those charges showed that Appomattox was billed for rental of the OWIRS at a rate of $90,000.00 per day, the same daily rate charged in the 2020 audit (Shell Audit No. 2020SOV_E112 - Exception No. 26). Information Request (IR) No. 19 from the 2020 Appomattox audit asked the Operator to explain and provide support for the calculation of the Operator-owned OWIRS daily rental rate. The Operator's response stated the rental rate was "based on market cost." In a follow-up response to IR No. 19, the Operator described "market cost" as "The rate is comparable to other commercially available systems with similar capabilities and pressure ratings." The use of "market cost" as the basis for the OWIRS rental rate is not in accordance with the Accounting Procedure attached as Exhibit C to the Greater Appomattox Area Unit Operating Agreement of July 1, 2015, and it overstates the rental rate. The Accounting Procedure provides in Section II, Paragraph 7, Equipment and Facilities Furnished by the Operator, two options for the Operator to use to calculate a rate to charge the Joint Account for use of Operator owned equipment: (1) a rate based on the actual costs of ownership and operation not to exceed average commercial rates or (2) a rate based on average commercial rates less 20%. The rate charged by the Operator doesn't meet either of those criteria. IR No. 19 requested the Operator to provide documentation supporting the acquisition cost of the OWIRS so that a rental rate based on the costs of ownership and operation could be calculated. The documentation has not yet been provided. Pending an acceptable explanation of how the rental rate used to charge the Appomattox Joint Account is in accordance with provisions of the Accounting Procedure, credit for the overstated rental rate is requested based on the "market cost" rate used by the Operator less 20% ($90,000 X 80% = $72,000.00). Therefore, credit of $666,000.00 is requested for the incorrect equipment rental rate charges plus 2.5% Development Overhead.

replies.text: Credit Denied. OWIRS is considered as major equipment. A market rate analysis was conducted by the business in 2018 to determine the day rates and interest rates . Since there has not been any new general assumptions since, the day rates and interest rates have stayed static. The day rate calculation came out to $191,205.54, but since the Operator concludes that we will not be able to recover the full cost for the year, a fixed daily rental rate of $90,000 (with an assumption of 40% for storage, maintenance, taxes & insurance) was applied instead since it is lower than the Shell Suggested Rate of $100,000 (see screen shot of table below) and day rate of $191,205.54. The property tax rate of 1.5% is indeed correct for the Louisiana property tax; however, the Texas property rate is 2.5% and this rate should have been applied instead. For this claim, the Operator has decided not to do a retroactive adjustment for the difference in the property tax rates since the day rate of $191,205.54 wasn’t used.

009.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged $5,434,294.45 for P&T Non-Labor charges from Shell Eastern Petroleum Ltd (SEPL) for the period of July 2020 to December 2020. IR11 and IR23 were submitted to the Operator requesting additional details to support these charges. In response to auditor's IR11 and IR23 on charges from SEPL, the operator stated that the both the Whale and Vito topsides construction costs were originally recorded to the Vito AFE. Reclass entries were made to move the Whale costs from Vito to the Whale project for a total credit of $6,074,190.60 posted in 2020. The auditor tried to reconcile the reclass entries with the SEPL charges posted in 2019 and 2020 but was not able to do so due to lack of supporting documents. The Vito Joint Account was charged a total of $18,070,860.35 from SEPL in 2019 and 2020 as displayed in the Jade lines. The Operator is requested to provide the following additional information to support the SEPL charges: 1. Please provide the detail support of the SEPL costs in the amount of $5,434,294.45 per the IR11 and IR23 request including contractor names, hours worked, service dates, positions, project, and service performed. 2. Please provide details support of the reclass SG facilities costs of -$6,074,190.60 including personnel names, hours worked, service date and projects. 3. Please provide a list of employees who worked for the Whale and Vito projects with start and end dates. The Operator is requested to provide the requested support or credit the Joint Account $5,570,151.81 ($5,434,294.45 plus 2.5% developmental overhead) for these unsupported labor charges. replies.text: Credit Denied This exception is composed of two separate issues. Item #1 pertaining to “the detail support of the SEPL costs in the amount of $5,434,294.45”: This is a Major Construction project for the fabrication team on site in Singapore for the Topside construction of Operator's Vito and Whale platforms in 2020. All costs were originally posted to the Vito WBS, and were later allocated between Vito and Whale for the percentage of time the crews worked on each project. The crews worked seven days a week, with extended hours routinely required for RFI (request for inspection) attendance. Additionally, the team is working in Singapore with a Houston based engineering team, which results in late evenings for interface telecoms. To reduce costs for each project, Vito and Whale shared resources in Singapore. A high level review was performed on a monthly basis to determine an equitable split of the resource cost between Vito and Whale based on the time spent on each project. Without this resource sharing mechanism, the overall cost to Vito would have been higher. The "Resource" file is attached for the employees on the projects. The payroll charges for the employees are from their Shell Eastern Petroleum (SEPL) home cost center and those high level costs are provided in attached file entitled " Ex #9 \_SG01201093 Vito Whale 2020 Cost Details ". The employees are listed in the file and are shown in the screen shot below with job positions. The quarterly IT Recoveries postings pertain to ‘ITSO recoveries for the Singapore Yard’ Please also note that in reviewing each of the 2020 invoices, the Operator discovered the Jan, Feb, and Mar 2020 invoices totaling $2,380,376.94 were incorrectly coded to a non-billable GL account. These transactions were reclassed to a billable GL Account in June 2022 business via SAP Document #131027071 (see screen shot below) and will be reflected in the June 2022 JIB. The November and December 2020 invoices processed in January 2021 business. Thus, the total SEPL charges for Vito in 2020 is $9,264,018. The Jan, Feb, and March invoices are attached. Item #2 pertaining to “support details of the reclass SG facilities costs of -$6,074,190.60 including personnel names, hours worked, service date and projects”: See paragraph above regarding shared costs between VITO and Whale in 2020. The IQN contractor costs were recorded as “P&T Non-Labor” via SIEP on the Affiliate invoices (and have been reviewed by Equinor during hosting and also part of Ex #11) and are reflected on the JADE as “Topsides Manpower”. The JADE lines totaling $18,866,186.89 are attached in the exception response. $6,074,190.60 was transferred from Vito to Whale for the share of time the IQN personnel worked on Whale…leaving a net to Vito of $12,792,006.29.

020.short_description: Contractor Overcharge - Jacobs Engineering Office Space Rental
020.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged $1,522,421.52 from various Jacobs Engineering* invoices for a full-time engineering staff contracted for construction and design efforts of Vito's Floating Production Unit. A review of the invoices revealed a $10K monthly charge for office space usage to accommodate Shell P&T personnel assigned to the Vito construction project as illustrated and detailed on the attached floor plan. On March 13, 2020 the president of the United States declared a nationwide state of emergency in response to the increased health and safety concern of the COVID-19 virus. As a result, many office-based personnel (mainly in the Energy Sector) were required to work from home to further reduce and mitigate the spread of the virus. Based on a "Business Update" published on Worley's website, all office-based personnel were required to work from home while field-based personnel remained on site. Consequently, any charges for office space rentals from March 13, 2020 going forward should be refunded by the vendor. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $44,685.71 ($43,809.52 plus 2% major construction overhead) as detailed on the attached schedule plus any additional office space rentals billed into the following audit period and/or provide a substantiative explanation as to why Worley should charge office space amid a nationwide pandemic. * Jacobs Engineering was acquired by Worley Parsons on October 22, 2018 Amount Claimed: $44,685.71 + T.B.D. (To Be Determined)

replies.text: Credit denied Although the Covid 19 spread started in March 2020, it took a while for everyone to get to the point where it was clear that personnel wouldn't be returning to work anytime soon. The Initial view was this was temporary and the team wanted to hold the space at Worley vs releasing it. When it became clear that no one is going back to the office any time soon the decision was made to work with Worley on a long - term suspension agreement. Credit for March - June 2020 is denied as the team made decision during that period to continue to pay to hold the space as things matured. 022.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged $6.7MM via two material transfers for 2 of 3 TFMC Enhance Vertical Deepwater Trees (EVDT's) to be installed on future Vito waterflood wells. The cost line items for each EVDT includes an SS Choke, materials, TFMC shop labor, and TFMC PMPE. 023.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged $26MM for various overhead rates applied across various AFE's during the period of January 2014 through December 2020. Due to numerous overhead adjustments made in the 2020 audit period, a proper overhead reconciliation could not be presented. As a result, an overall overhead reconciliation was performed on a total of 88 AFE's which includes costs for some projects going as far back as 2014. The 88 AFE's identified on the reconciliation were identified as a result of (a) previous/ongoing overhead claims, and/or (b) SIEP affiliate cost was included in the AFE. The auditors were unable to determine or back into the Operators calculations for overhead adjustments made to these AFE's. The auditors believe an overhead imbalance may be caused by SIEP affiliate cost. Since overhead elements are included in affiliate rates, overhead should not be applied to SIEP cost. Additionally, Section III d.(ii) (Addendum to Exhibit "C") of the Unit Operating Agreement states "Such rate shall be applied to the total cost (gross) incurred by the Joint Account excluding Affiliate charges." The Operator is requested to credit the Vito Joint Account a total of $2,438,610.14 for overhead charged in error or provide a comprehensive reconciliation for the attached AFE's in question. Amount Claimed: $2,438,610.14

replies.text: Partial credit granted. Although the auditor has made a claim from inception through December 2020 vs. rather than adhering to the JOA terms of 24 months prior + current year, the Operator has accepted the audit claim to resolve all OH related claims. Operator has performed the review from WBS inception through December 2022. Refer to the attached spreadsheet titled Ex 23 Operator working - Final V3 for Operator's calculation. The Operator has provided the working for all 88 WBSs from the Inception to December 2022. OH type for all WBSs are identified in "OH check" tab. Since the OH calculation is different for each OH type, we have created separate tab for IPT, Major construction (MC) and Development OH (Dev OH). IPT Tab: OH calculated excluding Affiliate Charges as per the JOA terms (refer Snapshot below) and compared with actual OH charged in JADE. This results in overcharge in the amount of $1,420,867.08 to the Joint Account MC Tab: OH calculated including Affiliate Charges as per the JOA terms (refer Snapshot below) and compared with actual OH charged in JADE. This results in undercharge in the amount of $1,331,527.17 to the Joint Account. Dev OH: OH calculated including Affiliate Charges at 2.5% and compared with actual OH charged in JADE. This results in undercharge in the amount of $35,864.18 to the Joint Account. Summary Tab: Consolidates the calculations from all three tabs and provides a summary view. Based on the calculations, an overall credit is due in the amount of $53,475.73. Entries will be processed in March 2023 Accounting. Note: As per the JOA - While calculating the Overhead amount, the Affiliate charges should be excluded only for IPT WBS. However, the auditor has excluded Affiliates Charges for all the WBS including Major Construction and development Over head in the working file submitted along with the claim.

025.short_description: Equipment Furnished by Operator - M&T Rentals - THRA
025.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged a total of $3.8MM in 2020 for the rental of several Tubing Hanger Running Assemblies (THRA) at $9,900/day as part of the Operator's Machine & Tool package during the period of December 2019 through March 2020. In previous audit correspondence, the Operator provided an explanation stating the rentals are based on a flat market rate and included a supporting "Market Costs" spreadsheet detailing the specifics of these costs. A review of the "Market Costs" spreadsheet revealed the Operator added several other ancillary costs to the THRA’s daily rate which include; test fixtures, accessories, personnel, storage, maintenance, taxes, and insurance. The percentage-based calculation appears to be more of an estimate. Since the Operator is billing out this rental equipment based on the market rates, Section II 7. B. (Equipment and Facilities Furnished by Operator) of Exhibit "C" states: "ln lieu of charges in Paragraph 7 A...Operator may elect to use average commercial rates prevailing in the immediate area of the Joint Property less twenty percent (20%)..." The auditor believes the 80% markup from the vendor's base price for the M&T rental package is excessive. It is also unclear as to why storage and maintenance cost is built into the calculation considering the equipment is being used offshore, on the rig. Since the Operators calculation is more of an estimate, the auditors cannot determine if the rental cost is in line with commercial rates. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account a total of $785,416.50 ($766,260.00 plus 2.5% development overhead) for equipment rental that exceeds the commercial rates. Note: It has been identified by the auditors that a correcting entry was made in the amount of $4.2MM relating to the M&T package for excessive equipment quantities charged and rental days billed to Vito covering the rental period of September 2019 through March 2020. However, based on the auditor’s analysis it appears an additional credit for these rentals that exceed commercial rates remain due at this time. * This exception is a continuation of last year's audit. To date, Equinor has not received a response to Shell audit no. 2020SOV_E113 (AE21). 20% of total rental charge Amount Claimed: $785,416.50

replies.text: Credit denied. - The additional fixtures and accessories are all things that TFMC would bill as separate line items but for ease, they were all lumped into one line item. - It is one Shell employee’s full time job to ensure these THRAs are ready for offshore. TFMC would bill that separately as PMPE, so it would not be included in the material line item but would be an overall cost of use. - Storage, Maintenance, Taxes and Insurance are billed as one line item. Taxes and Insurance are required to go offshore. Storage and maintenance are included because they cost monies but allow rigs flexibility. Correct, where TFMC will not charge storage, they also will not guarantee a rental when called out. Therefore, the options are to add storage costs to the tooling rate or risk rig delay. In summary, it is overall cheaper for Vito to use a THRA from the tool pool vs renting from TFMC (where availability is not guaranteed) or buying and maintain their own project THRA for ($3+ MM)

The EA-8 well was initially included in a campaign and C-Innovation was contracted to perform the job using the IslandIntervention vessel in July 2021. However, due to high currents in the field, the pumping of the asphaltene super solvent forEA8 was not possible.

As a result, the asphaltene super solvent was transferred to MPT tanks and stored at C-port until EA8could be rescheduled. The plan was to reattempt the pumping job in a September 2021 campaign with the Helix Q4000intervention vessel.

Unfortunately, Hurricane Ida struck on August 29, 2021, leading to the termination of the contract for the Helix Q4000campaign. Several of the MPT tanks were submerged under water due to the storm surge, resulting in the contamination of theEA-8 SuperSolvent stored at the Port Fourchon dock.

mycm Testing confirmed that 8 out of the 14 tanks were contaminated and hadPage 13 of 59to be disposed of.

The project experienced delays due to high currents, and the tanks were subsequently damaged by storm surge from Hurricane Ida, leadingto the contamination and necessary disposal of the asphaltene super solvent.

039.short_description: Operational Overhead used instead of Development Overhead
039.description:
This exception relates to IR # 60.

The Joint Account was charged a 13% overhead for WBS P.US.EUR.NF.20.001.7240A.

This WBS is for Europa EA6 AV and SI Tube Remediation .

Per Section III,1,B,2 Application of Overhead of Exhibit C of the JOA:

For the purpose of determining charges on a percentage basis under Paragraph 1B of this Section III, development shall include all costs in connection with drilling, redrilling, or deepening of any or all wells, and shall also include any remedial operations requiring a period of five (5) consecutive work days or more on any or all wells.

Since this WBS is for remediation work that required more than 5 consecutive work days, the overhead rate charged should be the development OH rate of 2.5% instead of 13%. Please credit the Joint Account $132,577.83, which is the difference between the 2.5% OH and 13% OH on these WBS' charges.

Credit Denied.

It is reasonable to refer to UOA, Exhibit C, III Overhead, 1. A. (2) (b), which states that such charges shall be applied for theperiod from date workover operations commence through date of rig or other unit release.

The count of the five (5) workover operationscommence and stops when rig is released. Prepping activity, travel days, and standby time do not count as ded from the 5 consecutive workdays rule.After carefully reviewing the information provided by the Non-Operator, it has been observed that the Non-Operator hasapplied the counting of 5 consecutive work days between the two invoices in question inconsistently and not incompliance withthe guidelines provided by UOA and COPAS MFI-48.

Regarding the invoice # 20001946 of the Subsea invoice, the days included in the invoice are from Jan. 18th through Jan. 29th,2020. Although, the invoice item 1 shows a vessel operating day of 6.53 days but the invoice Item no. 11 and 12 have shownHRS Operational Rate (1/25 - 1/29) for 4.85 days and the HRS Standby Rate (1/18 - 1/25) for 6.65 days respectively.

Therefore, the work took only 4.85 days and did not take more than 5 consecutive workdays.

Please see below screen shot of item no. 11and 12. In regard to the invoice #20001896 of the Subsea invoice, the days included in the invoice are from March 27th thru April 2nd.The invoice item 1 shows a vessel operating day of 1.65days.

Therefore, the work was completed in 1.65days. It did not takemore than 5 consecutive workdays. Since both campaigns were completed less than 5 consecutive workdays, the Operational overhead rate is applied correctly.

No credit is due to the Joint Account.

The Operator charged the Europa Joint Account (multiple WBS) for diesel fuel according to the attached JADE lines. The total of the charges from 2019-2021 is $2,212,388.71

Upon review of the support provided for the entries (see "Working Summary" tab), the total amount of the charges should have been $2,162,642.41 for the period.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $50,989.96 ($49,746.31 plus 2.5% OH) for the excess diesel charges.

replies.text: Credit denied. According to SAP Actual Cost Line Items report for projects of all relevant WBS elements from accounting periods of 2019 to 2021, it shows a total charge of $1,794,886.83 which is $367,755.37 lower than the amount of $2,162,642.20 calculated by the auditor. It would have been a charge instead of a credit. Therefore, no credit is due to the Joint Account. Please see the attached file of CJI3 report for detail.

The Operator claims that based on their calculation the correct amount is $1,794,886.83, however, the Operator charged to Europa Joint Account (multiple WBS) for diesel fuel and according with the JADE lines from 2019-2021 is $2,212,388.71.

Hence, the Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $417,501.88 (plus 2.5% OH) forthe excess diesel charges.

Credit denied.

Upon further evaluation of the JADE line entries from 2020 to 2021, it was discovered that certain debit entries were notconsidered in the initial analysis of the Operator.

As a result, the fuel oil expense from 2019 to 2021 which amountsto $1,794,886.83, was inaccurately calculated and underestimated. Consequently, there is no overcharge of $367,755.37, and the Joint Account is not owed any credit based on this calculation.

Furthermore, it was observed that the fuel oil charges of $1,333,684.18 from 2019 were included in this audit exception.

mycm However, the Non-Operator failed to provide sufficient evidence to support the Fuel consumption number determined in the Summary."

It should be noted that since the examination pertains only to the expenditures from 2020 to 2021 onlyfor this 2022 Europa audit, the expenses incurred in 2019 are outside the scope of this review.

Therefore, it is advisable for theNon-Operator to withdraw or resubmit this exception due to the lack of adequate supporting documentation for the Fuel Consumption number calculation.

No credit is due to the Joint Account.

In its response on June 30, 2023, the Operator claims that the correct fuel charge should only be $1,798,886.83 which would have resulted in a higher credit due of $417,501.88 (plus overhead). Then on its response on Sept. 4, 2024, the Operator claims that this figure is erroneous. So far, t overcharged by $50,989.96 as summarized from backup documentation obtained during field work.

Credit remains due until the Operator can explain why their calculated charge differs from the amount charged to the Joint Account as summarized and attached on the original exception.

mycm

The Europa 3 was allocated $12,407.13 of Bristow U.S. LLC invoice 90032979 totaling $396,976.29 for helicopter services provided during October and November 2021. Per the helicopter logs, no services were provided to Europa 3.

Per the Operator's response to IR #64, "The MSC rate on the airframe is split between all entities that have access to the service so that cost is split based off level of flight activity associated with each charge code that is given for that monthly period".

The helicopter logs clearly indicate the properties that were serviced. In order to achieve an equitable distribution, this invoice should have been allocated among the properties that were serviced and benefitted from the helicopter services provided.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $12,407.13 plus overhead of $310.18 totaling $12,717.31.

056.description:
This exception relates to IR #63.

The Europa 2 was charged $18,082.42 of Bristow U.S. LLC invoice 90029316 for helicopter services provided during 4/15/2021 and 4/16/2021. Per the Helicopter Reservation Cost Code, the Europa 2 was charged the following total flight times.

4/15/2021 - 153 minutes (pg. 16)

4/16/2021 - 145 minutes (pg. 17)

Per the supporting helicopter logs, the flights on these dates were to transport a passenger from MC 984 (Vito)/Globetrotter 1 to KHUM (Houma-Terrebonne Airport). Per the Daily Operations Report for Europa 2, the Globetrotter began transit to Europa 2 on 4/16/2021.

In response to IR #63, the Operator indicated that these individuals were flown out early to support the upcoming work for EuropaA02, and, unfortunately, due to family emergencies, they had to leave. Per the Operator, the Globetrotter 1 was at Europa A02 at 12:00AM on April 16, 2021, so the flying time/ charge on 4/16 should not be an issue at all. The helicopter logs, the Helicopter Reservation Cost Code and the Operator's response did not include the names of these individuals.

The Operator is requested to provide the names of the individuals these flights relate to for the auditors' review or credit the Joint Account $18,082.42 plus 13% overhead.

06.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $1,067,688.71 for VIT 31.5 casing according to the provided JADE lines.

The charges into the Joint Account were for material transfers for used casing that was not new when charged to the Joint Account. As this casing is not new, it should have been charged to the Joint Account at the "Condition B" price, which in this instance is $240.85/FT according to the Operator's credits to the Joint Account. (See MT doc 405707769 included with JADE file).

At a condition B price of $240.85/FT the correct charge to the Joint Account is $597,392.23.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $482,053.89 ($470,296.48 plus 2.5% OH) for the incorrectly priced casing.

replies.text:

However, the value type "J11000-106" in the material transfer entry refers that it is all "Condition A" materials and the auditor has not provided any documentation to show the condition is otherwise.

Hence the Joint Account is charged for the correct amount/ price.

07.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $136,800 plus 2.5% OH ($140,220) for Nabors invoice TOSL-P000507 dated 12/8/2021. Upon review of the invoice, it is for a "monthly flat rate for 11/8/21 through 11/26/21. This was raised in Information Request 039 during the fieldwork.

The Personnel On Board the Q4000 were reviewed, and relevant POB lines are attached showing that no Nabors (or Tesco) personnel had been on board the Q4000 anywhere near the time period charged. The Operator was able to provide a Daily Operations Report which claimed personnel were on site, however the POB is the document of record required by the Coast Guard and therefore is believed to be the accurate reference. As the personnel were not on-site they were not capable of performing any services.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $140,220.00 ($136,800 plus 2.5%OH) for the unneeded/unused services.

replies.text:
Credit denied.

The EA-8 well was initially included in a campaign and C-Innovation was contracted to perform the job using the Island Intervention vessel in July 2021. However, due to high currents in the field, the pumping of the asphaltene super solvent for EA8 was not possible. As a result, the asphaltene super solvent was transferred to MPT tanks and stored at C-port until EA8 could be rescheduled. The plan was to reattempt the pumping job in a September 2021 campaign with the Helix Q4000 intervention vessel.

Unfortunately, Hurricane Ida struck on August 29, 2021, leading to the termination of the contract for the Helix Q4000 campaign. Several of the MPT tanks were submerged under water due to the storm surge, resulting in the contamination of the EA-8 SuperSolvent stored at the Port Fourchon dock. Testing confirmed that 8 out of the 14 tanks were contaminated and had to be disposed of. The assessment of the samples of asphaltene super solvent, conducted by Sky Spring Oil and Gas Service Co. on October 12, 2021, supported this finding. It is attached for reference.

Considering this series of events, the storage tanks were leased for the Europa EA8 Stimulation project. The project experienced delays due to high currents, and the tanks were subsequently damaged by storm surge from Hurricane Ida, leading to the contamination and necessary disposal of the asphaltene super solvent. Therefore, the charges for renting the storage tanks from August to November 2021 are correctly applied to the EA-8 Stimulation project. No credit is due to the Joint Account.

23.description:
This exception relates to IR # 48.

The Joint Account was charged $1,133,691.87 for Chemical Allocations related to Asphaltene Inhibitor, Scale Inhibitor, Corrosion Inhibitor, and Subsea 226 Black Oil Foamer for the period Q1, 2020 to Q4, 2021. While a spreadsheet was made available showing the methodology for the allocation, we were unable to ascertain the validity of the gallons used as the basis for allocation or the price charged for the Chemicals.

Please provide backup documentation to corroborate the pricing used for Chemical charges and the gallons used to allocate chemical charges to the Joint Account. Otherwise, please credit the Joint account for $1,133,691.87 plus 13% overhead.

table_references.summary: This table shows **Adjusted Credit (Total)** figures broken down by year/period, split between "Credit" and "Cost" categories. Credit values span from 2020 to Q1/Q2 2022, with the highest amount in 2020 at **$20,991**, followed by **$16,359** in 2021, and a notably lower **$517** in Q1/Q2 2022. The only Cost entry is for Q3/Q4 2022, valued at **$15,315**.

This table contains two financial transactions with dates, amounts, and reference numbers. The transactions include a positive amount of **$37,867.00** (dated 03/24, ref. 131821010) and a negative amount of **-$15,315.16** (dated 08/22, ref. 131270640), suggesting one credit and one debit/reversal entry.

replies.text:
Credit denied. Since this exception is looking for backup documentation for the pricing used for Chemical charges and the gallons used to allocate chemical charges to the Joint Account, instead of having audit claim for the entire charges, it is more appropriated to have the audit claim as " TBD".

Europa is a subsea field that ties back to Mars TLP (MC 807). For the gallons used, it is based on Mars operation generated log on daily basis to capture the EA chemical daily usage. The unit is captured in gallon. Operation documents this on daily basis, and to arrive at the monthly usage. Please see the attached file for the tab of Europa Manual Rate Log for detail. And the pricing used for Chemical charges is based on information from the vendor. Please see attached file for the tab of "Pricing of Chemical Charge" for detail.

39.short_description: Operational Overhead used instead of Development Overhead
39.description:
This exception relates to IR # 60.

The Joint Account was charged a 13% overhead for WBS P.US.EUR.NF.20.001.7240A. This WBS is for Europa EA6 AV and SI Tube Remediation.

Per Section III,1,B,2 Application of Overhead of Exhibit C of the JOA:

For the purpose of determining charges on a percentage basis under Paragraph 1B of this Section III, development shall include all costs in connection with drilling, redrilling, or deepening of any or all wells, and shall also include any remedial operations requiring a period of five (5) consecutive work days or more on any or all wells.

Since this WBS is for remediation work that required more than 5 consecutive work days, the overhead rate charged should be the development OH rate of 2.5% instead of 13%. Please credit the Joint Account $132,577.83, which is the difference between the 2.5% OH and 13% OH on these WBS' charges.

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

It is reasonable to refer to UOA, Exhibit C, III Overhead, 1. A. (2) (b), which states that such charges shall be applied for the period from date workover operations commence through date of rig or other unit release. The count of the five (5) consecutive workdays or more for any remedial operations begins in the wellbore 'on the well' date workover operations commence and stops when rig is released. Prepping activity, travel days, and standby time do not count as being 'on the well' and are excluded from the 5 consecutive workdays rule.

After carefully reviewing the information provided by the Non-Operator, it has been observed that the Non-Operator has applied the counting of 5 consecutive work days between the two invoices in question inconsistently and not incompliance with the guidelines provided by UOA and COPAS MFI-48.

In regard to the invoice # 20001946 of the Subsea invoice, the days included in the invoice are from Jan. 18th through Jan. 29th, 2020. Although, the invoice item 1 shows a vessel operating day of 6.53 days but the invoice Item no. 11 and 12 have shown HRS Operational Rate (1/25 - 1/29) for 4.85 days and the HRS Standby Rate (1/18 - 1/25) for 6.65 days respectively. Therefore, the work took only 4.85 days and did not take more than 5 consecutive work days. Please see below screen shot of item no. 11 and 12.

[table 2]

In regard to the invoice #20001896 of the Subsea invoice, the days included in the invoice are from March 27th thru April 2nd. The invoice item 1 shows a vessel operating days of 1.65days. Therefore, the work was completed in 1.65days. It did not take more than 5 consecutive work days.

Since both campaigns were completed less than 5 consecutive workdays, the Operational overhead rate is applied correctly. No credit is due to the Joint Account.

The Europa 001 - NGT1 Covid AFE was charged $261,733.27 on SPA Doc 130276824 for COVID 19 Asset charges related to April 2021. The Joint Account was also charged $273,295.61 on SAP Doc 130484382 for COVID 19 Asset charges related to April 2021 and May 2021. The breakdown is included below.

55.description:
This exception relates to IR #64.

The Europa 3 was allocated $12,407.13 of Bristow U.S. LLC invoice 90032979 totaling $396,976.29 for helicopter services provided during October and November 2021. Per the helicopter logs, no services were provided to Europa 3.

Per the Operator's response to IR #64, "The MSC rate on the airframe is split between all entities that have access to the service so that cost is split based off level of flight activity associated with each charge code that is given for that monthly period".

The helicopter logs clearly indicate the properties that were serviced. In order to achieve an equitable distribution, this invoice should have been allocated among the properties that were serviced and benefitted from the helicopter services provided.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $12,407.13 plus overhead of $310.18 totaling $12,717.31.

replies.text:
Credit denied. The charge in question is from Bristow US LLC which is contracted for Search and Rescue (SAR), all assets in the based on total flight minutes. More flight minutes results in a higher allocation of the SAR Fixed Fee. When an asset executes an actual SAR journey, the asset is directly charged 100% for the journey. GoM share the SAR Fixed Fee, a "subscription" fee for access to SAR services. The SAR Fixed Fee is allocated proportionally

In according to Rig Schedule, it shows that the Rig of Helix Q4000 was at EUROPA A-03 (MC 0934 OCS-G 07975) from November 7 to November 26. And from the 2021 Helicopter reservation table, it also showed many trips have been made to Helix Q4000 for the activities of Joint Account.

Therefore, it is accurate to split invoice of Bristow among all assets based off their level of flight activity for that billing month.

The Operator is requested to provide the names of the individuals these flights relate to for the auditors' review or credit the Joint Account $18,082.42 plus 13% overhead.

001.description:
The Operator charged the Great White Joint Account $5,415,510.97 for Benefits & Burden uplift on all payroll cost charged into Great White in 2021.

A re-calculation of the B&B Uplift percentages against the charges noted that for October 2021, there was an overcharge of $33,839.23 plus 2.5% OH totaling $34,669.16. This was the subject of Information Request #02 which was raised during the field-work of the audit.

On 5/3/2022 the Operator replied confirming that the B&B calculation was incorrect in October on two WBS elements; P.US.AOP.EO.21.024.14 and P.US.AOP.EO.21.030.14 for $33,823.57, and that the correction had been made on SAP Doc #130951219 and provided the correction voucher dated 4/30/2022.

As the Operator has reviewed and corrected the issue during the Information Request process during fieldwork, this Exception is included here for information purposes only.

002.short_description: Rig - Pontus - CML MPD Upgrade
002.description:
The Operator charged the Great White Joint Account $16,191,669.06 plus 2.5% OH for a CML MPD Upgrade to the Transocean Pontus. This equipment was installed in late 2019 for 2020 and 2021 availability on Great White 001 and 003 P&A as well as some Perdido Phase 2 work.

This issue was raised in Great White Information Request (IR) 40 during the audit fieldwork. The Operator responded to this IR with a letter agreement dated February 2, 2017, signed by all parties covering the GD002 and GD003 wells which were drilled by the Transocean Thalassa. As the Thalassa is a different rig than the Pontus, this letter agreement is not applicable to the charges subject to this exception.

This system appears to have been permanently installed on the Pontus and will remain available for any and all subsequent wells drilled during the term of the rig's contract with the Operator. According to the Transocean Fleet Status Report, the Pontus remains on contract with Shell until October 2027 (5 years from now).

The Joint Account was charged directly for this upgrade; however, this cost appears to be one that should have been put in an accumulator account and then amortized over the (remaining) term of the rig contract. The Non-Operators understand that subsequent to a reversal and re-allocation, the GW properties will bear some portion of the allocated cost. The Auditors reserve the right to review the reallocation of an accumulator account once completed.

The Operator is requested to credit the Great White Joint Account $16,596,460.79 ($16,191,669.06 plus 2.5% OH of $404,791.73), less the reallocated portion, with reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text: This exception is currently being reviewed.

attachments: Great White MPD Letter Agreement Feb 2017.pdf

003.description:
The Operator charged the Great White Joint Account $600,314.21 plus 13% overhead for Non-Major Construction Overhead Payroll for employees who did not work onsite through allocations. The Auditors reviewed employee hours charged to the Joint Account compared to the number of days onsite per the POB reports to calculate the hours per day ratio (hours charged / number of days on POB.) Employees identified as offsite were not on board per the POB and helicopter logs. This was raised to the Operator in Great White Information Request 27 during the fieldwork.

Offsite payroll and burden is covered by overhead, per the Accounting Procedure at Exhibit "C", Section III Overhead, Paragraph (ii) which states, The salaries, wages and Personal Expenses of Technical Employees and/or costs of professional consulting services and contract services of technical personnel either temporally or permanently assigned to and directly employed in the operation of the Joint Property: (x) shall be covered by the overhead rates.

Additionally, the description of work provided by the Operator was compared to the various Billing Standards and was not found to be in compliance with Attachment 1 "Agreed OTL Definitions and Billing Standards", Section 3.A. "Regulatory Activity", 3.B. "Feasibility and Project Studies", and 3.C. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration". Included in supporting files is a column called "BP Comment" with a more detailed explanation of the reason for noncompliance with the Billing Standards.

For reference, this exception applies to three exceptions from the 2022 audit, Great White exception 3, Silvertip exception 27 and Tobago exception 11.

The Operator is requested to credit the Great White Joint Account $678,355.06 ($600,314.21 plus 13% overhead of $78,040.85) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number of the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
During the audit fieldwork the Operator provided information (including staff listings and job titles) in regards to the employees flagged by the Auditor. By using the Staff Listing, it is shown that the majority of employees are not above first level supervision as they either do not have reportees or if they do, then those reportees do not have direct reports. This Staff Listing must be used to determine job hierarchy as job titles alone will not provide this level of detail.

In addition, the employees were compared to the Settlement Agreement "Agreed OTL Definitions and Billing Standards". This determined which section they fall under from Section 3. OTL Chargeable Activities. And lastly, engineers may not be mentioned in sections 3.A; B; or C but they are specifically included in Section 2 "Definition of Technical Employees" which is the basis for section 3.

Please see attached for supporting documentation. The credit noted is in the process of being posted.

attachments: IR 27 - Staff Job Desc revised may 10 2022 JL Comments.xlsx

004.description:
The Operator charged the Great White Joint Account $679,974.68 for recurring and regular storage charges as according to the provided JADE lines. Upon review, storage charges cannot exceed six months unless the storage is related to critical spares and there must be a written agreement. This was the subject of Great White Information Request 30 which was raised during the fieldwork.

Please refer to the Billing Standards, Third Party Staging, Warehouse Facilities: For approved projects . . . . The chargeable amounts are limited to periods of six (6) months or less occurring prior to execution of the project. After use of the material or equipment for the Joint Operation is completed, the equipment or material storage costs will no longer be charged to the Joint Account unless the Parties have agreed in writing that the material or equipment is a critical spare.

The effective dates for the billing standards was January 1, 2020 for BP and January 1, 2019 for Chevron. As the audit period covered costs for January through December 2020, these billing standards would apply to this audit.

The Operator is requested to provide documentation for these critical spares as outlined in the billing standards or credit the Great White Joint Account $693,574.17 ($679,974.68 plus 2% overhead of $13,599.49) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number of the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text: This exception is currently being reviewed.

005.description:
The Operator charged the Great White Joint Account $172,849 for multiple Operator personnel above first level supervision which is covered by overhead. This was the subject of Great White Information Request 29 (GW IR-29) which was raised during the fieldwork. The specific individuals subject to this exception are a Mr. AJ Cozzens (who supervises Mr. Keith Hunt, who in turn supervises Ms. Karen Godfrey and Mr. Matt McDonald). This is noted in the "Org Structure" tab of the Report+P Cable excel file which is part of this exception.

As per the Geo-Operations Team Lead response on May 3, 2022, the personnel noted by the Auditor are Staff and were involved in the planning, preparations and operational management of the Cable Seismic Data Acquisition project as follows:

Matthew McDonald: Performed the survey design and the competitive tender which awarded NCS the work;

Keith Hunt : Team Lead providing guidance, support, and assurance to all standards throughout. Responsible for delivery of project;

Karen Godfrey : Project Manager for detailed planning and preparations and operational oversight;

AJ Cozzens : Provided technical assurance for the planning and survey design and overall accountability for the work;

Lewis French : Provided HSE management, oversight, and advice on complying with HSSE Control Framework.

Mr. Keith Hunt is noted to be part of "US AAP Job 1C - Middle Management - (Professional)" according to the 2021 SEPCO Staff listing provided by the Operator during the fieldwork (see Org Structure" tab, Col. S). The Settlement Agreement Attachment 1, Section 1.b. Definition of "Technical Employees" also states in part "For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include [...] management, supervision (excluding first level supervision of operational staff which is billable) [...]". Therefore Mr. Hunt's charges are not permissible under the Settlement Agreement.

The Operator stated, in their response to GW IR-29 that Ms. Karen Godfrey was "Project Manager for detailed planning and preparations and operational oversight." According to the Settlement Agreement, Billing Standards, Section k. Third-Party Project Management, "[...] costs related to third party project management that are charged as part of the overall cost for provision of goods and services [...] may be charged to the Joint Account as a component cost of the underlying goods and services and shall not be qualified as OTL or administrative costs covered under Overhead." As Ms. Godfrey is not Third-Party as required by the Settlement Agreement, but rather First-Party as a Shell employee, her project management services are disallowed under the Settlement Agreement.

Additionally, according to the Operator's response on GW IR-29, Mr. Matt McDonald "performed the survey design and the competitive tender which awarded NCS the work". Competitive Tendering is part of the Procurement process, and is disallowed by both the JOA and interpreting MFI's as noted below, as well as the Settlement Agreement Attachment 1, Section 1.b. Definition of "Technical Employees" which states in part that "For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include procurement [...]".

The Accounting Procedure attached to and made a part of the Joint Operating Agreement, "Exhibit C, Section III Overhead states,

"As compensation for administrative, supervision, office services and warehousing costs, Operator shall charge the Joint Account in accordance with this Section III.

Under Section II. Direct Charges, only First level supervision is allowed"

Per MFI 21, charges for services like planning, budgeting, legal, HR, procurement, etc., are Indirect Costs and are not allowed to be charged as Direct costs. Individuals performing such functions charged to the Joint Account are marked on our support provided to the Operator as "Other Covered by OVHD."

The Operator is requested to credit the Great White Joint Account $177,170.23 ($172,849.00 plus 2.5% overhead of $4,321.23) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number of the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
As noted in the Letter Agreement signed in July 2021 by both co-owners for the Great White Seismic P-Cable project, and attached by the auditor as support for the claim, the work performed by the team mentioned in this exception is covered under paragraph 9 costs (see below), which shall be direct billable. According to the Great White UOA Exhibit "C", Addendum to Exhibit "C", Statement of Clarification and Intent, the Operator may charge affiliate cost at an "all-inclusive standard rate" per the following: Affiliates shall maintain auditable records to support all charges made by it to the Joint Account and as to such charges shall be subject to the same audit requirements provided for Operator's charges in Section I, Paragraph 5 of this Exhibit "C." If an all-inclusive standard unit rate is used, such audit requirements shall be limited to verification that such rate is, in fact, the rate(s) customarily charged by its Affiliates.

007.description:
The Operator charged the Great White Joint Account $378,097.14 ($624,793.29 including B&B and OH) for timewriting provided by employees. This was the subject of Information Request 005 raised in the Fieldwork.

Upon review, none of the employees were found to be on-site at Perdido. These employees were found to be working at other projects, Mars, Auger, Poseidon, etc. Additionally, many were found not to have gone offshore.

According to the Chevron/Shell and BP/Shell Settlement Agreement Billing Standards, offsite technical labor is only billable for "Regulatory Activity, Feasibility and Project Studies, and Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration". To date, the Operator has not provided a description of the work activities for each employee, for the time periods charged, in accordance with the BP/Shell agreed ways of working discussed and agreed in February 2022 snipped below. Per this agreement, the Operator is required to identify the title (if unclear) email the employee (manager if employee not available) and provide a screenshot of the email.

The Operator has not provided emails as agreed or any other adequate documentation showing that OTL performed is in compliance with the Settlement Agreements signed by Co-Owners. In the Operators response to IR 005, for people subject to this exception, there were only two responses covering all individuals and all time periods. This appears inaccurate as many individuals would have been doing many different tasks throughout the year.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $624,793.29 ($378,282.86 plus B&B of $208,122.71 plus OH of $38,387.72) for the OTL not in compliance with the Settlement Agreement.
