015.short_description: OTL not in Compliance with Settlement Agreement
015.description:
The Operator charged the Great White Joint Account $224,003.97, before overhead, for Total System Integrators to provide Perdido General Support and Perdido Alarm Suppression Support through various monthly invoices. The invoices totaling $250,230.06 were allocated from the PRH Shared Opex - Perform Well and Facility WBS (O.US.132.PER.001.71300).

The Operator's response to Perdido Information Request 25 was that the sampled invoice 'included work to improve process safety and production availability on the Yokowama control system….this system is absolutely critical to be able to operate Perdido and is the entire interface that operations uses to control and maintain the process conditions within the optimal and safe operating ranges. The three consultants noted on the invoice worked on pipeline pump improvement, alarm management, and safety improvements. Based on COPAS MFI 44, these charges are direct billable to the Joint Account.'

While the offsite technical labor (OTL) providing IT support for the billable systems used on the platform may be required, they do not qualify for direct chargeability under the Billing Standards settlement agreements between the parties, as they have not been adequately and properly documented by the Operator as activities required to comply with regulatory activities, and they have not been identified as Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration whose job function was previously performed offshore/onsite but were relocated onshore.

The Operator is requested to credit the Great White Joint Account $253,124.49 ($224,003.97 plus 13% overhead of $29,120.52) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
The offsite technical labor noted by the Auditor was through TSI which is the core contractor that Shell uses to develop code for the Yokogawa control system. As noted in the Operator response to IR #25 during the audit fieldwork, this labor is supported by COPAS MFI 44 by being included under the software costs. The work done on this invoice was programming, testing, and developing installation procedures for various upgrade projects to improve process safety or production availability. More specifically:

- Devin was an assistant programmer for Perdido projects. His work was primarily programming for a pipeline pump improvement and a safety improvement for the topsides separation system.
- Mohammad was the primary asset support programmer for Perdido. His time was spent on a variety of projects supporting alarm management, control and safety improvements, and general troubleshooting to assist the offshore Electronics Technicians.
- Salvadores work was in support of our Alarm Management program for the facility. He was involved in making backups of the alarm database, helping to configure a new server for the system, and correcting the reports that the asset support team uses for technical monitoring.

Their work was directly associated with alarm management (Process Safety Basic Requirement within Shells HSSE framework); Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) action items that required remediation (required to maintain adequate process safety); and pipeline pump control logic improvements required to maintain the export pump system health (therefore required to keep the facility functional). In addition to their work being supported by MFI 44, these items are in the SEMS CFR 250.1910 category as well as under the Settlement Agreement Billing Standards for facility improvement projects.

No credit is due.

016.short_description: OTL not in Compliance with Settlement Agreement
016.description:
The Operator charged the Great White Joint Account $84,970.29, before overhead, for drafting & engineering services provided by Worley ECR Services on Invoice No. 332380. The invoice totaling $94,750.06 was allocated from the PRH Shared Opex - Perform Well and Facility WBS (O.US.132.PER.001.71300).

The Billing Standards settlement agreements between the parties only allows for offsite technical labor (OTL) associated with field improvement or facility improvement projects, and for feasibility studies undertaken to progress future projects, pursuant to a separately approved Authorization for Expenditure (AFE).

The Operator's response to Perdido Information Request 27 stated the water filtration equipment was temporary rental equipment and that no AFE was sent for election as it was production operations. Since the project was for operations and an AFE was not submitted as outlined in the Billing Standards, the OTL associated with the temporary water filtration equipment project is not chargeable.

The Operator is requested to credit the Great White Joint Account $96,016.43 ($84,970.29 plus 13% overhead of $11,046.14) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
As per the Asset Finance Manager and Shell Senior Legal Counsel, the Perdido overboard water was out of compliance with National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit, and the NPDES permits are governed by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). The Operator then had to install the equipment after EPA required them to mitigate in the short term with the carbon filtration temporary equipment. The Operator then had to engage BSEE for the limited purposes of submitting the topside modifications. These steps were necessary to bring the host into compliance with applicable law, regulations and permits. These charges are covered under the Settlement Agreement Billing Standards Regulatory Activities. The Auditor is requested to engage with their commercial teams as the charges being part of production operations were fully communicated to co-owners as well as being part of the co-owner meeting engagements.

No credit is due.

034.description:
Great White projects were allocated $919,540.16 during 2020-2021 for the $7.5 million estimated cost to demobilize the drillship Transocean Pontus at the end of the contract term as per guidelines stated in COPAS Model Form Interpretation 56, Rig Related Costs. The estimated cost was allocated based on initial contract term of 5 years, October 22, 2017 through October 22, 2022. The day rate of $4,105.09 ($7.5 million divided by 1,827 days) was billed to Great White for 224 days during this period.

A review of the Transocean Fleet Status report, Fleet Status Report | Transocean Investor Relations (deepwater.com), dated April 25, 2022 showed the Transocean Pontus estimated current contract expiration date of October 2027. Based on this information, the Transocean Pontus contract was extended to Shell for another 5 years.

COPAS MFI-56 states, If the Company extends the Rig Contract term, the recommended practice is to treat the Rig Contract extension period as a new Rig Contract rather than reallocating the Rig-Related Costs from the inception of the original Rig Contract to the termination date of the Rig Contract extension period. The MFI also stated that if another Company operating in the same area hires the Rig immediately following the end of the Rig Contract, there might not be a Demobilization cost or fee.

Because the extension is treated as a new Rig Contract immediately following the end of the original contract term, there

should not be any estimated demobilization cost allocated to the projects served under the original contract term. The Operator is requested to credit the Great White Joint Account $942,528.66 ($919,540.16 plus 2.5% overhead of $22,988.50) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text: This exception is currently being reviewed.

The estimated cost was allocated based on initial contract term of 5 years, February 6, 2016 through February 5, 2021. The day rate of $4,105.09 ($7.5 million divided by 1,827 days) was billed to Great White projects for 99 days during this period.

A review of the Transocean Fleet Status report, Fleet Status Report | Transocean Investor Relations (deepwater.com), dated April 25, 2022 showed the Transocean Thalassa estimated current contract expiration date of February 2026. Based on this information, the Transocean Thalassa contract was extended to Shell for another 5 years.

COPAS MFI-56 states, If the Company extends the Rig Contract term, the recommended practice is to treat the Rig Contract extension period as a new Rig Contract rather than reallocating the Rig-Related Costs from the inception of the original Rig Contract to the termination date of the Rig Contract extension period. The MFI also stated that if another Company operating in the same area hires the Rig immediately following the end of the Rig Contract, there might not be a Demobilization cost or fee.

Because the extension is treated as a new Rig Contract immediately following the end of the original contract term, there should not be any estimated demobilization cost allocated to the projects served under the original contract term.

036.description: The Operator charged the Great White Joint Account $1,332,095.04, before overhead, for a monthly Perdido Gas Buyback allocation during 2020-2021. The journal entries totaling $1,515,833.23 were allocated from the PRH Shared Opex - Perform Well and Facility WBS (O.US.132.PER.001.71300). Per Section 3.b of Perdido COUA Exhibit P-1 (Great White PHA Terms) and Exhibit P2 (Silvertip and Tobago PHA Terms), 'Host fuel gas consumption would be allocated on a monthly basis (based on production actually processed through the Host) to the Pr oducers…for production handling and operating services. The Producers would be obligated to and would furnish their monthlyallocated share of fuel gas…production handling and operating services in kind.' Based on the Production Schematic provided on the r evenue audit, the gas buyback is not flowing through the sales meter, but instead is taken to the Operations Master Fuel meter to be used as fuel gas. As a result, the value of this gas should not be a shared expenses nor be subject to the overhead percentage. The Operator is requested to credit the Great White Joint Account $1,505,267.40 ($1,332,095.04 plus 13% overhead of $173,172.36) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
The BSEE surface commingling permit drawing shows a simplified process flow diagram of the master fuel meter and two paths for fuel gas to flow to that master fuel meter.

During normal operations, all fuel is sourced from production and flow to the master fuel meter upstream of the sales meters (red dashed line). In this scenario, there is no gas flowing through the gas buyback meter.

During start-up or when leaner gas is needed for fuel, fuel gas will be sourced downstream of the sales meters. This fuel gas will be measured through the gas buyback meter prior to being measured by the master fuel gas meter (green dashed line). In this scenario, any production not following the normal red dashed line to the master fuel meter will flow through the sales meters (blue dashed line).

Within the Fuel Allocation section of Article VII Allocation in the Perdido Regional Host Measurement and Allocation Procedures Amendment No. 3, the measured buyback volume is removed from the measured fuel gas volume (master fuel gas volume) prior to allocating to the producing wells.

The Producers are getting credit for all gas that flows through the sales gas meters. Shell is buying any additional fuel gas needed downstream of the sales gas meters which is measured by the gas buyback meter and the buyback fuel gas OPEX is associated with this fuel gas not delivered by the Producers.

No credit is due.

replies.text:
As noted during the fieldwork, the Operator does not own the inventory at the vendor's facility. The contract provision described by Exhibit "C", Section III Overhead of the Unit Operating Agreement (UOA) is for when an Operator owns the warehouse and the inventory. Since this does not describe the sample submitted by the Auditor, the above contract provision does not apply.

Per UOA, Exhibit 'C' Section II Direct Charges, 4. Material, Material purchased or furnished by Operator for use on the Joint Property as provided under Section IV. Only such material shall be purchased for or transferred to the Joint Property as may be required for immediate use and is reasonably practical and consistent with efficient and economical operations. The accumulation of surplus stocks shall be avoided.

The consignment fee (which is neither a warehousing nor a storage fee) provides operational and cost efficiencies for the Joint Property with immediate availability and preventing the accumulation of surplus stock. The Joint Account will be invoiced by the vendor for these items when they have been shipped offshore for installation or consumption. Any items that are then not used, consumed or installed can be returned and credited to the Joint Account.

No credit is due.

The contract provision described by Exhibit "C", Section III Overhead of the Unit Operating Agreement (UOA) is for when an Operator owns the warehouse and the inventory. Since this does not describe the sample submitted by the Auditor, the above contract provision does not apply.

Per UOA, Exhibit 'C' Section II Direct Charges, 4. Material, Material purchased or furnished by Operator for use on the Joint Property as provided under Section IV. Only such material shall be purchased for or transferred to the Joint Property as may be required for immediate use and is reasonably practical and consistent with efficient and economical operations. The accumulation of surplus stocks shall be avoided.

The consignment fee (which is neither a warehousing nor a storage fee) provides operational and cost efficiencies for the Joint Property with immediate availability and preventing the accumulation of surplus stock. The Joint Account will be invoiced by the vendor for these items when they have been shipped offshore for installation or consumption. Any items that are then not used, consumed or installed can be returned and credited to the Joint Account.

No credit is due.

The material in question must be stored prior to usage and this storage "consignment" is the nature of the fee in question, which is disallowed by the JOA as it represents warehouse performance and inventory carrying cost.

From the Consignment Fee Contract:

## SCMFEE

SCM fees are subject to review and adjustment based on forecast accuracy and inventory turn performance. SCM Fees will be applied to the DDP price quoted to COMPANY for a particular item at time of mill order placement as per below. For a first 12 month period, the initial SCM fee shall be applied. The inventory turn will be measured during that period and the SCM fee for the next 6 months shall be determined based on a trailing 12-month inventory turn rate per below table. Inventory turns shall be calculated utilizing only those items that belong to the respective category. This process will repeat every six months as part of the overall inventory management review process. Any variation in 3-month LIBOR rates outside the range of 0.5%-1.5% shall be discussed between COMPANY and CONTRACTOR during the review meetings to determine how SCM fees shall be adjusted.

As this fee represents the cost of warehousing, it is covered by Overhead, and full credit remains due.

The Operator does not own the inventory at the vendor's facility and the Joint Account is not charged for the material until it is shipped out for installation, thus avoiding an accumulation of surplus stock. The service provided by Sumitomo, including consignment is direct chargeable as per the Operating Agreement, Exhibit 'C', Section II, 5.E, ' Pursuant to Article 5.1 of the Agreement, the Operator will procure services for Joint Operations based on contractual terms it deems appropriate. Costs related to those service contracts will be passed through to the Joint Account as billed by the vendor, or such costs will be allocated appropriately if the service benefits multiple properties .' The Operators position has not changed, and these charges are direct billable to the Joint Account.

In addition, the Operator requests the Auditor to provide where they obtained a snip-it of a contract, as after a review of the IR's it does not appear it was provided during the fieldwork of the current audit. Please provide the documentation in entirety and when it was obtained.

Not included are storage or carrying costs." The contract clause applies to material, not exclusively Operator owned material. Material provided by a third party is subject to Section IV.3.C.

007.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $2,586,138.51 in accumulator costs for rig mobilization, upgrades. These were the subject of Information Request 17 issued to the Operator during the fieldwork.

According to the attached JADE lines, in year 2020, the Globetrotter II rig charged $2,373,689.72 in costs using an allocation basis of 477 days according to the NGT II Accumulator Consolidated workbook, provided with the IR, which matches the JADE charges. According to the Noble Fleet Status report, also provided with the IR, the contract with Shell should be 1705 days. (Jan 1 2019 to Sept 1 2023).

Additionally, the workbooks used a budget figure to calculate the charges, not the actual costs, and no true-up was provided by the Operator. The budgeted mobilization figure used is $21,300,000 vs actual cost of $19,538,249. The budgeted upgrades figure used is $11,050,000 vs actual cost of $161,656. The Operator did not provide information regarding any potential true-up during the audit fieldwork.

A revised accumulator sheet has been prepared to accompany this exception using the corrected contract length which leads to a day rate of $11,459.38/day for mobilization and $94.81/day for the modifications. Using the corrected day rates, multiplied by 35 days of rig usage equals a charge of $404,396.87 which is what should have been charged to the Joint Account. The total overcharge to the Joint Account in 2020 is ($2,373,689.72-$404,396.87)=$1,969,292.85 plus overhead.

The JADE line from 2021 (Ref Doc # 130052082) does not have the correct NGT II Accumulator Consolidated workbook attached in SAP. Therefore, the auditor was unable to validate the calculation for the charge to the Joint Account of $212,448.79. The Operator is requested to provide the workbook which includes this support or credit the Joint Account.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $2,181,741.64 ($1,969,292.85 + $212,448.79) plus 2.5% overhead.

* an increase for upgrade from $11,050,000 budget to $12,168,425.12 actuals

replies.text:
The auditor is not able to make assessment from the snippet without key information such as the underlying rig, the parties involved in the contract, etc. Please kindly provide the full contract.

The auditor stand by the time period by which the accumulators should be amortized over the life of the agreement with the rig owner, the rationales have been laid out in COPAS MFI-53 and MFI-56 quoted below:

"Rig-related costs also include all costs for commissioning and mobilization of a rig, including, but not limited to, sea trials and transportation of the rig from its construction site to the Gulf of Mexico . "

"Generally speaking, Rig-Related Costs are borne by the properties that benefit. For costs such as construction, commissioning, and mobilization, that includes all the properties served over the life of the agreement with the rig owner. "

mycm MFI-56 Section VI notes the following regarding rig modifications:

"Rig modifications include, but are not limited to, changes made to meet: government regulations, technical requirements or specifications to make the rig suitable for drilling in a particular area or under certain drilling conditions; the Company's needs or standards, or to perform specific operations functions. "

"Often Rig Modifications benefit all wells drilled over the remaining life of the Rig Contract, but they could benefit only a subset of wells. "

Thus, it is incorrect for the Operator to use the time period when NGT2 is drilling at Great White to allocate mobilization and upgrade costs. These costs should be amortized for purposes of calculating charges over the life of the agreement with the rig owner.

In this case, NGT2 is leased to Shell for 1,705 days and therefore mobilization costs should be allocated over this period to all properties benefitting from the service of this rig during this time.

With that, the Auditor believes the revised accumulator sheet prepared on September 24, 2024 rebuttal to calculate charges to the Joint Account remains valid. By using actual costs ($33,673,773.15) and the corrected rig contract days (1,705 days) which leads to a day rate of $12,613.11 per day for mobilization and $7,136.91 per day for the modifications. Multiplying the corrected day rates by 35 days of rig usage equals a charge of $691,250.48 which is what should have been charged to the Joint Account. The total overcharge to the Joint Account is ($2,586,138.51 -$691,250.48) = $1,894,888.03 plus overhead. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $1,894,888.03 plus 2.5% overhead equals to $1,942,260.23.

mycm

Upon cross referencing the employee name with the POB list and helicopter logs, the employees were shown to be at other locations, or were not found, during the time period in question as noted in the "comments" field. This was the subject of Information Request 021 that was unanswered by the end of fieldwork.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $49,856.67 plus 2.5% Overhead for the coding errors.

Chevron was overcharged a net $1,291,208.45 relating to the operating rig rates billed to Chevron for floater rig Transocean Pontus conducting work on the Great White asset during 2021. The rig rates charged to Chevron during the drilling of the Great White and Silvertip leases were based on an agreement between Shell Offshore Inc and SOI Finance Inc. They were not the Contractor Rate that Transocean billed to Shell Oil Company.

In accordance with section 2.5 A of the Settlement Agreement effective January 1, 2019, Chevron agrees to pay the Contractor Rate for any rig-related operations conducted on or after the Effective Date of this Settlement Agreement at any Legacy OA assets, which includes the Great White UOA.

An analysis of the difference between the Contractor Rate billed to Shell Oil Company and the rate billed to Chevron for the accounting period January 1, 2021 through December 31, 2021, showed a net difference of $1,259,715.56 plus 2.5% overhead of $31,492.89.

Chevron should be credited a net of $1,291,208.45 with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

02.description:
Chevron was overcharged a net $169,912.43 relating to the operating and reduced rig rates included in the Transocean Pontus initial mobilization and startup cost pools that are being allocated to properties being serviced. The rig rates that are included in the pool allocation costs were based on an agreement between Shell Offshore Inc and SOI Finance Inc. They were not the Contractor Rate that Transocean billed to Shell Oil Company.

In accordance with section 2.5 A of the Settlement Agreement signed in July 2021 and made effective January 1, 2019, Chevron and Shell agreed to pay the Contractor Rate for any rig-related operations conducted on or after the Effective Date of this Settlement Agreement at any Legacy OA assets, which includes the Great White UOA.

An analysis of the operating and reduced operating rates used by Shell Oil Company and the actual Transocean rates that were included in the cost pool resulted in a reduced overall cost pool daily rate of $2,220.33. The Great White asset used the Transocean Pontus rig for 224 days from June 2020 through January 2021. Gross credit of $497,354.38 times our 33.33% working interest shows net credit due of $165,768.22 plus 2.5% overhead of $4,144.21.

Chevron should be credited a net of $169,912.43 with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

001.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $418,245.05 on various Sumitomo Corporation Of Americas invoices for SCM Fee Consignment charges. This is a management fee and is not a direct cost of the material but an additional fee to house the material and ensure it is available when needed.

Exhibit 'C' Section III Overhead of the Unit Operating Agreement states: "As compens ation for administrative, supervision, office services and warehousing costs, Operator shall charge the Joint Account in accordance with this Section III.'

Additionally, AG 19, Section IV.3.C states 'Actual costs may include costs of (I) Material, (2) mak ing it suitable for use, and (3) transportation from the point of acquisition to the Joint Property including loading and unloading. Not included are storage or carrying costs." This was the subject of Information Request 009 which was raised during the audit field work.

The Operator is requested to reimburse joint account for$418,245.05 plus overhead of 2.5%.

replies.text: Credit Denied. Per BP-SOI Settlement Agreement, dated December 2018, Section 3 Billing Disputes Paragraph l. Third-Party Project Management - Ancillary costs related to third party project management that are charged as part of the overall cost for provision of goods and services by such third party associated with a third party's provision of goods and services may be charged to the Joint Account as a component cost of the underlying goods and services and shall not be qualified as OTL or as administrative costs covered under Overhead. Sumitomo SCM fee is a component cost of the underlying goods and services, and it does not qualify as OTL or administrative costs covered under Overhead.

The SCM Fee is not third party project management, therefore the above cited provision of the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement does not apply. The SCM Fee is a storage/warehousing cost being charged by the vendor. Costs of this nature are not chargeable under either the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement or the UOA. Full credit remains due.

This Sumitomo Supply Chain Management (SCM) fee is the Ancillary costs related to Sumitomo project management that is charged as part of the overall cost for provision of goods and services. With this SCM fee that has enable Joint operation to

mycm comply to UOA, Exhibit 'C' Section II Direct Charges, 4. Material, only such material shall be purchased for or transferred to the Joint Property as may be required for immediate use…. The accumulation of surplus stocks could be avoided.

Per the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement, Section 3 Billing Disputes Paragraph l, third-party project management costs by such third party associated with a third party's provision of goods and services may be charged to the Joint Account as a component cost of the underlying goods and services and shall not be qualified as OTL, or as administrative costs covered under Overhead.

The Fee in question is not a direct cost of the Material; it is a fee paid separately to the vendor. According to MFI-38, direct material purchases "... should be charged to the joint account at the final price paid for the material." The SCM fee is not a cost of the material, nor is it a service associated with the material (such as coating, inspection or transportation). Therefore, it should be credited to the Joint Account. As discussed at COPAS meetings, chargeability cannot be outsourced. These costs of carry were not chargeable before and are not chargeable by virtue of being invoiced by a third party. Full credit remains due.

III.MATERIALS PRICING

## A. Direct Purchase Pricing

The operator generally is responsible for providing materials to be used by joint operations. The operator can provide these materials in several ways. The simplest way of providing materials, from an accounting standpoint, is vin a Direct Purchase. A Direet Purchase occurs when an agreement is created between the operator and a third party to provide materials for a specific project or a property. The operator can make a direet purehase of either new or used materials.

Direet Purehases should be charged to the joint aecount at the final price paid for the material. This is inclusive of all discounts received by the operator from the third party, as well as any costs for any special features or services associated with the material, such as coating, inspection and transportation. The operator should make a good faith effort to obtain the best possible value for the joint account. Refer to COPAS MFI-23, Díscownts, for specifie guidance on accounting for discounts and rebates.

The vendor is to invoice for goods/ products when they have been shipped offshore for installation or consumption and return and credit to the Joint Operation for any items not used/ consumed/installed.

This Sumitomo Supply Chain Management (SCM) fee is the Ancillary costs related to Sumitomo project management that is charged as part of the overall cost for provision of goods and services. With this SCM fee that has enable Joint operation to

mycm comply to UOA, Exhibit 'C' Section II Direct Charges, 4. Material, only such material shall be purchased for or transferred to the Joint Property as may be required for immediate use…. The accumulation of surplus stocks could be avoided.

Per the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement, Section 3 Billing Disputes Paragraph l, third-party project management costs by such third party associated with a third party's provision of goods and services may be charged to the Joint Account as a component cost of the underlying goods and services and shall not be qualified as OTL, or as administrative costs covered under Overhead.

The Fee in question is not a direct cost of the Material; it is a fee paid separately to the vendor. According to MFI-38, direct material purchases "... should be charged to the joint account at the final price paid for the material." The SCM fee is not a cost of the material, nor is it a service associated with the material (such as coating, inspection or transportation). Therefore, it should be credited to the Joint Account. As discussed at COPAS meetings, chargeability cannot be outsourced. These costs of carry were not chargeable before and are not chargeable by virtue of being invoiced by a third party. Full credit remains due.

III.MATERIALS PRICING

## A. Direct Purchase Pricing

The operator generally is responsible for providing materials to be used by joint operations. The operator can provide these materials in several ways. The simplest way of providing materials, from an accounting standpoint, is vin a Direct Purchase. A Direet Purchase occurs when an agreement is created between the operator and a third party to provide materials for a specific project or a property. The operator can make a direet purehase of either new or used materials.

Direet Purehases should be charged to the joint aecount at the final price paid for the material. This is inclusive of all discounts received by the operator from the third party, as well as any costs for any special features or services associated with the material, such as coating, inspection and transportation. The operator should make a good faith effort to obtain the best possible value for the joint account. Refer to COPAS MFI-23, Díscownts, for specifie guidance on accounting for discounts and rebates.
Based on the face-to-face meeting in February 2025 with SOI\_BP, both parties have agreed to escalate this issue to commercials of both companies.

To be escalated.

The letter agreement dated Feb. 13, 2019 governing Mars UOA, Accounting Rules and Offsite Technical Labor, Attachment 1, section 2, paragraph 2, states:

For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include procurement, administratic accounting and auditing, pipeline nominations and scheduling, human resources, manageme handling taxation matters, permitting/regulatory work, land and division order services. Overhe charges are compensation for all costs and expenses associated with such functions, including t salaries or wages plus applicable payroll burdens, benefits, and personal expenses of personı performing such functions, as well as their office and other support costs.

In response to IR 49, the Operator gave us a description of the Onshore Account Manager's role and responsibilities:

* Work safely and comply with Shell Life Saving Rules. Baker Hughes Life Rules, work ethically, follow procedures for all activities.

- Ensures that their team woks ethically, safely, and efficiently
- Responsible for Chemical Program Performance and delivery for their area of responsibility, track KPIs against plan to ensure efficient performance and identify risks/potential roadblocks
- Conduct monthly asset review of chemical program and KPI metrics with BHI field engineer and Shell chemical focal point
- Primary resource to Shell for production chemistry - technical focal point

HPHT corrosion, scale, asphaltene, and paraffin inhibitors)

- Coordinates collaboration between Shell and BHI SMEs
- Alignment of analytical testing protocols with Shell and Baker Hughes (flow assurance, asset integrity, production optimization)
- Responsible for writing case histories relevant to BHI and Shell joint ventures
- Assists in updating chemical program treating guides (CPTG)
- Responsible for coordinating waterflood healthchecks
- Responsible for coordi nating bacteria monitoring through bug bottles and/or new DNA techniques
- Assists Shell chemical focal point and BHI field engineer bridge any communication gaps between office and field
- Participates in Shell asset scorecard reviews
- Develops and submi ts action plan for yellow and/or red scorecard components to Shell chemical focal point and contract holder
- Acts as technical resource for shell chemical focal point and BHI field rep (research, development, problem solving, calculations)

- Attends assets specific operations meetings with or without the field engineer
- Participates in Close the Loop meetings
- Participates in Environmental Release Review (PW sheens, spills)
- Participates and provides data for incident review or root cause analysis
- Assists, reviews, and submits monthly analytical summary report (all analytical testing) to chemical focal point
- Ensure project/activity is in Shell Operations plans
- Responsible for efficient scheduling and conducting field service monitoring with chemical focal point
- Mentoring and training of field personnel
- Field site visits as required to support operations
- Liaise with Shell and Baker SMEs t o meet current and future technology innovation
- Responsible for continuous improvement on analytical procedures, equipment, and techniques as directed by Shell SMEs
- Participates and provides information on new Shell project developments.

From the above job description, it appears that the Account Manager performs a number of administrative and management functions such as KPI monitoring and reporting; new business development & continuous improvement; and various business liaising activities between Shell & Baker Petrolite (such as ensuring project is in Shell's Operations plans, bridging communication gaps, writing case histories relevant to Shell & Baker, etc). Since the Baker Petrolite account manager performs an administrative function, this role is not considered technical labor and should be part of overhead.

Please credit the Joint Account $129,813.03 plus 13% overhead.

from the working sheets attached to the SAP entries. The working sheets contain the monthly worksheet from January 2016 to current month and reflect the charges reduced year by year. The working sheets also illustrated the method of allocation. There are two layers of the allocation in this process. The first layer of the allocation is to split the overall cost of $35,063.33 among three areas; Permian, Argentina and GOM, it is allocated based on the total number of rigs used in each area for the month. Once the cost associated with GOM is obtained, the second layer of the allocation is to allocate the cost of GOM to assets in GOM based on the rig operating hours. The rig operating hours extracted from EDM Openwells is used as a basis for the second layer of the allocation. This exception is related to IR # 64.

The Joint Account was allocated charges from partner objects O.US.175.MAR.GEN.724FP and O.US.175.MAR.PLF.71300. Upon examination of the charges in these partner objects, it was noted several Stress Engineering and Worley/Jacobs Engineering invoices were for Offsite Technical Labor.

We compared the contractors noted on these invoices against the PoB and found only one instance where a contractor was onsite. This was for Joshua Plaisance on May 9-11, 2021 as related to Worley inv # 287064.

Stress Engineering inv 21030108 was for "evaluation of three valves" and Stress Engineering inv 21060205 was for "Crane Boom Weld Crack Analysis". None of the contractors were found on the PoB during the period that was billed.

According to Attachment 1, section 3 OTL Activities of the Letter Agreement dated Feb 14, 2019, OTL is only chargeable if they are for 1. Regulatory Activity, 2. Feasibility & Project Studies, and 3. Planners & Schedulers working on maintenance and turnaround activities.

In response to the IR, the Operator has noted that these contractors were planners and schedulers working on maintenance. The Operator cited the following work scope for the services rendered:

replies.text:
Reference is made to The Letter Agreement dated Feb 13, 2019 Attachment I. Agreed OTL Definition and Billing Standards.

## ATTACHMENT 1 AGREED OTL DEFINITION AND BILLING STANDARDS

## 1. Definition of Offsite Technical Labor ("OTL")

"OTL" shall mean actual costs incurred (including salaries and wages) for Technical Employees (as defined herein) and/or actual costs incurred for professional consultant services and contract services of technical personnel either temporarily or permanently assigned to and working for the principle benefit of the Joint Operations (as defined in the Mars UOA) but located 'offsite' or off of the Joint Property (as defined in Mars UOA), which are part of approved activities or activities conducted by the Operator which do not require vote or election (as defined in the Mars UOA).

## 2. Definition of"Technical Employees"

"Technical Employees" shall mean those employees, having special and specific engineering, geological, geophysical technical or operational skills (including planners, schedulers and execution support for facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities), and whose function in Joint Operations (as defined in the Mars UOA) is providing services for the benefit of the Joint Property (as defined in the Mars UOA).

For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include procurement, administration, accounting and auditing, pipeline nominations and scheduling, human resources, management, supervision (excluding first level supervision of operational staff which is billable), legal services, handling taxation matters, permitting/regulatory work, land and division order services. Overhead charges are compensation for all costs and expenses associated with such functions, including the salaries or wages plus applicable payroll burdens, benefits, and personal expenses of personnel performing such functions, as well as their office and other support costs.

## 3. OTL-Chargeable Activities

The Parties agree that OTLis chargeable for:

## 1. Regulatory Activity

OTL is chargeable by the Operator to the joint account for activities required to comply with any governmental agency, authority, commission, political subdivision, or any other governmental body or entity, including but not limited to the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE), and any applicable law or regulation, including but not limited to 30 CFR 250 Subpart S (as the mandatory practice following the voluntary API RP 75 which preceded it). Mandatory OTL, regulatory requirements for drilling, completion, and intervention activities will be chargeable by the Operator to the joint account as designated within the BSEE Certified Federal Register.

OTL charges related to the above regulatory activities must be adequately and properly documented by the Operator, identifying the specific activity of the individual(s), and will reference specific program elements as described in the Federal Register. Thiswill be noted in the Authority for Expenditure document where appropriate.

mycm

## 2.Feasibility and Project Studies

OTL associated with approved field improvement or facility improvement projects and for feasibility studies undertaken to progress future projects is chargeable by the Operator.

## 3. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration

OTL is chargeable by the Operator to the joint account for planners, schedulers, and plan execution supporters working on facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities.

The OTL activities of Worley/Jacobs and Stress Engineering are chargeable to the Joint Account in accordance with paragraph 2. Feasibility and Project Studies as referenced above. These studies are necessary to determine any potential maintenance activities to ensure the Joint Account is safe and reliable. As referenced in the Definition of OTL both parties agree the technical employee can be located 'offsite' or off the Joint Property while performing these services.

No credit is due the Joint Account for these chargeable OTL services.

The work in question was charged to generic Opex and therefore is not a feasibility study to progress a future project as required per the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement. Full credit remains due.

057.description:
For each month of 2021, the Operator has manually transferred pursuant to a journal entry $175,000 in boat charges from the drilling network attracting 2.5% overhead to an Operations charge code attracting 13%. The total amount for these marine Capex to Opex transfers was $2,118,747.07 gross. The net effect of these transfers is 10.5% (13% - 2.5%) representing the overhead difference, and the exception amount.

Effective January 1, 2020 and as shown in the Operator's Concurrent Operating Agreement, this was the Operator's policy to account for Ops worked performed by boats on Mars that didn't require a special boat run. The Operator is not able to provide proper support for the $175,000 transfer each month. Therefore, these transfers out of CAPEX and into OPEX are not proper entries and charges to the Joint Account.

Pursuant to COPAS Model Form Interpretation MFI-43, Auditors are expected to take exception with Joint Account transactions that, in their opinion, are not supported by adequate documentation. During 2021, in addition to these fixed unsupported Opex transfers totaling $2,118,747.07 gross, the Operator has booked $2,526,739.05 in boat charges directly to OPEX with boat logs provided as support.

Additionally, the Joint Account derives no benefit from the 10.5% increase in costs. The Operator already accounts for the logistics Capex/Opex split correctly by charging the voyages directly to the appropriate cost object. In this exception, the Operator chooses to re-classify a portion of the logistics cost solely to increase overhead recovery from the Non-Operator.

Therefore, in order to be consistent, provide proper support, and reduce the possibility of a duplicate charge in their booking of these Opex costs, credit is requested in the amount of $222,468.44 ($2,118,747,07 x .105).

The vessels which are drivers of the costs contemplated here are coding their time to projects, capital expenditures, and operational expenditures as they deem appropriate based on the nature of the work they are doing. As such, it is inappropriate to reclassify some of the charges, which the vessels had already correctly made. Full credit remains due as requested.

replies.text:
Credit denied.

The work in question did not take more than five consecutive workdays. The Unit Operating Agreement (UOA), Attachment I, Exhibit C, III Overhead, 1. Overhead - Drilling and Producing Operations, B. Overhead Percentage Basis, (2)Application Overhead, indicates " any remedial operations required a period of five (5) consecutive workdays or more on any or all wells." It does not stipulate any other detail as mentioned by the auditor.

However, the guideline for the five (5) consecutive work days or more has been described in UOA, Exhibit C, III Overhead, 1. Overhead - Drilling and Producing Operations, Paragraph A. Overhead - Fixed Rate Basis, (2) Application of Overhead - Fixed Rate Basis, (b) Charges for wells undergoing any type of workover or recompletion for a period of five (5) consecutive work days or more shall be made at the drilling well rate.

Such charges shall be applied for the period from date workover operations, with rig or other units used in workover, commence through date of rig or other unit release .... Accordingly, it does support Shell's practice of 5 days starts when the activity begins in the wellbore, 'on the well'.

mycm Additionally, per COPAS MFI-48 Application and Calculation of Drilling Overhead, the count of the five (5) consecutive work days or more for any remedial operations begins in the wellbore, 'on the well' Date workover operations, with rig commence and stop when rig released. Prepping activity, travel days and stand by time do not count as being 'on the well' and are excluded from the 5 consecutive workdays rule.

Therefore, it is incorrect to use dates of billing period from invoices of Marine service vessel, tool rental or rig as a basis to determine 5 consecutive workdays for this audit claim. Please refer to COPAS MFI-48 Application and Calculation of Drilling Overhead for further detail.

As an example, the Daily Operation Report (DOR) for P.US.MR2.Ws.20.007.7241A of WEST BOREAS WB001\_WIN\_DOR\_01122021 To 01192021 had shown that there were travel and preparation time from 112-2021 to 1-14-2021, the job was interrupted and stopped due to weather condition on 1-15-2021 and 1-162021. They had to wait on weather from 1-15-2021 to 1-16-2021 and wait on stim vessel again due to USCG halted the traffic. Therefore, the job did not exceed 5 consecutive workday and the OVHD rate for this job has been applied correctly.

The following Helix invoice snip-it shows the work in question lasted 7.25 work days to start. 7.25 is greater than the minimum 5 needed; therefore credit remains due. The other findings are all similar in nature and therefore full credit remains due for these incorrect OH charges.

068.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $11,287,952.67 for all affiliate labor cost in 2021 and $4,243,142.90 in 2020. On March 4, 2008 the Parties executed a Letter Agreement defining a fixed affiliate rate to cover affiliate charges to Major Construction Projects, and Integrated Project Teams. Additionally, the Statement of Clarification and Intent (SoCI) states that affiliate costs at the agreed rate charged to Major Construction and IPTs may not be audited and the Operator is not required to otherwise support the rates.

The costs questioned here are charged into projects other than Major Construction Projects and IPTs. These costs are not covered by the agreed rate language from the 2008 Letter Agreement or SoCI, and are therefore subject to Audit, or to other documentation that the rates charged into the Joint Account are at cost, such as a Cost Certificate which is signed and attested by the Operator's Statutory Auditors.

The Operator was requested to provide a Cost Certificate for 2020 and 2021 in Information Request 008 which was issued during the fieldwork. In conversation regarding this IR, the Operator stated that the Cost Certificate for 2021 cost would not be available until 2023. The Operator then stated that the 2020 Cost Certificate was available, although it was not provided to the Auditors during or after the fieldwork.

The Non-Operator is therefore taking exception to $10,490,676.92 of 2021 affiliate costs, and $3,774,640.15 of 2020 affiliate cost as noted in the attached JADE lines pending the Operator providing the requested cost certificates.

replies.text: This exception is under review. A response will be provided once the review is completed.

The Operator charged the Joint Account $418,245.05 on various Sumitomo Corporation Of Americas invoices for SCM Fee Consignment charges. This is a management fee and is not a direct cost of the material but an additional fee to house the material and ensure it is available when needed.

Exhibit 'C' Section III Overhead of the Unit Operating Agreement states: "As compensation for administrative, supervision, office services and warehousing costs, Operator shall charge the Joint Account in accordance with this Section III.'

Additionally, AG 19, Section IV.3.C states 'Actual costs may include costs of (I) Material, (2) making it suitable for use, and (3) transportation from the point of acquisition to the Joint Property including loading and unloading. Not included are storage or carrying costs." This was the subject of Information Request 009 which was raised during the audit field work.

The Operator is requested to reimburse joint account for$418,245.05 plus overhead of 2.5%.

replies.text:
Credit Denied. Per BP-SOI Settlement Agreement, dated December 2018, Section 3 Billing Disputes Paragraph l. Third-Party Project Management - Ancillary costs related to third party project management that are charged as part of the overall cost for provision of goods and services by such third party associated with a third party's provision of goods and services may be charged to the Joint Account as a component cost of the underlying goods and services and shall not be qualified as OTL or as administrative costs covered under Overhead. Sumitomo SCM fee is a component cost of the underlying goods and services, and it does not qualify as OTL or administrative costs covered under Overhead.

replies.text:
The Fee in question is not a direct cost of the Material; it is a fee paid separately to the vendor. According to MFI-38, direct material purchases "...should be charged to the joint account at the final price paid for the material." The SCM fee is not a cost of the material, nor is it a service associated with the material (such as coating, inspection or transportation). Therefore, it should be credited to the Joint Account. As discussed at COPAS meetings, chargeability cannot be outsourced. These costs of carry were not chargeable before and are not chargeable by virtue of being invoiced by a third party. Full credit remains due.

## III. MATERIALS PRICING

## A. Direct Purchase Pricing

The operator generally is responsible for providing materials to be used by joint operations. The operator can provide these materials in several ways. The simplest way of providing materials, from an accounting standpoint, is via a Direct Purchase. A Direct Purchase occurs when an agreement is created between the operator and a third party to provide materials for a specific project or a property. The operator can make a direct purchase of either new or used materials.

Direct Purchases should be charged to the joint account at the final price paid for the material. This is inclusive of all discounts received by the operator from the third party, as well as any costs for any special features or services associated with the material, such as coating, inspection and transportation. The operator should make a good faith effort to obtain the best possible value for the joint account. Refer to COPAS MFI-23, Discounts, for specific guidance on accounting for discounts and rebates.

The amortization for 2017 and 2018 had been charged to Non Billable cost elements but amortization for 2019 and 2020 was charged to the Joint Account.

During fieldwork, the auditors raised the issue of this expense being charged to the Joint Account outside of the allowed 24-month period, as stated in Section I, 4 of Exhibit C of the JOA :

During September 2021 business, the Joint Account was charged $176,467.32 for the license fee amortization for years 2019 and 2020 as provided in response to Information Request 27. See excel file DDR from 2017.xlsx. The amortization of these charges are within the 24 month period. Credit Denied.

It is the industry practice to amortize software license fees over multiple accounting periods (years).

The Engenuity Software license fees are amortized from 2017 to 2020 for four years. Because of the 24-month rule, the amortization of Engenuity software license fee for the year 2017 and 2018 are not billable to the Joint Account. 03.description:
This exception is related to IR 22.

The Joint Account was charged $421,210.94 via 2 invoices for upgrades/updates to the NGT1 per attached JADE. These charges appear to be costs that will benefit future wells serviced by NGT1 and should be included in the accumulator.

Invoice 90020325A for $43,260.66 consists of charges for electrical work to install motion sensor light switches in all accommodation rooms to reduce power usage and for OPC tags for rig data coming into Well Vantage.

Invoice 90020569A for $377,950.28 consists of charges for an "Upgraded Door Assembly". It was a regulatory requirement to upgrade the blind shear rams to LFS5 rams and was a part of the BOP upgrade.

The Operator agrees that the Upgraded Door Assembly costs should be included in the accumulator and has granted this credit during fieldwork. The correcting entries to move the charge to NGT1 LFS 5 BOP upgrade accumulator has already been made in June 2022 per the attached file.

The auditor believes that the Motion Sensors and OPC tags are also expenses which should be included in the accumulator because these will benefit future wells serviced by NGT1. Please credit the Joint account $43,260.66 plus 13% overhead.

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

The remaining balance of $43,260.25 for the motion light switches work is not a part of any other already established accumulator and does not fit the definition per MFI 56 as a major maintenance expense. This is considered a minor maintenance job. No credit is due to the Joint Account.

The invoice numbered 90020325A, issued by Noble Drilling, comprises the following components:

1. Labor Cost: Amounting to $29,992.00, this covers the payment for two electricians, their travel expenses, quarantine days, and mileage. These services were provided by vendor Gonzales Electric.
2. Software Engineer's Cost: Totaling $7,052.00, this expense pertains to GT1 OPC missing tag research and was incurred from vendor HUISMAN.
3. Material Cost: The materials procured from Gonzales Electric include:
- 130 pieces of #TS 0S5-W2P-UF sensors at $33.94 each.
- 130 pieces of Surface Mount Boxes at $4.30 each.
- 130 pieces of face plates at $0.60 each.
- 300 pieces of close end connectors at $0.35 each.
- 150 pieces of BUTT at $0.46 each.
- 150 pieces of BUTT connectors at $0.41 each.
- 300 Wago Lever Nuts at $0.47 each.

Materials, such as sensors, mount boxes, face plates, and connectors, are not considered as capitalized assets. The installation and replacement of these materials is a small maintenance job.

replies.text:
Per MFI-56, "costs for repairs not caused by operations on a specific property are part of the overall compensation due the drilling contractor and are directly chargeable to all wells using the repaired equipment over the remaining life of the Rig Contract". This specific scenario is part of why the Operator has established the accumulator account and bill-out process.

The light switch/system was not damaged/replaced as the result of any particular well operation and benefits all wells. Therefore it is appropriate to include in the accumulator as originally requested. The balance of requested credit remains due.

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

Per SOI-BP Settlement, dated December 19, 2018 Agreement, Section 3, f. Preservation & Maintenance Facilities - BP may charge to the Joint Account as a direct charge the facility and labor costs for BP's Preservation and Maintenance Shorebase Facility per [Direct Paragraph 7 in the Accounting Procedure.] For avoidance of doubt, the BP PMF was also accepted as a Shorebase Facility with associated labor agreed to be billable to the Joint Account. In the event Shell constructs, acquires, develops, and/or operates a similar facility, Shell may charge to the Joint Account as a direct charge the facility and labor costs for such facility and such facility shall be accepted as a Shorebase Facility with associated labor to be billable to the Joint Account. Shell's GOM DC is considered the same as BP's PMF and is billable to the Joint Account.

Additionally, per MFI -46 Shorebase Facilities and Offshore Staging Areas, IV Costs Included in Shorebase Operations, 2nd paragraph, the Operator should recover cost of investment through a "rate to recover cost of ownership" charge which may be the same as the "Equipment and Facilities furnished by Operator" provision in the Accounting Procedure. For this purpose, all investments should be taken into account, including land, parking lots, etc. It may include construction overhead and on/off

业

site technical labor according to the provisions of the Accounting Procedures in effect covering the operations served. The "rate to recover cost of ownership should consist of 1) Amortization, 2) Interest, 3. Insurance, 4. Tax.

The charges in question represent recovery of the cost of investment of newly constructed buildings, facilities for areas of Climate Floor (4,000 Sq Ft), Climate Rack (6,000 Sq Ft), Floor (21,000 Sq Ft), Rack (25,000 Sq Ft), Bin (4,000 Sq Ft), Receive Stage (1,500 Sq Ft), Lay Down (27 acres), and Access to Intracoastal Waterway. The amount charged is calculated based on the square footage occupied by the Joint Properties multiplied by the market rental rate less 20% which is in accordance with the Mars UOA Section 7.B. The document explaining the nature of this charge and its methodology was provided to the auditor during the field audit.

The analysis of the benchmark market rate was also provided to the auditor during the field audit. The analysis of the market vs. Operator's billing rate (GOM DC) is shown

[table 3]

below.

[table 4]

While comparing rates used by GOM DC against vendors' rates, it shows the rate used by GOM DC is fairly close or way below the rate of market rate less 20%. To maintain a conservative approach, there is no plan on adjusting GOM DC rates at this time. Therefore, no adjustment will be made to the Joint Account

Credit Denied.

Stress Engineering Services Inc. provided PRT (Production Rise Tensioner) calculations. The production riser tensioner is a device used to maintain the tension in a production riser to prevent excessive bending, vibration, and fatigue during operation. This ensures the riser remains stable and allows for efficient and safe production operations. Overall, the production riser tensioner plays a crucial role in ensuring the integrity and reliability of the production riser, allowing for safe and efficient oil and gas production in offshore environments. 30 CFR 250.1165 and 250.1916. Per Feb. 2019 Letter agreement, 3.1 Regulatory activities, the costs of contract services of Stress Engineering Services Inc. are directly chargeable to the Joint Account.

## Description:

This exception is related to IR 49.

The Joint Account was charged costs from partner object O.US.175.MAR.GEN.71300.

Upon examination of costs within this partner object, we noted that there was a total of $129,813.03 in monthly charges for an onshore account manager from Baker Petrolite. (see 2nd tab of attached "JADE --IR 49" file.)

The letter agreement dated Feb. 13, 2019 governing Mars UOA, Accounting Rules and Offsite Technical Labor, Attachment 1, section 2, paragraph 2, states:

For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include procurement, administration, accounting and auditing, pipeline nominations and scheduling, human resources, management, supervision (excluding first level supervision of operational staff which is billable), egal services, handling taxation matters, permitting/regulatory work, land and division order services. Overhead charges are compensation for all costs and expenses associated with such functions, including the salaries or wages plus applicable payroll burdens, benefits, and personal expenses of personnel performing such functions, as well as their office and other support costs.

In response to IR 49, the Operator gave us a description of the Onshore Account Manager's role and responsibilities:

* Work safely and comply with Shell Life Saving Rules. Baker Hughes Life Rules, work ethically, follow procedures for all activities.
- Ensures that their team woks ethically, safely, and efficiently
- Responsible for Chemical Program Performance and delivery for their area of responsibility, track KPIs against plan to ensu re efficient performance and identify risks/potential roadblocks
- Conduct monthly asset review of chemical program and KPI metrics with BHI field engineer and Shell chemical focal point
- Primary resource to Shell for production chemistry - technical focal point
- Proactively participate in regular formal reviews with key Shell stakeholders
- Interact with Engineering and Field Operations for troubleshooting and provide technical support
- Delivery of key technical projects and value propositions (business improvement/risk reduction). Prepare scope of work/ TORs for projects agreed and in asset work phase
- Communicates daily with chemical focal points to update action items and KPI discussions
- Provides Research on new products and/or technology at Shell's request
- Provides Lunch and Learns on new product and/or technology for Shell Chemical Team
- Applies new technology (products and/or services) to existing assets through plant trials

业

- Attempts to sponsor new product development based on Shell's technological needs (ex. New AI, combination products, HPHT corrosion, scale, asphaltene, and paraffin inhibitors)
- Coordinates collaboration between Shell and BHI SMEs
- Alignment of analytical testing protocols with Shell and Baker Hughes (flow assurance, asset integrity, production optimization)
- Responsible for writing case histories relevant to BHI and Shell joint ventures
- Assists in updating chemical program treating guides (CPTG)
- Re sponsible for coordinating waterflood health checks
- Responsible for coordinating bacteria monitoring through bug bottles and/or new DNA techniques
- Assists Shell chemical focal point and BHI field engineer bridge any communication gaps between office and field
- Participates in Shell asset scorecard reviews
- Develops and submits action plan for yellow and/or red scorecard components to Shell chemical focal point and contract holder
- Acts as technical resource for shell chemical focal point and BHI fiel d rep (research, development, problem solving, calculations)
- Responsible for new product screening on all assets (better performers and/or more economical performers)
- Attends assets specific operations meetings with or without the field engineer
- Participates in Close the Loop meetings
- Participates in Environmental Release Review (PW sheens, spills)
- Participates and provides data for incident review or root cause analysis
- Assists, reviews, and submits monthly analytical summary report (all analyt ical testing) to chemical focal point
- Ensure project/activity is in Shell Operations plans
- Responsible for efficient scheduling and conducting field service monitoring with chemical focal point
- Mentoring and training of field personnel
- Field site visits as required to support operations
- Liaise with Shell and Baker SMEs to meet current and future technology innovation
- Responsible for continuous improvement on analytical procedures, equipment, and techniques as directed by Shell SMEs
- Participate s and provides information on new Shell project developments.

From the above job description, it appears that the Account Manager performs a number of administrative and management functions such as KPI monitoring and reporting; new business development & continuous improvement; and various business liaising activities between Shell & Baker Petrolite (such as ensuring project is in Shell's Operations plans, bridging communication gaps, writing case histories relevant to Shell & Baker, etc). Since the Baker Petrolite account manager performs an administrative function, this role is not considered technical labor and should be part of overhead.

Please credit the Joint Account $129,813.03 plus 13% overhead.

06.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $196,221.98 for Houma Distribution Center costs according to the attached JADE lines. These were the subject of Information Request 30 where the Operator explained that these costs were charged in accordance with the Mars UOA Section 7.B. which allows the Operator to charge company owned facilities and equipment at market rate less 20%.

The Operator did not provide sufficient analysis of the market. These costs are therefore not chargeable in accordance with Section 7.B. of the Mars UOA and should be credited to the Joint Account.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $196,221.98 including overhead for these costs.

Note: This Exception 6 is taken in parallel with Exception 7 which charges for the cost of Ownership and Operation in accordance with 7.A. of the Mars UOA. Either method is acceptable under the UOA, however not both. Therefore exception to both methods is taken until such time as the Operator determines which method they have chosen.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $605,461.57 plus 2.5% Overhead for costs not chargeable under Section 7.B of the Mars UOA.

Note: This Exception 7 is taken in parallel with Exception 6. According to the Mars UOA, Either the 7.A. or 7.B. method is acceptable, however not both. Exception is taken here until such time as the Operator determines which method they have chosen.

This change will be implemented immediately, and any adjustment will be made retroactively in June 2024. The auditors from co-owner could review this change and impact during 2025 Mars field audit.

08.description:
This exception consists of 5 coding errors which have been identified by the auditors as recurring issues during Mars audits.

1. The Joint Account was allocated costs from partner object O.US.175.MAR.GEN.71300. See JADE lines on combined spreadsheet. Upon examination of costs charged to this partner object, it was noted that Offshore Chemist, Jeremy Chenier, was erroneously charged to this WBS in Sept, 2021 even when the POB shows that he was in Perdido and Salsa during Sept, 2021. In response to IR 48, the Operator acknowledges that Mr. Chenier was not at Mars during Sept, 2021 because Mars was shut-in as a result of Hurricane Ida. Furthermore, the Operator provided email evidence from Baker Hughes that confirms Mr. Chenier was at Enchilada providing "coupon training" to the Baker rep at that site. Given the confirmed facts that Mr. Cheniere's services did not benefit Mars in September, 2021, please credit the Joint Account $30,654.17 ($27,127.58 plus 13% overhead of $3,526.59).
2. R360 ES Holdings invoice no. U579138 dated July 27, 2021 totaling $16,027.00 charged the Joint Account to dispose of oil base drilling waste. The original invoice and work ticket indicate that the AC815 Silvertip project should have been charged Please credit the Joint Account $16,427.68 ($16,027.00 plus 2.5% overhead of $400.68).
3. Donovan Controls invoice no. 137808 dated November 5, 2021 totaling $25,225.20 charged the Joint Account for work on a new flow computer. The original invoice and work ticket indicate that MC 809 Ursa project should have been charged. Please credit the Joint Account $28,504.48 ($25,225.20 plus 13% overhead of $3,279.28).
4. PSC Industrial invoice LPF2100711 dated 8/2/2021 totaling $10,320.00 charged the Joint Account for tank and container cleaning for the Deepwater Proteus. This was drill rig was not used on the Joint Account and therefore this invoice should be charged to that project. Please credit the Joint Account $10,577.96 ($10,320.00 plus 2.5% OH).
5. The following exception is related to IR #38 : The Joint Account was charged $32,926.00 for M&T

业

Additional billing via doc # 130282628. The documentation attached to the SAP entry does not show that any of the M&T billing should go to Mars.

On 8/8/2022, the Operator replied by email that credit had been issued for IR #38 on SAP Doc 131082007 for $32,926.00. This coding error item is therefore considered closed and for informational purposes only.

The Operator was requested to provide a final Bill of Materials and Reconciliation for this well in IR-003 submitted during the fieldwork.

The Operator was unable to provide a final Bill of Materials and Reconciliation and was not otherwise able to substantiate that the materials in question were used in joint operations.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $3,759,934.79 plus 2.5% OH or provide documentation to substantiate the usage of materials in the Joint Operations.

replies.text:
Credit Denied. The charges in question are for Mars BOP Regulatory Compliance project (WBS: C.US.MAR.PD.19.005.0942A). Please see AFE in the attached file for details. Project Justification / Description of Work Performed references 30 CFR 250.733 paragraph (1) surface BOP stacks must have blind shear rams capable of shearing at any point along the tubular body of any drill pipe (excluding tool joints, bottom-hole tools, and bottom hole assemblies that include heavy-weight pipe or collars) workstring, tubing and associated exterior control lines, and any electric-, wire-, and slick-line that is in the hole and sealing the wellbore after shearing by April 29, 2021.

Mars currently has a NOV 203/4' 3K and a Cameron 13 5/8' 10K BOP stacks with blind shear rams that do not meet the regulatory shearing requirements for wireline operations.

The charges in question contain cost for material, spare parts, service, testing and milestone payments to ensure the BOP meets regulatory compliance. No BOM or reconciliations are to be provided for these types of material and services. Please refer to DOR (Daily Operation report) for the BOP activities.

In accordance with Exhibit C - Accounting Procedure Offshore Joint Operations, Section IV of the Mars UOA Accounting Procedure states that:

'The Operator is responsible for Joint Account Material and shall make proper and timely charges and credits for all material movements affecting the Joint Property.'

Additionally, under Section V - Inventories, Subsection 2 - Reconciliation and Adjustment of Inventories, the Lake Cleanup Project was initiated. This initiative aimed to reconcile and disposition physical inventory across completed projects as of

August 2019.

In accordance with Exhibit C - Accounting Procedure Offshore Joint Operations, Section IV of the Mars UOA Accounting Procedure states that:

'The Operator is responsible for Joint Account Material and shall make proper and timely charges and credits for all material movements affecting the Joint Property.'

Additionally, under Section V - Inventories, Subsection 2 - Reconciliation and Adjustment of Inventories, the Lake Cleanup Project was initiated. This initiative aimed to reconcile and disposition physical inventory across completed projects as of August 2019.

To align financial records with physical inventory, all VPS inventory was issued out and reloaded based on the vendor's recor ds of ownership and valuation. Following this process, the remaining inventory was transferred to Investment Recovery.

After the face-to-face meeting between SOI and BP in February 2025, a review of the nonoperator's latest reconciliation of Multi Jade was conducted. Based on this review, no credit to the Joint Account is warranted, as the charges in question are directly related to the Lake Cleanup Project and its objective of aligning financial and physical inventory records.

replies.text:
The credit claim totaling of $282,411.54 has been denied.

The Non-Operator acknowledged the ability to trace the IT & COMM SV, WELLVANTAGE ROC SUPPORT charges in question from the working sheets attached to the SAP entries.

The working sheets contain the monthly worksheet from January 2016 to current month and reflect the charges reduced year by year. The working sheets also illustrated the method of allocation. There are two layers of the allocation in this process. The first layer of the allocation is to split the overall cost of $35,063.33 among three areas; Permian, Argentina and GOM, it is allocated based on the total number of rigs used in each area for the month. Once the cost associated with GOM is obtained, the second layer of the allocation is to allocate the cost of GOM to assets in GOM based on the rig operating hours. The rig operating hours extracted from EDM Openwells is used as a basis for the second layer of the allocation.

As indicated earlier, the IT & COMM SV, WELLVANTAGE ROC SUPPORT is pertinent to the operation of the Joint Account and

业

the charges of the supporting cost are reduced from year to year. Since the Non-Operator reviewed the IT & COMM SV, WELLVANTAGE ROC SUPPORT charges each year since 2017 and has not raised an audit exception in this area until now, it is an indication that the Non-Operator has found no concerns in this area in its audits of prior years. It is inappropriate to make a claim simply for not having copy of the 3rd party invoice.

The Non-Operator applied the Operating Overhead of 13%. This is incorrect as 24 WBS codes are at the Development Overhead rate of 2.5% and 5 WBS codes are at the Operating Overhead rate of 13%. See the below schedule. The correct overhead amount is $7,505.15 and not $32,489.82 calculated by the Non-Operator. No credit is due to the Joint Account.

## Description:

This exception relates to IR #70.

The Joint Account was charged $270,787.63 for Material # 1002309332 (CSG,14.000,115.00,TN125HC,TSHBLU+,R3,BBE). The auditors examined the BoM provided by the Operator for C.US.MAR.PD.18.003.0942A and noted that while there had been transfers-in and out in the WBS element for this material, there were no installations of this material to the project.

During fieldwork, the Operator explained that the charge was due to the change in value of the material as a result of the change in its condition. The Operator also noted that the material was transferred from C.US.MAR.PD.14.002.0942A to C.US.MAR.PD.18.001.0942A and then to the current WBS.

The material was never installed or used in the Joint Property. Since the Joint Property never benefitted from the use of this material, it should not be charged for the change in value/condition of the material.

Please credit the joint account for $270,787.63 plus 2.5% overhead for charges related to material not used in the joint property.

replies.text:
The credit claim totaling of $282,411.54 has been denied.

The Non-Operator acknowledged the ability to trace the IT & COMM SV, WELLVANTAGE ROC SUPPORT charges in question from the working sheets attached to the SAP entries.

The working sheets contain the monthly worksheet from January 2016 to current month and reflect the charges reduced year by year. The working sheets also illustrated the method of allocation. There are two layers of the allocation in this process. The first layer of the allocation is to split the overall cost of $35,063.33 among three areas; Permian, Argentina and GOM, it is allocated based on the total number of rigs used in each area for the month. Once the cost associated with GOM is obtained, the second layer of the allocation is to allocate the cost of GOM to assets in GOM based on the rig operating hours. The rig operating hours extracted from EDM Openwells is used as a basis for the second layer of the allocation.

业

As indicated earlier, the IT & COMM SV, WELLVANTAGE ROC SUPPORT is pertinent to the operation of the Joint Account and the charges of the supporting cost are reduced from year to year. Since the Non-Operator reviewed the IT & COMM SV, WELLVANTAGE ROC SUPPORT charges each year since 2017 and has not raised an audit exception in this area until now, it is an indication that the Non-Operator has found no concerns in this area in its audits of prior years. It is inappropriate to make a claim simply for not having copy of the 3rd party invoice.

The Non-Operator applied the Operating Overhead of 13%. This is incorrect as 24 WBS codes are at the Development Overhead rate of 2.5% and 5 WBS codes are at the Operating Overhead rate of 13%. See the below schedule. The correct overhead amount is $7,505.15 and not $32,489.82 calculated by the Non-Operator. No credit is due to the Joint Account.

[table 1]

46.description:
This exception relates to IR #70.

The Joint Account was charged $270,787.63 for Material # 1002309332

(CSG,14.000,115.00,TN125HC,TSHBLU+,R3,BBE). The auditors examined the BoM provided by the Operator for C.US.MAR.PD.18.003.0942A and noted that while there had been transfers-in and out in the WBS element for this material, there were no installations of this material to the project.

During fieldwork, the Operator explained that the charge was due to the change in value of the material as a result of the change in its condition. The Operator also noted that the material was transferred from C.US.MAR.PD.14.002.0942A to C.US.MAR.PD.18.001.0942A and then to the current WBS.

The material was never installed or used in the Joint Property. Since the Joint Property never benefitted from the use of this material, it should not be charged for the change in value/condition of the material.

Please credit the joint account for $270,787.63 plus 2.5% overhead for charges related to material not used in the joint property.
