Reference is made to The Letter Agreement dated Feb 13, 2019 Attachment I. Agreed OTL Definition and Billing Standards.

业

## ATTACHMENT 1 AGREED OTL DEFINITION AND BILLING STANDARDS

## 1. Definition of Offsite Technical Labor ("OTL")

"OTL" shall mean actual costs incurred (including salaries and wages) for Technical Employees (as defined herein) and/or actual costs incurred for professional consultant services and contract services of technical personnel either temporarily or permanently assigned to and working for the principle benefit of the Joint Operations (as defined in the Mars UOA) but located 'offsite' or off of the Joint Property (as defined in Mars UOA), which are part of approved activities or activities conducted by the Operator which do not require vote or election (as defined in the Mars UOA).

## 2. Definition of "Technical Employees"

"Technical Employees" shall mean those employees, having special and specific engineering, geological, geophysical technical or operational skills (including planners, schedulers and execution support for facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities), and whose function in Joint Operations (as defined in the Mars UOA) is providing services for the benefit of the Joint Property (as defined in the Mars UOA).

For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include procurement, administration, accounting and auditing, pipeline nominations and scheduling, human resources, management, supervision (excluding first level supervision of operational staff which is billable), legal services, handling taxation matters, permitting/regulatory work, land and division order services. Overhead charges are compensation for all costs and expenses associated with such functions, including the salaries or wages plus applicable payroll burdens, benefits, and personal expenses of personnel performing such functions, as well as their office and other support costs.

## 3. OTL-Chargeable Activities

The Parties agree that OTL is chargeable for:

## 1. Regulatory Activity

OTL is chargeable by the Operator to the joint account for activities required to comply with any governmental agency, authority, commission, political subdivision, or any other governmental body or entity, including but not limited to the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE), and any applicable law or regulation, including but not limited to 30 CFR 250 Subpart S (as the mandatory practice following the voluntary API RP 75 which preceded it). Mandatory OTL, regulatory requirements for drilling, completion, and intervention activities will be chargeable by the Operator to the joint account as designated within the BSEE Certified Federal Register.

OTL charges related to the above regulatory activities must be adequately and properly documented by the Operator, identifying the specific activity of the individual(s), and will reference specific program elements as described in the Federal Register. This will be noted in the Authority for Expenditure document where appropriate.

业

## 2.Feasibility and Project Studies

OTL associated with approved field improvement or facility improvement projects and for feasibility studies undertaken to progress future projects is chargeable by the Operator.

## 3. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration

OTL is chargeable by the Operator to the joint account for planners, schedulers, and plan execution supporters working on facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities.

The OTL activities of Worley/Jacobs and Stress Engineering are chargeable to the Joint Account in accordance with paragraph 2. Feasibility and Project Studies as referenced above. These studies are necessary to determine any potential maintenance activities to ensure the Joint Account is safe and reliable. As referenced in the Definition of OTL both parties agree the technical employee can be located 'offsite' or off the Joint Property while performing these services.

No credit is due the Joint Account for these chargeable OTL services.

## Description:

This exception is related to IR # 64.

The Joint Account was allocated charges from partner objects O.US.175.MAR.GEN.724FP and O.US.175.MAR.PLF.71300. Upon examination of the charges in these partner objects, it was noted several Stress Engineering and Worley/Jacobs Engineering invoices were for Offsite Technical Labor.

The Worley/Jacobs invoices are for engineering services related to "Mars--Weight Mitigation". We compared the contractors noted on these invoices against the PoB and found only one instance where a contractor was onsite. This was for Joshua Plaisance on May 9-11, 2021 as related to Worley inv # 287064.

Stress Engineering inv 21030108 was for "evaluation of three valves" and Stress Engineering inv 21060205 was for "Crane Boom Weld Crack Analysis". None of the contractors were found on the PoB during the period that was billed.

According to Attachment 1, section 3 OTL Activities of the Letter Agreement dated Feb 14, 2019, OTL is only chargeable if they are for 1. Regulatory Activity, 2. Feasibility & Project Studies, and 3. Planners & Schedulers working on maintenance and turnaround activities.

In response to the IR, the Operator has noted that these contractors were planners and schedulers working on maintenance. The Operator cited the following work scope for the services rendered:

Mars CRN1 Boom Weld Crack Analysis

- -perform metallurgical failure analysis of weld cracks on CRN1 Boom Gusset Plates.
- -Visual examination & photographic documentation of welds
- -Wet fluorescent magnetic particle examination of welds
- -break open a representative weld crack
- -Crack surface examination by stereomicroscopy & scanning electrons microscopy (SEM) analysis
- -Energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analysis
- -Metallography of weld with & without cracks
- -Hardness tests
- -Chemical analysis by optical emission spectroscopy
- -provide final Report

Weight mitigation study includes the following tasks:

- Facilitate weight mitigation workshops with key stakeholders.
- Determine a good as -is weight status of the platform, while outlining operating limits.

业

- Determine expected weight status of the platform for operations as well as planned and future projects (future identified projects).
- Develop a list of opportunities for weight mitigation including associated costs, shut -in impacts and overall feasibility/complexity.
- Establish different levels of weight mitigation ranges/opportunities.
- Evaluate how these weight mitigation levels may impact various operating scenarios or types of projects that may be desired in the future (Stability Analyses).

The work descriptions provided by the Operator are not planning and scheduling in nature and therefore, the work is not chargeable under Attachment 1, section 3, OTL Activities, of the Letter Agreement dated Feb 14, 2019. Please credit the Joint Account $87,556.04 plus 13% overhead.

The reclassification charges are for overtime charges incurred in April, May and June 2021 derived from the cost centers CC 101013 U1-Mars Ops Home Oper and CC 329782 Olympus Ops Hourly CC, respectively. The overtime charges were then transferred from these two cost centers to Internal order no. 61250544 and 61250642 in order to reclassify these overtime charges under COVID 19 Abnormal Operation. The reclassification entries shown below are posted in June 2021 and include overtime charges of April, May, and June partially Therefore, the overtime charges in question are billed as COVID 19 Abnormal Operations with no financial impact. ## Description:

For each month of 2021, the Operator has manually transferred pursuant to a journal entry $175,000 in boat charges from the drilling network attracting 2.5% overhead to an Operations charge code attracting 13%. The total amount for these marine Capex to Opex transfers was $2,118,747.07 gross. The net effect of these transfers is 10.5% (13% - 2.5%) representing the overhead difference, and the exception amount.

Effective January 1, 2020 and as shown in the Operator's Concurrent Operating Agreement, this was the Operator's policy to account for Ops worked performed by boats on Mars that didn't require a special boat run. The Operator is not able to provide proper support for the $175,000 transfer each month. Therefore, these transfers out of CAPEX and into OPEX are not proper entries and charges to the Joint Account.

Pursuant to COPAS Model Form Interpretation MFI-43, Auditors are expected to take exception with Joint Account transactions that, in their opinion, are not supported by adequate documentation. During 2021, in addition to these fixed unsupported Opex transfers totaling $2,118,747.07 gross, the Operator has booked $2,526,739.05 in boat charges directly to OPEX with boat logs provided as support.

Additionally, the Joint Account derives no benefit from the 10.5% increase in costs. The Operator already accounts for the logistics Capex/Opex split correctly by charging the voyages directly to the appropriate cost object. In this exception, the Operator chooses to re-classify a portion of the logistics cost solely to increase overhead recovery from the Non-Operator.

Therefore, in order to be consistent, provide proper support, and reduce the possibility of a duplicate charge in their booking of these Opex costs, credit is requested in the amount of $222,468.44 ($2,118,747,07 x .105).

Credit denied.

The work in question did not take more than five consecutive workdays. The Unit Operating Agreement (UOA), Attachment I, Exhibit C, III Overhead, 1. Overhead - Drilling and Producing Operations, B. Overhead Percentage Basis, (2)Application Overhead, indicates " any remedial operations required a period of five (5)

业

consecutive workdays or more on any or all wells." It does not stipulate any other detail as mentioned by the auditor.

However, the guideline for the five (5) consecutive work days or more has been described in UOA, Exhibit C, III Overhead, 1. Overhead - Drilling and Producing Operations, Paragraph A. Overhead - Fixed Rate Basis, (2) Application of Overhead - Fixed Rate Basis, (b) Charges for wells undergoing any type of workover or recompletion for a period of five (5) consecutive work days or more shall be made at the drilling well rate. Such charges shall be applied for the period from date workover operations, with rig or other units used in workover, commence through date of rig or other unit release .... Accordingly, it does support Shell's practice of 5 days starts when the activity begins in the wellbore, 'on the well'.

Additionally, per COPAS MFI-48 Application and Calculation of Drilling Overhead, the count of the five (5) consecutive work days or more for any remedial operations begins in the wellbore, 'on the well' Date workover operations, with rig commence and stop when rig released. Prepping activity, travel days and stand by time do not count as being 'on the well' and are excluded from the 5 consecutive workdays rule.

Therefore, it is incorrect to use dates of billing period from invoices of Marine service vessel, tool rental or rig as a basis to determine 5 consecutive workdays for this audit claim. Please refer to COPAS MFI-48 Application and Calculation of Drilling Overhead for further detail.

As an example, the Daily Operation Report (DOR) for P.US.MR2.Ws.20.007.7241A of WEST BOREAS WB001\_WIN\_DOR\_01122021 To 01192021 had shown that there were travel and preparation time from 112-2021 to 1-14-2021, the job was interrupted and stopped due to weather condition on 1-15-2021 and 1-162021. They had to wait on weather from 1-15-2021 to 1-16-2021 and wait on stim vessel again due to USCG halted the traffic. Therefore, the job did not exceed 5 consecutive workday and the OVHD rate for this job has been applied correctly.

This exception is related to IR #28.

The Joint Account was charged $6,574,022.40 in Accumulator costs for Pontus for August-Dec, 2021. Costs in the accumulator were amortized from start date of 10/22/2017 to 10/22/2022, a total of 1827 days. However, per section 1.2 of the 2019 Settlement Agreement, the amortization period for Transocean rig Pontus should be 10/21/2017 to 12/31/2023, a period of 2263 days.

- 1.2 "Amortization Period" shall mean the period of time commencing on the first day of the SOl Rig Contract for each of the respective Transocean Rigs as specified in this Section 1.2 and continuing through the end of December 31, 2023. The first day of the SOl Rig Contract for the each of the Transocean Rigs is as follows: (i) Transocean Thalassa – February 6, 2016, (ii) Transocean Proteus - May 5, 2016, (iii) Transocean Pontus - October 21, 2017, and (iv) Transocean Poseidon - February 12,2018.

The attached file called "Exc 60 JADE lines and analysis" shows the difference between the accumulator costs as charged per JADE vs the recalculated accumulator costs using the correct amortization period. The recalculation of accumulator charges based on the agreed upon amortization period is shown on the file "Pontus unwind consolidated-- Sept-Dec.xlsx", also attached.

Please credit the Joint Account $379,891.34 ($370,625.70 plus 2.5% overhead) to correct the accumulator charges using the agreed upon amortization period.

In its response to IR#28, the Operator noted that it has credited the Joint Account $3,203.87 in Jan, 2022; $53,125.94 in March 2022; and $117,436.30 in July, 2022. However, based on the screenshots of SAP screens

业

shown in the Operator's response, these credits do not appear to pertain to an adjustment of the amortization period but rather, appear to be rig rate adjustments.

Operator is requested to provide additional backup/reconciliation to substantiate that the credits shown are for an adjustment of the amortization period and not for rig rate adjustments. Otherwise, the credit due remains at $379,891.34.

62.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $1,304,521.88 for material write-offs according to the attached JADE lines. Some of these lines were questioned in Information Request 50 submitted to the Operator during the fieldwork. In the response, the Operator indicated that the charge was for writing off some materials, and also stated that it was due to valuation differences.

The materials in question were already purchased by the Joint Account in this and previous periods (including periods prior to this audit). As the materials are already jointly owned, the Joint Account is only due a credit for scrappage value and no further charges.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $1,304,521.88 for these material write-offs.

Operator charged the Joint Account $9,315,531.19 for Mars payroll charges. In response to IR32 the Operator provided job descriptions and locations for a select group of employees that could not be located on the POB.

After review of the support provided by Operator, it was determined that the description of work did not fall under the qualified offsite technical labor activity. Per the 2019 Letter Agreement Exhibit "C" Section 3. OTLChargeable Activities, the above costs do not appear to be "1. Regulatory Activity, 2. Feasibility and Project Studies, or 3. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration"

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $526,261.45 plus associated overhead to the Joint Account for these non-billable payroll expenses.

Please see attached support for this exception.

Credit Denied.

Bryan Jolley -Credit in the amount of $240,518.56 is denied. Bryan Jolly provided technical support to the Mars Corridor Waterflood Expansion - Select to FID Feasibility Studies, Olympus Waterflood Development across various life extension scenarios and Waterflood Expansion - Phase 2 Olympus Development. Per Feb. 2019 settlement, Attachment I, 3.1 Regulatory Activities, Subpart H - Oil and Gas Production Safety System (250.800 - 250.892) and 3.2. Feasibility and Project Study. No credit is due the Joint Account.

业

Blake Cado - Credit in the amount of $89,098.52 is denied. Blake Cado provided support for Rig Pontus emergency response recovery/remediation efforts in accordance with 30 CFR 250.1916, Mars flare tip replacement in accordance with 30 CFR 250.841(b), and Mars vibration monitoring upgrade to ensure proper maintenance of machinery and predicting equipment failure in accordance with 30 CFR 250.1916. Per Feb. 2019 settlement, Attachment I, 3.1 Regulatory Activities are chargeable. No credit is due the Joint Account.

Scott Chiasson - Credit in the amount of $35,546.44 is denied. Scott Chiasson is the HSE Lead and an HSE Assist and Assurance Coach to ensure operation of drilling or abandonment are complying to Subpart D - Oil and Gas Drilling Operations, CFR 250.400 - 250.490. Per Feb. 2019 settlement, Attachment I, 3.1 Regulatory Activities are chargeable., No credit is due the Joint Account.

Johnny Clark - Credit in the amount of $39,038.42 is denied. Johnny Clark is a well supervisor and worked on the Olympus MB16 stimulation in accordance with 30 CFR 250.1165. Per Feb. 2019 settlement, Attachment I, 3.1 Regulatory Activities are chargeable. No credit is due the Joint Account.

Scott Frazier - Credit in the amount of $22,863.08 is denied. Scott Frazier is an Operation Readiness Focal Point. In accordance with 2019 Letter Agreement, 2. Definition of Technical employees, 2nd paragraph. Scott Frazier provided design and execution of the DCS Phase 3 project; upgrade the (4) existing Allen Bradley DA PLC5's to C ontrolLogix, migrates PID loops from the DA PLCs to the DCS, migrates select allocation meter runs to Operator approved Flow Computers, and updates the DCS & PCD hardware and software to extend the support and service life of the primary facility controls. No credit is due the Joint Account.

Christopher Holloway - Credit in the amount of $9,801.64 is denied. Christopher Holloway is an Operation Readiness Assurance (ORA) Lead and participated in the internal technical review and audit of Pontus Emergency Response recovery/remediation project and the Olympus Waterflood Expansion project. The audit and internal technical review are part of the process of project readiness to ensure the project will transition to operation safely I accordance with Subpart H - Oil and Gas Production Safety System (250.800 - 250.892). Per Feb. 2019 settlement, Attachment I, 3.1 Regulatory Activities are chargeable. No credit is due the Joint Account.

Matthew Madden - Credit in the amount of $4,055.85 is denied. Matthew Madden worked on the Olympus Waterflood Development project to identify and select the optimal waterflood solution to support the prolific Mars Basin in the GOM, to understand if waterflood capacity on the Mars TLP should be expanded, install a new waterflood module on the Olympus TLP and understand robustness of design options across various life extension scenarios. Per Feb. 2019 settlement, Attachment I, 3.1 Regulatory Activities, Subpart H - Oil and Gas Production Safety System (250.800 - 250.892) are chargeable. No credit is due the Joint Account.

Scott Meric - Credit in the amount of $9,091.96 is denied. Scott Meric supported the activities of LLE specification, acquisition of wellhead flanges, instrumentation, and well equalization valves for MB-02 in compliance to 30 CFR 250.1916 Mechanical Integrity (Assurance of Quality and Mechanical Integrity of Critical Equipment). Per Feb. 2019 settlement, Attachment I, 3.1 Regulatory Activities is chargeable. No credit is due the Joint Account.

Richard Rabaca - Credit in the amount of $43,418.40 is denied. Richard Rabaca is a HSSE supervisor supporting all platform rigs such as Mars, Olympus, etc. His work typically consists of being the subject matter expert on all HSSE related matters. He provided support/advice for project planning, task planning, behavior-based safety, incident management, company audits, regulator audits, training, environmental matters, and safety coaching. In accordance with the Feb. 2019 settlement, Attachment I, 3.1 Regulatory Activities; CFR 250.1911, 250.1917 - 250.1920, 250.1930, 250.1933 is chargeable. No credit is due to the Joint Account.

业

Miguel Saballos - Credit in the amount of $15,419.92 is denied. Miguel Saballos supported the activities of LLE specification, acquisition of wellhead flanges, instrumentation, and well equalization valves for MB-02 in compliance with 30 CFR 250.1916 Mechanical Integrity (Assurance of Quality and Mechanical Integrity of Critical Equipment). In accordance with r Feb. 2019 settlement, Attachment I, 3.1 Regulatory Activities is chargeable. No credit is due to the Joint Account.

68.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $11,287,952.67 for all affiliate labor cost in 2021 and $4,243,142.90 in 2020. On March 4, 2008 the Parties executed a Letter Agreement defining a fixed affiliate rate to cover affiliate charges to Major Construction Projects, and Integrated Project Teams. Additionally, the Statement of Clarification and Intent (SoCI) states that affiliate costs at the agreed rate charged to Major Construction and IPTs may not be audited and the Operator is not required to otherwise support the rates.

The costs questioned here are charged into projects other than Major Construction Projects and IPTs. These costs are not covered by the agreed rate language from the 2008 Letter Agreement or SoCI, and are therefore subject to Audit, or to other documentation that the rates charged into the Joint Account are at cost, such as a Cost Certificate which is signed and attested by the Operator's Statutory Auditors.

The Operator was requested to provide a Cost Certificate for 2020 and 2021 in Information Request 008 which was issued during the fieldwork. In conversation regarding this IR, the Operator stated that the Cost Certificate for 2021 cost would not be available until 2023. The Operator then stated that the 2020 Cost Certificate was available, although it was not provided to the Auditors during or after the fieldwork.

The Non-Operator is therefore taking exception to $10,490,676.92 of 2021 affiliate costs, and $3,774,640.15 of 2020 affiliate cost as noted in the attached JADE lines pending the Operator providing the requested cost certificates.

69.description:
Operator charged the Joint Account $836,515.33 for personnel expenses related to IQN. In response to IR60 the Operator provided job descriptions and work locations for a select group of contractors that could not be located on the POB.

After review of the support provided by Operator, it was determined that the description of work did not fall under the qualified offsite technical labor activity. Per the 2019 Letter Agreement Exhibit "C" Section 3. OTLChargeable Activities, the above costs do not appear to be "1. Regulatory Activity, 2. Feasibility and Project Studies, or 3. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration"

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $205,358.80 plus associated overhead to the Joint Account for these non-billable expenses.

Please see attached support for this exception.

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

The Letter Agreement of 2019 is an extension of the Accounting Procedure of UOA. Per the 2019 Letter Agreement Exhibit "C" Section 3. OTL-Chargeable Activities, 2. Definition of Technical Employees that "For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include procurement, administration, accounting and auditing, pipeline nominations and scheduling, human resources, management, supervision (excluding first level supervision of operational staff which is billable), legal services, handling taxation matters, permitting/regulatory work, land and division order services. Most of the employees in question are not in any of the disciplines mentioned in 2. Definition of Technical Employees. Therefore, they are within the OTL guideline of the Letter Agreement.

According to the guideline of the 2019 Letter Agreement Exhibit "C" Section 2. OTL Definition and 3. OTLChargeable Activities, all of the costs in question appear to be for in the category of '1. Regulatory Activity, 2.

业

Feasibility and Project Studies, or 3. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration" activities.

1. Akanbi, Adeyemi; Budkley, Michae; and Meric, April are Planners. Their charges of $72,632.09 are directly chargeable to the Joint Account.
2. Fos, Timothy is a Staff Technical Consultant 2 He is responsible for project planning, IE Draft Procedures, managing vessels, tooling for offshore campaigns and the West Boreas CSWT inspection plan. The credit claim of $55,077.33 is denied.
3. Ruhlman, John is a Staff Technical Consultant 2. He is an inspector, construction/ROV specialists and is a Shell representative monitoring the subsea construction and intervention activities. The credit claim of $27,958.93 is denied.
4. Yurco, Isaac is a Staff Technical Consultant 2. He is responsible for project planning and program, including CMF work, Injection points, and Pipe Systemization, maintains the PEI inspection database system (wIMS) ensuring all Risk Based inspection work is complete, consistent, and providing accurate inspections for Olympus Pressure Equipment ensuring BSSE requirements are met. The credit claim of $49,690.45 is denied.

01.description:
SPLITTING THIS CLAIM INTO 2 PARTS: 01A IS JUST THE OVERHEAD THAT WAS NOT ISSUED WHEN THE PARTNER DIRECT CREDITS WERE GIVEN.

Chevron was overcharged a net $1,511,640.03 relating to the operating rig rates billed to Chevron for floater rigs Transocean Pontus and Thalassa conducting work on the Silvertip asset during 2021. The rig rates charged to Chevron during the drilling of the Silvertip leases were based on an agreement between Shell Offshore Inc and SOI Finance Inc. They were not the Contractor Rate that Transocean billed to Shell Oil Company.

In accordance with section 2.5 a of the Settlement Agreement effective January 1, 2019, Chevron agrees to pay the Contractor Rate for any rig-related operations conducted on or after the Effective Date of this Settlement Agreement at any Legacy OA assets, which includes the Silvertip JOA.

An analysis of the difference between the Contractor Rate billed to Shell Oil Company and the rate billed to Chevron for the accounting period January 1, 2021 through December 31, 2021, showed a net difference of $3,084,588.26 plus applicable overhead of $61,691.77. The audit did identify direct credits of $1,634,640.00 given to Chevron during 2021. The resulting difference is a net credit of $1,511,640.03 due to Chevron.

Chevron should be credited a net $1,511,640.03 with a reference to Chevron's audit number a nd exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

Chevron was overcharged a net $75,916.40 relating to the operating and reduced rig rates included in the Transocean Thalassa initial mobilization and startup cost pools that are being allocated to properties being serviced. The rig rates that are included in the pool allocation costs were based on an agreement between Shell Offshore Inc and SOI Finance Inc. They were not the Contractor Rate that Transocean billed to Shell Oil Company.

In accordance with section 2.5 A of the Settlement Agreement signed in July 2021 and made effective January 1, 2019, Chevron and Shell agreed to pay the Contractor Rate for any rig-related operations conducted on or after the Effective Date of this Settlement Agreement at any Legacy OA assets, which includes the Silvertip JOA.

An analysis of the operating and reduced operating rates used by Shell Oil Company and the actual Transocean rates that were included in the cost pool resulted in a reduced overall cost pool daily rate of $2,067.44. The Silvertip asset used the Transocean Thalassa rig for 60 days from November 2020 through January 2021. Gross credit of $124,046.40 times our 60% working interest shows net credit due of $74,427.84 plus 2% overhead of $1,488.56

Chevron should be credited a net of $75,916.40 with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

05.short_description: Seismic Acquisition-Affiliate Labor Covered by Overhead
05.description:
The Operator charged the Silvertip Joint Account $103,145.00 for Affiliate Labor personnel utilized on the 2021 ST P-Cable Seismic Data Acquisition project. Five (5) Affiliate Labor personnel above first level supervision, or otherwise covered by overhead, were utilized for this project based on the attached Great White exception 05 Auditor Support Worksheet and Great White Information Request 29 (hereafter GW IR-29) which was raised during the fieldwork. The exception also applies to Silvertip.

The specific individuals subject to this exception are French Lewis, Karen Godfrey, Keith Hunt, Matthew McDonald, and Austin Joe (AJ)Cozzens (who supervises Keith Hunt, who in turn supervises Karen Godfrey and Matthew McDonald). This information was obtained from the 2021 Consolidated Employee Listing provided by Shell.

As per the Geo-Operations Team Lead response on May 3, 2022, the personnel noted by the Auditor are Staff and were involved in the planning, preparations and operational management of the Cable Seismic Data Acquisition project as follows:

Matthew McDonald-performed the survey design and the competitive tender which awarded NCS the work; Keith Hunt-Team Lead providing guidance, support, and assurance to all standards throughout. Responsible for delivery of project;

Karen Godfrey-Project Manager for detailed planning and preparations and operational oversight;

AJ Cozzens-Provided technical assurance for the planning and survey design and overall accountability for the work; Lewis French-provided HSE management, oversight, and advice on complying with HSSE Control Framework.

The Billing Standards-Chevron Shell Settlement Agreement effective January 1,2019, was used as the basis for evaluating "direct chargeability" for all charges within this Audit Exception. A Section 2. Attachment Section 2. of this document titled Definition of Technical Employees, in part, states:

For the avoidance of doubt, Technical Employees do not include procurement, administration, accounting and auditing, pipeline nominations and scheduling, human resources, management, supervision (excluding first level supervision of operational staff which is billable)), legal services, handling taxation matters, permitting/regulatory work, land and division order services .

According to the Operator's response on Great White IR-029, Matthew McDonald performed the survey design and the competitive tender which awarded NCS the work. Competitive Tendering is part of the Procurement process and is disallowed by both the JOA and interpreting MFI's, as well as the Billing Standards referenced above which states (in part) that For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include procurement [...]. Therefore, Matthew McDonald's charges are not permissible under this aforementioned Agreement.

Mr. Keith Hunt is noted to be part of "USAAP Job 1C - Middle Management - (Professional)" according to the 2021SEPCO Staff listing provided by the Operator during the fieldwork (see Org Structure" tab, Col. S). The Settlement Agreement Attachment 1, Section1.b. Definition of "Technical Employees" also states in part "For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include[...] management, supervision (excluding first level supervision of operational staff which is billable) [...]". Therefore Mr. Hunt's charges are not permissible under the Settlement Agreement.

The Operator stated, in their response to GWIR-29 that Ms. Karen Godfrey was "Project Manager for detailed planning and preparations and operational oversight." According to the Settlement Agreement, Billing Standards, Section k. Third-Party Project Management, "[...] costs related to third party project management that are charged as part of the overall cost for provision of goods and services [...] may be charged to the Joint Account as a component cost of the underlying goods and services and shall not be qualified as OTL or administrative costs covered under Overhead." As Ms. Godfrey is not Third-Party as required by the Settlement Agreement, but rather First-Party as a Shell employee, her project management services are disallowed under the Settlement Agreement.

Additionally, according to the Operator's response on GW IR -29, Mr. Matt McDonald "performed the survey design and the competitive tender which awarded NCS the work". Competitive Tendering is part of the Procurement process, and is disallowed by both the JOA and interpreting MFI's as noted below, as well as the Settlement Agreement Attachment 1, Section 1.b. Definition of "Technical Employees" which states in part that "For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include procurement [...]".

AJ Cozzens reports directly to the GM Geophysics West and is above first level of supervision, which is not permissible under this aforementioned Agreement.

The Accounting Procedure attached to and made a part of the Joint Operating Agreement, "Exhibit C, Section III Overhead states,

"As compensation for administrative, supervision, office services and warehousing costs, Operator shall charge the Joint Accounting accordance with this Section III.

Under Section II. Direct Charges, only First level supervision is allowed"

Per MFI 21, charges for services like planning, budgeting, legal, HR, procurement, etc., are Indirect Costs and are not allowed to be charged as Direct costs. Individuals performing such functions charged to the Joint Account are marked on our support provided to the Operator as "Other Covered by OVHD."

The Operator is requested to credit the Silvertip Joint Account $76,969.20 ($75,460.00 plus 2.0% overhead of $1,509.20) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

11.description:
The Operator charged $3,336,923.38 to the PRH Shared Opex - Natural Catastrophes WBS (O.US.132.PER.001.79100) through Perdido H&P 205 Rig-Perdido-TS IDA-Abn WBS (P.US.AOP.EO.21.024.27) and Perdido H&P 205 Rig-Perdido-TS Nicholas- WBS (P.US.AOP.EO.21.030.24) for costs incurred during Hurricanes Ida and Nicholas.

For Hurricane Ida (8/29/21-9/13/21), the rig schedule provided by the Operator classified the hurricane evacuation was associated with and affected the Perdido Caisson C ESP 880 motor upgrade, although the project wrapped up prior to the hurricane. Since this was an upgrade of equipment, it was a development project that should have incurred the associated development overhead percentages, as outlined in the audit report.

For Hurricane Nicholas (9/13/21-9/20/21), the rig schedule provided by the Operator classified the hurricane evacuation was associated with and affected the Great White GA-009 Zonal Isolation Project. This was a development project and incurred 2.5% overhead.

The H&P 205 Rig Use Agreement dated June 1, 2020, Section 1.12 - Great White Time, states that time during storm evacuation or any interruption of Great White Rig Activity for any reason including Force Majeure events shall be Great White Time, and Section 1.16 - Host Time, shall mean all periods of time that are not Great White Time. Therefore, any costs associated with Great White Time and Host Time that was to incur development overhead but was delayed due to shut down, should also incur development overhead rather than production overhead.

The Operator is requested to credit the Silvertip Joint Account $91,515.93 ($55,859.14 plus overhead of $35,656.79) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
As per the Senior Finance Advisor, the overhead application for abnormal operations immediate response AFEs will follow the OH rate of the prevailing AFE. The Ida AFE followed the ESP C AFE which is a maintenance item and applicable to the 13% OH rate. The Nicholas AFE slip attached to the GA09 zonal isolation and is also a maintenance activity and should be applicable to the 13% OH rate.

No credit is due.

12.short_description: OTL not in Compliance with Settlement Agreement
12.description:
The Operator charged the Silvertip Joint Account $21,436.74, before overhead, for Total System Integrators to provide Perdido General Support and Perdido Alarm Suppression Support through various monthly invoices. The invoices totaling $250,230.06 were allocated from the PRH Shared Opex - Perform Well and Facility WBS (O.US.132.PER.001.71300).

The Operator's response to Perdido Information Request 25 was that the sampled invoice 'included work to improve process safety and production availability on the Yokowama control system….this system is abso lutely critical to be able to operate Perdido and is the entire interface that operations uses to control and maintain the process conditions within the optimal and safe operating ranges. The three consultants noted on the invoice worked on pipeline pump improvement, alarm management, and safety improvements. Based on COPAS MFI 44, these charges are direct billable to the Joint Account.'

While the offsite technical labor (OTL) providing IT support for the billable systems used on the platform may be required, they do not qualify for direct chargeability under the Billing Standards settlement agreements between the parties, as they have not been adequately and properly documented by the Operator as activities required to comply with regulatory activities, and they have not been identified as Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration whose job function was previously performed offshore/onsite but were relocated onshore.

The Operator is requested to credit the Silvertip Joint Account $24,009.15 ($21,436.74 plus 12% overhead of $2,572.41) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
The offsite technical labor noted by the Auditor was through TSI which is the core contractor that Shell uses to develop code for the Yokogawa control system. As noted in the Operator response to IR #25 during the audit fieldwork, this labor is supported by COPAS MFI 44 by being included under the software costs. The work done on this invoice was programming, testing, and developing installation procedures for various upgrade projects to improve process safety or production availability. More specifically:

- Devin was an assistant programmer for Perdido projects. His work was primarily programming for a pipeline pump improvement and a safety improvement for the topsides separation system.
- Mohammad was the primary asset support programmer for Perdido. His time was spent on a variety of projects supporting alarm management, control and safety improvements, and general troubleshooting to assist the offshore Electronics Technicians.
- Salvadores work was in support of our Alarm Management program for the facility. He was involved in making backups of the alarm database, helping to configure a new server for the system, and correcting the reports that the asset support team uses for technical monitoring.

Their work was directly associated with alarm management (Process Safety Basic Requirement within Shells HSSE framework); Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) action items that required remediation (required to maintain adequate process safety); and pipeline pump control logic improvements required to maintain the export pump system health (therefore required to keep the facility functional). In addition to their work being supported by MFI 44 , these items are in the SEMS CFR 250.1910 category as well as under the Settlement Agreement Billing Standards for facility improvement projects.

No credit is due.

13.short_description: OTL not in Compliance with Settlement Agreement
13.description:
The Operator charged the Silvertip Joint Account $8,231.60, before overhead, for drafting & engineering services provided by Worley ECR Services on Invoice No. 332380. The invoice totaling $94,750.06 was allocated from the PRH Shared Opex - Perform Well and Facility WBS (O.US.132.PER.001.71300).

The Billing Standards settlement agreements between the parties only allows for offsite technical labor (OTL) associated with field improvement or facility improvement projects, and for feasibility studies undertaken to progress future projects, pursuant to a separately approved Authorization for Expenditure (AFE).

The Operator's response to Perdido Information Request 27 stated the water filtration equipment was temporary rental equipment and that no AFE was sent for election as it was production operations. Since the project was for operations and an AFE was not submitted as outlined in the Billing Standards, the OTL associated with the temporary water filtration equipment project is not chargeable.

The Operator is requested to credit the Silvertip Joint Account $9,219.39 ($8,231.60 plus 12% overhead of $987.79) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
As per the Asset Finance Manager and Shell Senior Legal Counsel, the Perdido overboard water was out of compliance with National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit, and the NPDES permits are governed by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). The Operator then had to install the equipment after EPA required them to mitigate in the short term with the carbon filtration temporary equipment. The Operator then had to engage BSEE for the limited purposes of submitting the topside modifications. These steps were necessary to bring the host into compliance with applicable law, regulations and permits. These charges are covered under the Settlement Agreement Billing Standards Regulatory Activities. The Auditor is requested to engage with their commercial teams as the charges being part of production operations were fully communicated to co-owners as well as being part of the co-owner meeting engagements.

No credit is due.

14.description: The Operator charged the Silvertip Joint Account $2,428,576.77 for Affiliate Labor charges from the Operator's P&T Affiliate. These charges were the subject of Great White Information Requests (IR's) 15, 16, 17, and 18 which were raised during the audit Fieldwork. The Silvertip rate issues were very similar to the issues on Great White, so these Great White Information Requests are incorporated as support for this exception. According to the Silvertip UOA Exhibit C, Addendum to Exhibit C, Statement of Clarification and Intent, the Operator may charge Affiliate Labor at an "all-inclusive standard rate" per the following: Affiliates shall maintain auditable records to support all charges made by it to the Joint Account and as to such charges shall be subject to the same audit requirements provided for Operator's charges in Section I, Paragraph 5 of this Exhibit C. If an all-inclusive standard rate is used, such audit requirements shall be limited to verification that such rate is, in fact, the rate(s) customarily charged by its Affiliates. During the audit, and in the responses to the above-mentioned IR's, the Operator was not able to substantiate or confirm that the rate charged was valid and permissible, in accordance with the Statement of Clarification and Intent. The Operator is requested to credit the Silvertip Joint Account $2,477,558.44 ($2,428,576.77 plus $48,981.67 of calculated Overhead) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing

replies.text:
The Operator provided support and examples during the audit fieldwork in regards to affiliate rates. For further clarity, a customarily charged affiliate rate was used in regards to affiliates, which may also include contractors. The rates customarily charged by the affiliates would have been available to the auditor when vouching the applicable SIEP invoices. By following the examples provided during the fieldwork, the Auditor would then be able to confirm that each rate charged was valid and permissible.

Please see attached for a summary.

No credit is due.

attachments: SIL AE-14.JADE and Support back to auditor.xlsx

15.description:
Chevron was overcharged a net $93,760.19 relating to the operating and reduced rig rates included in the Transocean Pontus initial mobilization and startup cost pools that are being allocated to properties being serviced. The rig rates that are included in the pool allocation costs were based on an agreement between Shell Offshore Inc and SOI Finance Inc. They were not the Contractor Rate that Transocean billed to Shell Oil Company.

In accordance with section 2.5 A of the Settlement Agreement signed in July 2021 and made effective January 1, 2019, Chevron and Shell agreed to pay the Contractor Rate for any rig-related operations conducted on or after the Effective Date of this Settlement Agreement at any Legacy OA assets, which includes the Silvertip JOA.

An analysis of the operating and reduced operating rates used by Shell Oil Company and the actual Transocean rates that were included in the cost pool resulted in a reduced overall cost pool daily rate of $2,220.33. The Silvertip asset

used the Transocean Pontus rig for 69 days from June 2021 through August 2021. Gross credit of $153,202.91 times our 60% working interest shows net credit due of $91,921.75 plus 2% overhead of $1,838.44.

Chevron should be credited a net of $93,760.19 with a reference to Chevron's audit num ber and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

26.description:
Silvertip projects were allocated $283,251.21 during 2021 for the $7.5 million estimated cost to demobilize the drillship Transocean Pontus at the end of the contract term as per guidelines stated in COPAS Model Form Interpretation 56, Rig Related Costs. The estimated cost was allocated based on initial contract term of 5 years, October 22, 2017 through October 22, 2022. The day rate of $4,105.09 ($7.5 million divided by 1,827 days) was billed to Silvertip for 69 days during this period.

A review of the Transocean Fleet Status report, Fleet Status Report | Transocean Investor Relations (deepwater.com), dated April 25, 2022 showed the Transocean Pontus estimated current contract expiration date of October 2027. Based on this information, the Transocean Pontus contract was extended to Shell for another 5 years.

COPAS MFI56 states 'If the Company extends the Rig Contract term, the recommended practice is to treat t he Rig Contract extension period as a new Rig Contract rather than reallocating the Rig-Related Costs from the inception of the original Rig Contract to the termination date of the Rig Contract extension period'. The MFI also stated that if another Company operating in the same area hires the Rig immediately following the end of the Rig Contract, there might not be a Demobilization cost or fee.

Because the extension is treated as a new Rig Contract immediately following the end of the original contract term, there should not be any estimated demobilization cost allocated to the projects served under the original contract term.

The Operator is requested to credit the Silvertip Joint Account $288,916.23 ($283,251.21 plus 2% overhead of $5,665.02) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

30.short_description: Transocean Pontus - Blind Ram Sheers Upgrade
30.description:
Silvertip projects were overcharged $77,004.00 during 2021 for the incorrect day rate used to allocate the $785,000 budgeted cost relating to the April 2021 blind sheer rams upgrade on Transocean Pontus. The day rate used ($1,448.00/day) to allocate the charge was based on the remaining life of the initial contract from April 29, 2021 through October 22, 2022, or 542 days. However, the day rate should have been calculated from the initial install through the end of the extended contract, April 29, 2021 through October 22, 2027 or 2,368 days resulting in a day rate of $332/day. Credit for the rate difference of $1,116/day is requested for the 69 days used on the Silvertip projects.

A review of the Transocean Fleet Status report, Fleet Status Report | Transocean Investor Relations (deepwater.com), dated April 25, 2022 showed the Transocean Pontus estimated current contract expiration date of October 2027. Based on this information, the Transocean Thalassa contract was extended to Shell for another 5 years.

COPAS MFI56 states 'When material Rig Modifications, Rig Repairs or Program Moves are performed near the end of a Rig Contract term and are directly linked to the Company's decision to extend the Rig Contract, the extension term should be included along with the remainder of the original contract term when allocating the accumulated costs of those activities'.

The Operator is requested to credit the Silvertip Joint Account $78,544.08 ($77,004.00 plus 2% overhead of $1,540.08) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
The Auditor included three months (June, July and August) of unwind charges from the JADE report as support for their calculation. This exception is specifically related to the Blind Sheer Ram Upgrade (BSRU) on Transocean Pontus. Although the BSRU June charges were initially charged to the Joint Account within the unwind charges, they were reversed in July as is detailed on the JADE. These JADE lines were not included in the supporting documentation for the exception by the Auditor, but for ease of reference have been attached. In addition, July and August unwind charges did not include any charges for the Blind Sheer Ram Upgrade. Therefore, the Joint Account was not charged for this upgrade and the exception is denied.

No credit is due.

31.description:
The Operator charged the Silvertip Joint Account $152,013.22, before overhead, for a monthly Perdido Gas Buyback allocation during 2020-2021. The journal entries totaling $1,515,833.23 were allocated from the PRH Shared Opex - Perform Well and Facility WBS (O.US.132.PER.001.71300). Per Section 3.b of Perdido COUA Exhibit P-1 (Great White PHA Terms) and Exhibit P-2 (Silvertip and Tobago PHA Terms), 'Host fuel gas consumption would be allocated on a monthly basis (based on production actually processed through the Host) to the Producers…for production handling and operating services. The Prod ucers would be

obligated to and would furnish their monthlyallocated share of fuel gas…production handling and operating services in kind.' Based on the Production Schematic provided on the revenue audit, the gas buyback is not flowing through the sales meter, but instead is taken to the Operations Master Fuel meter to be used as fuel gas. As a result, the value of this gas should not be a shared expenses nor be subject to the overhead percentage. The Operator is requested to credit the Silvertip Joint Account $170,254.81 ($152,013.22 plus 12% overhead of $18,241.59) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
The BSEE surface commingling permit drawing shows a simplified process flow diagram of the master fuel meter and two paths for fuel gas to flow to that master fuel meter.

During normal operations, all fuel is sourced from production and flow to the master fuel meter upstream of the sales meters (red dashed line). In this scenario, there is no gas flowing through the gas buyback meter.

During start-up or when leaner gas is needed for fuel, fuel gas will be sourced downstream of the sales meters. This fuel gas will be measured through the gas buyback meter prior to being measured by the master fuel gas meter (green dashed line). In this scenario, any production not following the normal red dashed line to the master fuel meter will flow through the sales meters (blue dashed line).

Within the Fuel Allocation section of Article VII Allocation in the Perdido Regional Host Measurement and Allocation Procedures Amendment No. 3, the measured buyback volume is removed from the measured fuel gas volume (master fuel gas volume) prior to allocating to the producing wells.

The Producers are getting credit for all gas that flows through the sales gas meters. Shell is buying any additional fuel gas needed downstream of the sales gas meters which is measured by the gas buyback meter and the buyback fuel gas OPEX is associated with this fuel gas not delivered by the Producers.

No credit is due.

For Hurricane Ida (8/29/21-9/13/21), the rig schedule provided by the Operator classified the hurricane evacuation was associated with and affected the Perdido Caisson C ESP 880 motor upgrade, although the project wrapped up prior to the hurricane. Since this was an upgrade of equipment, it was a development project that should have incurred the associated development overhead percentages, as outlined in the audit report. For Hurricane Nicholas (9/13/21-9/20/21), the rig schedule provided by the Operator classified the hurricane evacuation was associated with and affected the Great White GA-009 Zonal Isolation Project. This was a development project and incurred 2.5% overhead. The H&P 205 Rig Use Agreement dated June 1, 2020, Section 1.12 - Great White Time, states that time during storm evacuation or any interruption of Great White Rig Activity for any reason including Force Majeure events shall be Great White Time, and Section 1.16 - Host Time, shall mean all periods of time that are not Great White Time. Therefore, any costs associated with Great White Time and Host Time that was to incur development overhead but was delayed due to shut down, should also incur development overhead rather than production overhead. The invoices totaling $250,230.06 were allocated from the PRH Shared Opex - Perform Well and Facility WBS (O.U S.132.PER.001.71300). The Operator's response to Perdido Information Request 25 was that the sampled invoice 'included work to improve process safety and production availability on the Yokowama control system….this system is absolutely critical to be able to operate Perdido and is the entire interface that operations uses to control and maintain the process conditions within the optimal and safe operating ranges. The three consultants noted on the invoice worked on pipeline pump improvement, alarm management, and safety improvements. Based on COPAS MFI 44, these charges are direct billable to the Joint Account.'

While the offsite technical labor (OTL) providing IT support for the billable systems used on the platform may be required, they do not qualify for direct chargeability under the Billing Standards settlement agreements between the parties, as they have not been adequately and properly documented by the Operator as activities required to comply with regulatory activities, and they have not been identified as Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration whose job function was previously performed offshore/onsite but were relocated onshore. The Operator is requested to credit the Tobago Joint Account $5,364.07 ($4,789.35 plus 12% overhead of $574.72) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
The offsite technical labor noted by the Auditor was through TSI which is the core contractor that Shell uses to develop code for the Yokogawa control system. As noted in the Operator response to IR #25 during the audit fieldwork, this labor is supported by COPAS MFI 44 by being included under the software costs. The work done on this invoice was programming, testing, and developing installation procedures for various upgrade projects to improve process safety or production availability. More specifically:

- Devin was an assistant programmer for Perdido projects. His work was primarily programming for a pipeline pump improvement and a safety improvement for the topsides separation system.
- Mohammad was the primary asset support programmer for Perdido. His time was spent on a variety of projects supporting alarm management, control and safety improvements, and general troubleshooting to assist the offshore Electronics Technicians.
- Salvadores work was in support of our Alarm Management program for the facility. He was involved in making backups of the alarm database, helping to configure a new server for the system, and correcting the reports that the asset support team uses for technical monitoring.

Their work was directly associated with alarm management (Process Safety Basic Requirement within Shells HSSE framework); Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) action items that required remediation (required to maintain adequate process safety); and pipeline pump control logic improvements required to maintain the export pump system health (therefore required to keep the facility functional). In addition to their work being supported by MFI 44, these items are in the SEMS CFR 250.1910 category as well as under the Settlement Agreement Billing Standards for facility improvement projects.

No credit is due.

The Operator's response to Perdido Information Request 27 stated the water filtration equipment was temporary rental equipment and that no AFE was sent for election as it was production operations. replies.text:
As per the Asset Finance Manager and Shell Senior Legal Counsel, the Perdido overboard water was out of compliance with National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit, and the NPDES permits are governed by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). The Operator then had to install the equipment after EPA required them to mitigate in the short term with the carbon filtration temporary equipment. The Operator then had to engage BSEE for the limited purposes of submitting the topside modifications. These steps were necessary to bring the host into compliance with applicable law, regulations and permits. These charges are covered under the Settlement Agreement Billing Standards Regulatory Activities. The Auditor is requested to engage with their commercial teams as the charges being part of production operations were fully communicated to co-owners as well as being part of the co-owner meeting engagements.

No credit is due.

The Operator charged the Tobago Joint Account $11,867.44 plus 13% overhead for Non-Major Construction Overhead Payroll for employees who did not work onsite through allocations. The Auditors reviewed employee hours charged to the Joint Account compared to the number of days onsite per the POB reports to calculate the hours per day ratio (hours charged / number of days on POB.) Employees identified as offsite were not on board per the POB and helicopter logs. This was raised to the Operator in Great White Information Request 27 during the fieldwork. Additionally, the description of work provided by the Operator was compared to the various Settlement Agreements and was not found to be in compliance with Attachment 1 "Agreed OTL Definitions and Billing Standards", Section 3.A. "Regulatory Activity", 3.B. "Feasibility and Project Studies", and 3.C. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration". For reference, this exception applies to three exceptions from the 2022 audit, Great White exception 3, Silvertip exception 27 and Tobago exception 11. 12.description: The Operator charged the Tobago Joint Account $31,724.96, before overhead, for a monthly Perdido Gas Buyback allocation during 2020-2021. The journal entries totaling $1,515,833.23 were allocated from the PRH Shared Opex - Perform Well and Facility WBS (O.US.132.PER.001.71300). Per Section 3.b of Perdido COUA Exhibit P-1 (Great White PHA Terms) and Exhibit P-2 (Silvertip and Tobago PHA Terms), 'Host fuel gas consumption would be allocated on a monthly basis (based on production actually processed through the Host) to the Producers…for production handli ng and operating services. The Producers would be obligated to and would furnish their monthlyallocated share of fuel gas…production handling and operating services in kind.' Based on the Production Schematic provided on the revenue audit, the gas buyback is not flowing through the sales meter, but instead is taken to the Operations Master Fuel meter to be used as fuel gas. As a result, the value of this gas should not be a shared expenses nor be subject to the overhead percentage. The Operator is requested to credit the Tobago Joint Account $35,531.96 ($31,724.96 plus 12% overhead of $3,807.00) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
The BSEE surface commingling permit drawing shows a simplified process flow diagram of the master fuel meter and two paths for fuel gas to flow to that master fuel meter.

During normal operations, all fuel is sourced from production and flow to the master fuel meter upstream of the sales meters (red dashed line). In this scenario, there is no gas flowing through the gas buyback meter.

During start-up or when leaner gas is needed for fuel, fuel gas will be sourced downstream of the sales meters. This fuel gas will be measured through the gas buyback meter prior to being measured by the master fuel gas meter (green dashed line). In this scenario, any production not following the normal red dashed line to the master fuel meter will flow through the sales meters (blue dashed line).

Within the Fuel Allocation section of Article VII Allocation in the Perdido Regional Host Measurement and Allocation Procedures Amendment No. 3, the measured buyback volume is removed from the measured fuel gas volume (master fuel gas volume) prior to allocating to the producing wells.

The Producers are getting credit for all gas that flows through the sales gas meters. Shell is buying any additional fuel gas needed downstream of the sales gas meters which is measured by the gas buyback meter and the buyback fuel gas OPEX is associated with this fuel gas not delivered by the Producers.

No credit is due.

The Operator charged the Joint Account $26,500.00, for insurance underwriting costs on Marsh JLT Specialty invoice ENGEE2000009001, through WBS C.US.WHL. PD.19.002.123AU (Whale Finance-CAR Insurance Underwriting).

Exhibit C, Section III (Overhead) - states that administration costs are covered by the agreed upon percentage overhead rates. While the insurance premiums for the Whale CAR insurance were agreed upon by the parties, the underwriting costs are not the insurance itself but are for the professionals who evaluate and analyze the risks involved in insuring people and assets and establish pricing for accepted insurable risks. Therefore, these costs are administrative in nature and covered by the overhead rates.

The Operator should credit the Joint Account $27,560.00 ($26,500.00 plus 4% overhead of $1,060.00) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
Insurance underwriting is a technical report of the project in order to be able to obtain CAR insurance on the project. Without this document, CAR insurance cannot be created. This document is put together by an independent third party (Marsh) who reviews technical data from the team and interviews team members in order to best represent the risk of the project. As per the Finance Manager, they provide the technical details of the scope and the associated risks and then the market determines the pricing for these risks. As agreed by the Auditors commentary, this work is done by professional insurance risk managers. A professional degree, certifications, and years of experience are required to build an insurance for a complex project such as this and therefore demonstrates that it is not administrative in nature.

No credit is due.

So even though Affiliate is mentioned under the definition of Employees under Exhibit G, the clarification and distinction in the Accounting Procedure gives the direction of how to charge for each. The “one full day per a given month is only applicable to Employees, and not Affiliates. Screen shot below is an excerpt from Exhibit “G” regarding IPT. It defines Employees, but it also lists in Section 2.0 the distinction of Employee Staff contributing 2.1.1 and Affiliate and Contract Staff 2.1.2. Accounting Procedure Section III Overhead 2.C: Excerpts below are from Exhibit “C” Statement of Clarification:

As Shell properly recognizes, the definition of "Employees" contained in Exhibit G of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement (Integrated Project Team and Technology Sharing) expressly defines "Employees" to include any individual under the employment of any Affiliate of any Party to the Operating Agreement. Therefore, any Employee of a Shell Affiliate that is a member of the Integrated Project Team, is considered an Employee of Shell. The Addendum to Exhibit C of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement expressly incorporates by reference the terms and conditions of Exhibit G (See Addendum to Exhibit C, p.1). Consequently, all wages paid to Shell Affiliates are chargeable in accordance with Section III, Paragraph 2.B. Moreover, Shell has noted that there is a prior course of dealing between CNOOC and Shell regarding audit exceptions for employee charges of less than one day per month, which further supports CNOOC's position. As Shell is aware, a prior course of dealing is "a sequence of previous conduct between the parties to the agreement," which can provide "a common basis of understanding for interpreting their expressions and other conduct" (RESTATEMENT (SECOND) OF CONTRACTS § 223, 1981). Given Shell's longstanding approval of CNOOC's interpretation requiring salaries of Shell's Affiliates to be subject to the time requirement of Section III, Paragraph 2.B(a), the parties have established a course of dealing regarding the interpretation of the Joint Operating Agreement concerning the subject audit exception.

Credit denied. There is no change in the Operator’s stance even though prior years audit exceptions were incorrectly interpreted by the Operator. As previously mentioned, the Addendum to Exhibit C for Section III (Overhead), Paragraph 2.C points out the distinction between a) services rendered by Employees of Participants and, b) Affiliate and Drafting Services. Paragraph “a” for employees has the reference of at least one full day during a given month, but the Affiliate paragraph “b” does not. Thus, the “one full day per a given month” is only applicable to Employees, and not Affiliates and Contract Staff.

This exception remains open. The Operator presents several reasons for denying this claim. First, the Operator’s assertion that MFI-19, Section II.2.C (Direct Charges - Labor) is a reason for denying this exception is incorrect. The Interpretative Section of MFI-19, Section II.2.C states “Since these costs are limited, being based upon a maximum amount earned by each employee and the maximum earnings may be different for each category of charge, the cost terminates at various times during the year for individual employees.” This item addresses those labor costs based upon the maximum amount earned by each employee, such as FICA and unemployment taxes, the cost incurred usually terminates at various times during the year for individual employees. This citation is not applicable to the audit exception. Secondly, the Operator’s states MFI-19 II.15 (Other Expenditures) applies since the costs are an expenditure “not covered or dealt with in the foregoing provisions of this Section II, or in Section III and which is of direct benefit to the Joint Property and is incurred by the Operator in the necessary and proper conduct of the Joint Operations.” The chargeability of Labor is addressed in Section II.2.A and offsite technical labor is specifically addressed in Section II.2.A(5). Therefore, Section II.15 does not apply since the Labor expenditure is already addressed in the Accounting Procedure. Thirdly, the Operator suggests those individuals supporting SEMS-related activities are directly billable to the joint account since they are directly employed in the operation of the joint property and fall under Section II - Direct Labor, of the Accounting Procedure. As shown below from Section II.B.2, Technical Labor, of *MFI – 21, Overhead Principles* , “in the operation of” means “offsite.” Technical Labor costs are classified as either "on-site" or "off-site." Either one or both may qualify as a Direct Charge or as Overhead depending upon the terms of the agreement. On-site Technical Labor includes Technical Personnel directly employed on the Joint Property, while off-site includes those not working on the Joint Property but directly employed in the operation of the Joint Property.

11.description: Four major construction WBS’ were charged a total of $1.3 million for SIEP labor as shown in the tab 'Exc 11.1 JADE'. A review of the CJI3 report of each WBS revealed some SIEP employees and SIEP contractors charged less than one day per month to the Major Construction project. It should be noted these four major construction projects were not included in Exception No 3 of this Audit Report. The Addendum to Exhibit "C", Accounting Procedure Statement of Clarification and Intent provides in its clarification to Section III, Paragraph 2.B.a "Services Rendered by Operator's Employees": "Salaries will be charged to the Joint Account based upon actual days worked only when such time totals at least one day or more per month that is devoted to the Major Construction project." Exhibit "G" attached to and made part of the Prospect Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement provides in its Section 1.6 Employees: "Employees shall mean any individual under the employment of any party to this Operating Agreement including any Affiliate or contractor which may represent any Party hereunder." The audit worksheet 'Exc 11.6\_CJI3 Summary', provided herein, presents JADE analysis and identification of 12 SIEP employees charging a total of 116.0 hours to major construction projects during the service period of September 2020 through October 2021 with those hours reported totaling less than 1 full day (8 hours) in each month. The Operator is requested to credit the various WBS’ identified in 'Exc 11.6\_CJI3 Summary' in the amount of $36,858.00, plus 2.0% Major Construction Overhead. Credit Requested $36,858.00 Overhead $ 737.16 Exception Total $37,595.16

replies.text: Credit denied. Each of the WBS codes on this exception are Major Construction AFEs (as noted by the auditor in the exception summary), however, they are not part of the IPT. The auditor is referencing Exhibit “G” (Integrated Project Team and Technology Sharing) as the basis for defining employee. Exhibit “G” is for the Integrated Project Team and not applicable to all Major Construction projects. The 8-hour monthly limitation for Major Construction projects does not apply to Employees or Affiliates. The Addendum to Exhibit C for Section III Overhead 2.B points out the distinction between services rendered by a. Employees of Participants and b. Affiliate and Drafting Services. Neither Paragraph “a” for employees nor paragraph 'b" for affiliates reference of at least one full day during a given month. See screen shots below. Accounting Procedure Section III Overhead 2.B:

This exception remains open. As Shell properly recognizes, the definition of "Employees" contained in Exhibit G of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement (Integrated Project Team and Technology Sharing) expressly defines "Employees" to include any individual under the employment of any Affiliate of any Party to the Operating Agreement. Therefore, any Employee of a Shell Affiliate that is a member of the Integrated Project Team, is considered an Employee of Shell. The Addendum to Exhibit C of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement expressly incorporates by reference the terms and conditions of Exhibit G (See Addendum to Exhibit C, p.1). Consequently, all wages paid to Shell Affiliates are chargeable in accordance with Section III, Paragraph 2.B. Moreover, Shell has noted that there is a prior course of dealing between CNOOC and Shell regarding audit exceptions for employee charges of less than one day per month, which further supports CNOOC's position. As Shell is aware, a prior course of dealing is "a sequence of previous conduct between the parties to the agreement," which can provide "a common basis of understanding for interpreting their expressions and other conduct" (RESTATEMENT (SECOND) OF CONTRACTS § 223, 1981). Given Shell's longstanding approval of CNOOC's interpretation requiring salaries of Shell's Affiliates to be subject to the time requirement of Section III, Paragraph 2.B(a), the parties have established a course of dealing regarding the interpretation of the Joint Operating Agreement concerning the subject audit exception.

Credit denied. There is no change in the Operator’s stance even though prior years audit exceptions were incorrectly interpreted by the Operator. As previously mentioned, the Addendum to Exhibit C for Section III (Overhead), Paragraph 2.C points out the distinction between a) services rendered by Employees of Participants and, b) Affiliate and Drafting Services. Paragraph “a” for employees has the reference of at least one full day during a given month, but the Affiliate paragraph “b” does not. Thus, the “one full day per a given month” is only applicable to Employees, and not Affiliates.

30.description: In accordance with Exhibit "G" attached to and made part of the Prospect Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement provides in its Section 1.6 Employees: "Employees shall mean any individual under the employment of any party to this Operating Agreement including any Affiliate or contractor which may represent any Party hereunder." Further, the Addendum to Exhibit "C", Accounting Procedure Statement of Clarification and Intent provides in its clarification to Section III, Paragraph 2.C.a "Services Rendered by Employees of Participants": "A pro rata share of salaries, wages, payroll burden and Personal Expenses of part\_x0002\_time technical personnel may be charged direct if the individual's time devoted to the project totals as least one full day during a given month." In the worksheet Ex34.02 - Exception Schedule, a JADE analysis and identification of various employees charging a total of 268.79 hours to the Project over the service period of January through December 2021 with those hours reported totaling less than 1 full day (8 hours) in each month. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account for the employee labor costs that were charged to the Joint Account and when accumulated by month total less than 8 hours. These costs have been summarized in the supporting worksheets and total $39,050.43 plus the applicable overhead of $2,188.91 for a total exception amount of $41,239.34. replies.text: Credit denied. The auditor is referencing Exhibit “G” of the JOA pertaining to IPT for this entire claim. In reviewing the working file provided by the auditor in ‘worksheet Ex34.02 - Exception Schedule’, the employees identified wrote time to numerous WBS codes, including IPT, Development, and Production WBS codes. In order to investigate further, the Operator is requesting the auditor to provide a revised file summarizing and identifying the employees in question that wrote time to IPT codes only.

As Shell properly recognizes, the definition of "Employees" contained in Exhibit G of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement (Integrated Project Team and Technology Sharing) expressly defines "Employees" to include any individual under the employment of any Affiliate of any Party to the Operating Agreement. Therefore, any Employee of a Shell Affiliate that is a member of the Integrated Project Team, is considered an Employee of Shell. The Addendum to Exhibit C of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement expressly incorporates by reference the terms and conditions of Exhibit G (See Addendum to Exhibit C, p.1). Consequently, all wages paid to Shell Affiliates are chargeable in accordance with Section III, Paragraph 2.B. Moreover, Shell has noted that there is a prior course of dealing between CNOOC and Shell regarding audit exceptions for employee charges of less than one day per month, which further supports CNOOC's position. As Shell is aware, a prior course of dealing is "a sequence of previous conduct between the parties to the agreement," which can provide "a common basis of understanding for interpreting their expressions and other conduct" (RESTATEMENT (SECOND) OF CONTRACTS § 223, 1981). Given Shell's longstanding approval of CNOOC's interpretation requiring salaries of Shell's Affiliates to be subject to the time requirement of Section III, Paragraph 2.B(a), the parties have established a course of dealing regarding the interpretation of the Joint Operating Agreement concerning the subject audit exception.

Credit denied. There is no change in the Operator’s stance regarding the JOA interpretation pertaining to IPT. As previously mentioned, the employees identified wrote time to numerous WBS codes, including IPT, Development, and Production WBS codes. 54.description: During the period 05/05/2016 through 05/04/2021 various Appomattox WBS have been allocated a portion of the rig Deepwater Proteus demobilization costs. The demobilization amount charged was determined by applying a demobilization rate of $4,107.34 per day multiplied by the number of days the rig was on location. The demobilization rate was calculated by dividing the Operator's estimation of demobilization costs of $7,500,000.00 by the number of days in the original term, 1,826 (05/05/2016 - 05/04/2021), of the Assignment Agreement between Shell Offshore Inc. (SOI) and Shell EP Wells Equipment Services B.V (SEPWES) for use of the Proteus in the Gulf of Mexico. A new Assignment Agreement was entered into between SOI and SEPWES effective 05/06/2021 with an Assignment Period of 12 months with SOI having four extension options of one year each. Standard industry practice is to true-up the demobilization estimated costs to the actual demobilization costs when demobilization occurs and make appropriate adjustments to the locations served during the assignment term which may have been over or under charged. Since a new Assignment Agreement was entered into, the Proteus was not demobilized, and no actual demobilization costs were incurred by the Operator. Council of Petroleum Accountants Societies (COPAS) in Model Form Interpretation (MFI) 56, Rig-Related Cost states in Section XX, Rig Contract Extensions, "If the Company extends the Rig Contract term, the recommended practice is to treat the Rig Contract extension as a new Rig Contract rather than reallocating the Rig-Related Costs from the inception of the original Rig Contract to the termination date of the Rig Contract extension period." In accordance with COPAS guidelines, a new Rig Contract was established when the new Assignment Agreement was effective 05/06/2021 and since no demobilization costs were actually incurred, the Operator should reverse all demobilization charges made during the original Assignment agreement period and establish a new Demobilization Accumulator using updated demobilization cost estimates and assignment period to be charged to the locations served during the new assignment period. Credit of $6,013,145.76 is requested for the demobilization charges plus 2.5% Development Overhead. Credit Requested $ 6,013,145.76 Overhead $ 150,328.64 Exception Total $ 6,163,474.40
