The Operator is requested to provide the following evidence that a physical inventory was taken:

1. Invitation to the other Non-Operator(s) as required by the Mars UOA Section V.1. (snipped below)
2. The physical inventory report showing the actual stock counts vs. the Blueprint (financial) inventory count
3. The complete transaction detail for all adjustments made as a result of the required physical inventory.

If the Operator cannot provide evidence that a physical inventory was taken and that the Non-Operator was invited, then the charges are not allowable per MFI-40 as cited by the Operator and full credit remains due.

## V. INVENTORIES

The Operator shallmaintaindetailed records of Controllabíe Material.

## I. Periodic laventories, Norice and Representation

- At reasonable intervats, inventories shall be taken by Operator of the Joinr Account Controllable Material, Written notice of intention to take inventory shali be given by Operator at least thirry (30) days before any inventory is to begin so that invenrory shall bind Non-Operators to accept the inventory taken by Operaror.

## II.INTERPRETATION

## First-Time Charges

The model form accounting procedure language imposes the same 24-month adjustment period for a non-operator to request adjustment to the Joint Account as for an operator to make Joint Account adjustments. This ensures that each party may timely close its books for the period(s) beyond the 24-month period allowed for adjustment. There are situations, however, where it is permissible for an operator to book debits or credits to the Joint Account beyond the 24-month period allowed for adjustment, or to recognize the 24-month period may start at different times, depending on the circumstances. Such entries are not considered "adjustments" under the model form language but treated as first-time charges to the Joint Account so that the 24-month limitation on adjustments is not based on when the operator first incurred the cost. Examples of these situations are detailed below.

## A. Physical Inventory

Adjustments resulting from a physical inventory of jointly owned Controllable Material as normally allowed under the provisions of the governing Accounting Procedure are usually permitted beyond the 24-month adjustment period. However, depending on the COPAS model form, adjustments are required to be made within either six months or 12 months of the taking of the physical inventory, or receipt of the non-operator inventory report. Therefore, such adjustments resulting from a physical inventory of jointly owned Controllable Material are an allowable adjustment to the Joint Account after expiration of the 24-month adjustment period to which the adjustment applies, provided they are made within any prescribed period after taking the physical inventory stipulated within the specific Accounting Procedure. Adjustments arising from an inventory of operator-owned Material are subject to the 24-month adjustment period.

Note there may be a potential conflict between the inventory provision which requires inventory adjustments within a certain time after taking the inventory and the 24-month adjustment period in Section I.

The NonOperator previously reviewed this well, determined that it was Closed/TECO. The reconciliation was performed and noted that this part was not used in the destination well either. In accordance with the agreed February 2024 Expense Audit Principles, section 9.b.iii., the reconciliation to the transferred-to well is not clear as it does not show the usage or installation of this part.

9. For materials transferred to another well within the joint account after exception has been identified:
- a. If transferred to an open well, not yet audited,
- i. Once confirmed the materials are transferred, the original exception is closed.
- b. If transferred to a well that is closed and already audited or subject to a current audit,
- i. Technical reports shall be provided, or if already provided, operator shall specify which audit.
- ii. Auditor will review the documents and audit work papers before requesting more information.
7. If reconciliation to transferred well is not clear, exception will remain open as part of original audit where exception was identified.
- iv. A rebuttal will be issued to clarify what remains and operator will focus on only the remaining portion.

The Operator is therefore requested to account for the value of the part using this exception. If the Operator is unable to document that the part was used in any well, then it is requested to credit the Joint Account for the unused part as originally written.

replies.text:
In its previous response the Operator indicated that the part was transferred to another well within the Mars field. The NonOperator previously reviewed this well, determined that it was Closed/TECO. The reconciliation was performed and noted that this part was not used in the destination well either. This recon was provided to the Operator in the previous response by the Non-Operator in a file titled "Exc 53j C.US.MR2.XC.21.001.0943A Recon.xlsx" with that detail.

In accordance with the agreed February 2024 Expense Audit Principles, section 9.b.iii., the reconciliation to the transferred-to well is not clear as it does not show the usage or installation of this part.

9. For materials transferred to another well within the joint account after exception has been identified:
- a. If transferred to an open well, not yet audited,
- i. Once confirmed the materials are transferred, the original exception is closed.
- b. If transferred to a well that is closed and already audited or subject to a current audit,
- i. Technical reports shall be provided, or if already provided, operator shall specify which audit.
- ii. Auditor will review the documents and audit work papers before requesting more information.
7. If reconciliation to transferred well is not clear, exception will remain open as part of original audit where exception was identified.
- iv. A rebuttal will be issued to clarify what remains and operator will focus on only the remaining portion.

The Operator is therefore requested to account for the value of the part using this exception. If the Operator is unable to document that the part was used in any well, then it is requested to credit the Joint Account for the unused part as originally written.

07/18/2023 Update: Document number 131519477 posted for the amount granted.

Partially accepted. Please find attached Shell's comments in the attached spreadsheet.

Credit Denied.

Charges in the amount of $224,442.28 is denied for personnel performing work in accordance with the February 2019 Letter Agreement. See attached file for details. No credit is due to the Joint Account.

Partial credit in the amount of $7,839.68 granted via Document Number 131519477 in July, 2023 business.

[table 1]

The Operator provided no rebuttal/refutation for Mike Buckley and Timothy Fos and is requested to credit the Joint Account $7,839.68 plus 2.5% OH accordingly.

## Additionally:

Adeyemi Akanbi ($3,242.82) - Planning Engineer - he did not charge his time to a Well Maintenance, Facility Maintenance, or TAR AFE, and therefore was not working on those activities as required by the February 2019 Letter Agreement. The Operator is requested to issue credit for the non-chargeable OTL.

Robert Dowdy ($78,549.31) - Systems Engineer - per the Operator's description he was working on Project Management work which is not chargeable in accordance with the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement. The Operator has cited Section 3.1 of the Same, however this work is not required by any regulatory authority. Full credit remains due.

Tom Klepcyk ($36,417.13) - Offshore Engineer Special 5 - The Operator cited the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement section 3.3. However, this individual is not a "planner or scheduler" and is not working on "Well Maintenance, Facility Maintenance, or TAR" as required by Same. Therefore the activities are not chargeable to the Joint Account. Full credit remains due.

Bryan Wick - no longer questioned.

Isaac Yurco ($70,223.17) - Staff Technical Consultant 2 - the Operator stated that he was "...developing inspection strategy and scope to assist with campaign inspections offshore, and integrating them into Risk Based Inspection model for future work scope.". While this work may be necessary, it is not for the benefit of Mars/Olympus but rather the Operator's wider Gulf portfolio (hence usage of the word campaign) and therefore it is not chargeable directly to Mars. Instead it should be charged to all properties in the Gulf. Full credit remains due.

Updated JADE and other details are provided in a file called "Exc 57 Details.xlsx".

Mike Buckley and Timothy Fos:

The partial amount granted was for Mike Buckley and Timothy Fos $7,839.68 plus 2.5% OH. Document number 131519477 posted for the amount granted.

## Additionally:

Adeyemi Akanbi ($3,242.82) - Planning Engineer - Section 3.3 of the February 2019 Letter Agreement explicitly includes Operating Technical Liaison (OTL) activities as chargeable. Adeyemi's work creating and maintaining project schedules for Mars/Olympus projects is an OTL function supporting ongoing operations. Chargeable under OTL provisions; no credit due.

Robert Dowdy ($78,549.31) - Systems Engineer -Robert's activities, writing commissioning/startup procedures and providing operational support, are tied to regulatory compliance and safe startup of subsea systems. Section 3.1 of the Letter Agreement covers Regulatory Activities, and BSEE 250.1916 mandates mechanical integrity and commissioning standards. Work is regulatory-driven and necessary for Mars asset integrity; no credit due.

Tom Klepcyk ($36,417.13) - Offshore Engineer Special 5 - Tom's work on King Embayment recovery and THS repair is remedial maintenance. Section 3.3 of the Letter Agreement classify maintenance as operating costs. These activities restore functionality to Mars subsea equipment and are not discretionary project management.

Isaac Yurco ($70,223.17) - Isaac's scope included developing inspection strategy and analyzing Mars/Olympus inspection results for integration into RBI. While RBI methodology is standardized, the work performed was specific to Mars/Olympus compliance with BSEE 250.1916. Section 3.1 of the Letter Agreement allow charging regulatory compliance costs to the benefiting property. Activities were Mars/Olympus-specific; no credit due.

The Non-Operator offers the following comments:

Adeyemi Akanbi ($3,242.82) - Planning Engineer - The Operator stated that Section 3.3 of the February 2019 Letter Agreement applies. The Non-Operator does not dispute that this is the governing language and reiterates it below:

## 3. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration

OTL is chargeable by the Operator to the joint account for planners, schedulers, and plan execution supportersworking on facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities.

As highlighted in the agreement, Mr. Akanbi must be working on Facility Maintenance, Well Maintenance, or Turnaround activities. Per the Operator's response, he was working on "supporting ongoing operations" which is not in compliance with the highlighted portion of the Agreement and credit remains due.

Robert Dowdy ($78,549.31) - Systems Engineer - Per the Operator's own coding, Mr. Dowdy is doing Project Management work.

[table 1]

Per Section 2. Definition of Technical Employees of the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement, excerpted below, management is not considered to be a Technical Employee and therefore Mr. Dowdy's time is not chargeable for Project Management.

For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include procurement, administration accounting and auditing, pipeline nominations and scheduling, human resources,management, supervision (excluding first level supervision of operational staff which is billable), legal services, handling taxation matters, permitting/regulatory work, land and division order services. Overhead charges are compensation for all costs and expenses associated with such functions, including the salaries or wages plus applicable payroll burdens, benefits, and personal expenses of personnel performing such functions, as well as their office and other support costs.

Full credit remains due.

Tom Klepcyk ($36,417.13) - Offshore Engineer Special 5 - Similar to Mr. Akanbi, the Operator states that section 3.3 of the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement is governing. The Non-Operator does not dispute this, and notes that similar to Mr. Akanbi, Mr. Klepcyk is not working on "Facility Maintenance, Well Maintenance, or Turnaround" as required by the Agreement. Mr. Klepcyk's time was charged to "KE-002 Pontus Emergency Ops Wells" which is not "Facility Maintenance, Well Maintenance or Turnaround" and further supports the Non-Operator's position that his time is not chargeable. Full credit remains due.

Issac Yurco - accepted and no longer questioned.

Credit of $121,346.04 including Overhead remains due.

The Non-Operator has re-reconciled this casing using ITD JADE and finds that the Joint Account is still charged 13,198.59 feet. Per the Operator's provided Recon, 9,521.31 feet were installed, plus thread loss. The Non-Operator does not dispute this installation figure.

Therefore based on the updated recon, using the ITD JADE and the Operator's update installation figure, the Joint Account is due a credit of $396,284.06 plus 2.5% OH.

The Operator is requested to issue the credit to the Joint Account for the unused materials.

Note: The updated recon file accompanies this exception, titled "Exc 60k C.USMR2.PD.19.004.0942A Recon BP Rebuttal 2.xlsx".

0002.description:
The Operator charged the Perdido Joint Account $52,274.74 for CATS Payroll costs which appear to be administrative in nature and covered by OH (SAP support specialists, data reporting techs, etc.). This was the subject of Perdido Information Request 13 issued to the Operator during the fieldwork.

The identified labor does not qualify for direct chargeability under the Billing Standards settlement agreements between the parties, as they have not been adequately and properly documented by the Operator as activities required to comply with regulatory activities, and they have not been identified as Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration whose job function was previously performed offshore/onsite but were relocated onshore. In addition, the identified personnel did not have a job title that enabled the auditor to conclude the personnel possessed special & specific engineering, geological, geophysical or operational skills absent proper documentation being provided by the Operator to support this labor classification.

The Operator is requested to credit the Perdido Joint Account $52,274.74 with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
As per the Settlement Agreements, signed in 2021 and 2022 between Shell and Chevron / BP, and the Exhibit for Agreed OTL Definition and Billing Standards, sections 3.A Regulatory Activity and 3.C Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration, show that both of these individuals are direct chargeable, as the nature of their jobs is technical.

Robert Indelicato's job profile from the staff listing shows he is a CMMS Engineer for Production Operations. As noted in the attached spreadsheet he is within the Maintenance, Reliability and Turnaround job group. His work either qualified for section 3.A of the Billing Standards as regulatory work (as noted by the CFR codes) or section 3.C for maintenance and turnaround work related to SAP support during these activities.

Tracey Champagne's job profile from the staff listing shows she is a CMMS Support for Maintenance. As noted in the attached spreadsheet she is within the Maintenance, Reliability and Turnaround job group. Her work either qualified for section 3.A of the Billing Standards as regulatory work (as noted by the CFR codes) or section 3.C for maintenance and turnaround work related to SAP support during these activities.

No credit is due.

0003.short_description: COUA - Project/OPEX Matrix - CBOH - Offsite Tech - CATS Labor
0003.description:
The Operator charged the Perdido Joint Account $157,928.70 for CATS Payroll costs which appear to be coding errors. Upon review of Heli Logs and POBs, the employees were working at other locations.

This was the subject of Perdido Information Request 12, which the Operator responded, "The majority of the charges in this IR, show the Perdido CATS time-writing was at a different period of time as to when the employees traveled to other assets. Their time-writing was for regulatory work as shown by the CFR codes noted in column K or planners and schedulers. As per the Settlement Agreements, signed in 2021 and 2022 between Shell and Chevron / BP, and their applicable Exhibit for Agreed OTL Definition and Billing Standards, sections 3.A and 3.C show that both of these categories are direct chargeable. Thanks."

Upon review of the response spreadsheet provided by the Operator, there was no substantiation that the particular time charged was for the Joint Account and not for other properties as noted in the workpapers provided. According to the agreements regulatory work will be charged to the joint account provided such charges are pursuant to an approved AFE which the regulatory activities must be adequately and properly documented by the Operator, identifying the specific activity of the individuals and will reference specific program elements as described in the Federal Register. None of the AFE's being charged in this exception reflect this regulatory designation prescribed by the settlement agreement. In addition, no additional support was provided to reflect that the work being performed by the personnel identified as Planners & Schedulers as part of this exception was performing a function that was previously performed offshore.

The Operator is requested to credit the Perdido Joint Account $157,928.70 with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:

0012.short_description: COUA - Project - CBOH - Offsite Tech - HAZOP Actions Engineer Study (2020-2022)
0012.description:
On December 1 & 21, 2020, Chevron responded to the Operator that the costs associated with Perdido HAZOP Actions Engineer Study, while related to HAZOP, was for engineering and project management costs covered by overhead. Per the Perdido COUA referenced in the letter, overhead will cover any professional or contract services provided by technical personnel that are offsite. It remains Chevron's position that Shell cannot charge out any of these engineering and project management costs described in the AFE.

The AFE provided did not conform to the requirements described in the letter agreement dated October 13, 2021 that commenced for charges beginning January 1, 2019. In this agreement it states the following as it relates to OTL-Chargeable Activities (Attachment I, paragraph 3.A Regulatory Activity), " ...OTL charges related to the above regulatory activities must be adequately and properly documented by the Operator, identifying the specific activity of the individual(s), and will reference specific program elements as described in the Federal Register. Following execution of this Settlement Agreement, this will be noted separately in the AFE document..."

The attached AFE is lacking documentation to the specific program elements as described in the Federal Register that the AFE is intending to address.

The Operator is requested to credit the Silvertip Joint Account $30,915.59 ($27,603.20 plus overhead of $3,312.39) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
The AFE sent in December 2020 was an 'information only AFE' as it was under the $300,000 threshold as noted in the Perdido COUA, Article 6, section 6.2 AFEs, '… the Operator will not make any single expenditure or undertake any activity or operation costing three Hundred Thousand Dollars ($300,000.00) or more, unless an AFE has been included in a proposal for an activity or operation … '. This Information Only AFE was total gross amount of $232,500 for the estimated costs associated with the Perdido HAZOP Actions Engineer Study and the Operator was furnishing written information describing the expenditure to each of the Participating Parties.

The AFE was provided in December of 2020 which was before the signing of the Settlement Agreements noted by the Auditor. The quote from the Settlement Agreement provided by the Auditor was not the full paragraph which is included here for ease of reference. ' OTL charges related to the above regulatory activities must be adequately and properly documented by the Operator, identifying the specific activity of the individual(s), and will reference specific program elements as described in the Federal Register. Following execution of this Settlement Agreement, this will be noted separately in the AFE document where applicable .'

The work performed by Keystone Engineering Inc was done to comply with HSSE control framework and OSHA 1910 regulatory requirements to address assigned HAZOP action items under CFR 250.1910 which is direct billable as per the Settlement Agreement Billing Standards, Exhibit C, 3.A Regulatory Activity.

No credit is due.

0013.description:
The Silvertip Joint Account was charged $348,849.43 on multiple AFE's related the replacement of ESP (Electric Subsea Pump) which was billed at the Operating Overhead rate of 13.0% in lieu of the appropriate $72,665.34 Development Overhead rate of 2.5% as the AFE's indicate the replacements are not similar, but rather an upgrade with increased performance and output than what was originally installed.

Per the operating agreement Section III (Overhead), 2 (Application of Overhead- Percentage basis), a.5

- a. Development shall include all costs in connection with:
1. drilling, redrilling, plugging back or deepening of any or all wells
2. workover operations requiring a period of fifteen(15) consecutive work days or more on a well,
3. preliminary expenditures necessary in preparation for drilling,
4. expenditures incurred in abandoning when the well is not completed as a producer,
5. original construction or installation of fixed assets, expansion of fixed assets and any other project clearly discernible as a fixed asset, except Major Construction as defined in Paragraph 3 of Section Ill

The Operator is requested to credit the Silvertip Joint Account $276,184.09 with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
As per our regulatory SME (subject matter expert), ESP's are not classified as a well, as they have no API assigned to them. They are classified as production equipment thus are subject to the agreed upon appropriate Operating overhead rate. The replacement/maintenance of the ESP since inception (post first capitalization of first replacement) has always been b illed as an operating expense and not an 'upgrade'. In addition, there is only one type of ESP on the market.

The section of the Operating Agreement Section III (Overhead), 2 (Application of Overhead - Percentage basis) quoted by the Auditor, is related to wells and is not applicable to an ESP (as noted above).

As per the Senior Finance Advisor, ESP installations are considered as Facility Maintenance activities as the ESPs have required changeouts every 1-3 years since Perdido startup. The only change was in Shell's internal accounting treatment in complying with IFRS16 lease interpretations that they are to be treated as a Right of Use Asset which sits on the balance sheet therefore requiring us to capitalize internally. There has been no change to overhead application or proposal through the COUA as a maintenance activity. This is the same consistent message that has been conveyed to Chevron Finance. If the Auditor requires further clarification, it may be best placed to seek resolution through the Finance and Commercial teams.

No credit is due.

0002.short_description: COUA - Project - CBOH - Offsite Tech - HAZOP Actions Engineer Study (2020-2022)

Per the Perdido COUA referenced in the letter, overhead will cover any professional or contract services provided by technical personnel that are offsite. It remains Chevron's position that Shell cannot charge out any of these engineering and project management costs described in the AFE.

The AFE provided did not conform to the requirements described in the letter agreement dated October 13, 2021 that commenced for charges beginning January 1, 2019. In this agreement it states the following as it relates to OTL-Chargeable Activities (Attachment I, paragraph 3.A Regulatory Activity), "...OTL charges related to the above regulatory activities must be adequately and properly documented by the Operator, identifying the specific activity of the individual(s), and will reference specific program elements as described in the Federal Register. Following execution of this Settlement Agreement, this will be noted separately in the AFE document..."

The attached AFE is lacking documentation to the specific program elements as described in the Federal Register that the AFE is intending to address.

The Operator is requested to credit the Tobago Joint Account $6,183.14 ($5,520.68 plus overhead of $662.46) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
The AFE sent in December 2020 was an 'information only AFE' as it was under the $300,000 threshold as noted in the Perdido COUA, Article 6, section 6.2 AFEs, '… the Operator will not make any single expenditure or undertake any activity or operation costing three Hundred Thousand Dollars ($300,000.00) or more, unless an AFE has been included in a proposal for an activity or operation … '. This Information Only AFE was total gross amount of $232,500 for the estimated costs associated with the Perdido HAZOP Actions Engineer Study and the Operator was furnishing written information describing the expenditure to each of the Participating Parties.

The AFE was provided in December of 2020 which was before the signing of the Settlement Agreements noted by the Auditor. The quote from the Settlement Agreement provided by the Auditor was not the full paragraph which is included here for ease of reference. ' OTL charges related to the above regulatory activities must be adequately and properly documented by the Operator, identifying the specific activity of the individual(s), and will reference specific program elements as described in the Federal Register. Following execution of this Settlement Agreement, this will be noted separately in the AFE document where applicable .'

The work performed by Keystone Engineering Inc was done to comply with HSSE control framework and OSHA 1910 regulatory requirements to address assigned HAZOP action items under CFR 250.1910 which is direct billable as per the Settlement Agreement Billing Standards, Exhibit C, 3.A Regulatory Activity.

No credit is due.

0003.description:
The Tobago Joint Account was charged $47,785.13 on multiple AFE's related the replacement of ESP (Electric Subsea Pump) which was billed at the Operating Overhead rate of 13.0% in lieu of the appropriate $9,953.64 Development Overhead rate of 2.5% as the AFE's indicate the replacements are not similar, but rather an upgrade with increased performance and output than what was originally installed.

Per the operating agreement Section III (Overhead), 2 (Application of Overhead- Percentage basis), a.5

- a. Development shall include all costs in connection with:
1. drilling, redrilling, plugging back or deepening of any or all wells
2. workover operations requiring a period of fifteen(15) consecutive work days or more on a well,
3. preliminary expenditures necessary in preparation for drilling,
4. expenditures incurred in abandoning when the well is not completed as a producer,
5. original construction or installation of fixed assets, expansion of fixed assets and any other project clearly discernible as a fixed asset, except Major Construction as defined in Paragraph 3 of Section Ill

The Operator is requested to credit the Tobago Joint Account $37,831.49 with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
As per our regulatory SME (subject matter expert), ESP's are not classified as a well, as they have no API assigned to them. They are classified as production equipment thus are subject to the agreed upon appropriate Operating overhead rate. The replacement/maintenance of the ESP since inception (post first capitalization of first replacement) has always been billed as an o perating expense and not an 'upgrade'. In addition, there is only one type of ESP on the market.

The section of the Operating Agreement Section III (Overhead), 2 (Application of Overhead - Percentage basis) quoted by the Auditor, is related to wells and is not applicable to an ESP (as noted above).

As per the Senior Finance Advisor, ESP installations are considered as Facility Maintenance activities as the ESPs have required changeouts every 1-3 years since Perdido startup. The only change was in Shell 's internal accounting treatment in complying with IFRS16 lease interpretations that they are to be treated as a Right of Use Asset which sits on the balance sheet therefore requiring us to capitalize internally. There has been no change to overhead application or proposal through the COUA as a maintenance activity. This is the same consistent message that has been conveyed to Chevron Finance. If the Auditor requires further clarification, it may be best placed to seek resolution through the Finance and Commercial teams.

No credit is due.

0014.description:
The Operator charged the Tobago Joint Account $1,310.55 for CATS Payroll costs which are not chargeable under the terms of the Settlement Agreement.

The Operator was requested to explain these charges in Perdido Information Request 14, to which they responded, "Upon review of the spreadsheet and information provided, it classifies personnel according to the work order/cost object/posting object description. These cost object descriptions are part of SAP master data created when the cost object is set up; i.e. it is the "description" field within SAP. This master data does not provide a description of the specific activity performed for the Joint Account, nor an indication that the individual performed work on behalf of the Joint Account. For example, if the individual timewriter was actually spending an increment as small as 0.02HR of time (1.2 minutes) working on an activity for the Joint Account, as it may not be possible to spend such an infinitesimal amount of time working on behalf of the Joint Account."

According to the agreements regulatory work will be charged to the joint account provided such charges are pursuant to an approved AFE which the regulatory activities must be adequately and properly documented by the Operator, identifying the specific activity of the individuals and will reference specific program elements as described in the Federal Register. None of the AFE's being charged in this exception reflect this regulatory designation prescribed by the settlement agreement. In addition, no additional support was provided to reflect that the work being performed by the personnel identified as Planners & Schedulers as part of this exception were performing a function that was previously performed offshore.

The Operator is requested to credit the Tobago Joint Account $1,310.55 ($1,149.20 plus overhead of $161.35) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:

As per the Settlement Agreement, signed in 2021 between Shell and Chevron, and the Exhibit for Agreed OTL Definition and Billing Standards, the nature of their roles is technical. Their work either qualified for section 3.A of the Billing Standards as regulatory work (as noted by the CFR codes) or section 3.C for facility or well maintenance operations.

040.short_description: SIEP Employees – Less Than Eight Hours Billed in a Month
040.description: The Addendum to Exhibit "C", Accounting Procedure Statement of Clarification and Intent provides in its clarification to Section III, Paragraph 2.B.a "Services Rendered by Operator's Employees": "Salaries will be charged to the Joint Account based upon actual days worked only when such time totals at least one day or more per month that is devoted to the Major Construction project." Exhibit "G" attached to, and made part of the Prospect Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement provides in its Section 1.6 Employees: "Employees shall mean any individual under the employment of any party to this Operating Agreement including any Affiliate or contractor which may represent any Party hereunder." As Shell properly recognizes, the definition of "Employees" contained in Exhibit G of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement (Integrated Project Team and Technology Sharing) expressly defines "Employees" to include any individual under the employment of any Affiliate of any Party to the Operating Agreement. Therefore, any Employee of a Shell Affiliate that is a member of the Integrated Project Team, is considered an Employee of Shell. The Addendum to Exhibit C of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement expressly incorporates by reference the terms and conditions of Exhibit G (See Addendum to Exhibit C, p.1). Consequently, all wages paid to Shell Affiliates are chargeable in accordance with Section III, Paragraph 2.B. Moreover, Shell has noted that there is a prior course of dealing between CNOOC and Shell regarding audit exceptions for employee charges of less than one day per month, which further supports CNOOC's position. As Shell is aware, a prior course of dealing is "a sequence of previous conduct between the parties to the agreement," which can provide "a common basis of understanding for interpreting their expressions and other conduct" (RESTATEMENT (SECOND) OF CONTRACTS § 223, 1981). Given Shell's longstanding approval of CNOOC's interpretation requiring salaries of Shell's Affiliates to be subject to the time requirement of Section III, Paragraph 2.B(a), the parties have established a course of dealing regarding the interpretation of the Joint Operating Agreement concerning the subject audit exception. The audit worksheet 'Exc 40.2\_Pvt Hrs < 8 Hrs', provided herein, presents JADE analysis and identification of 50 SIEP employees charging a total of 510.75 hours to major construction projects during the service period of January through December 2022 with those hours reported totaling less than 1 full day (8 hours) in each month. The Operator is requested to credit the various WBS' identified in 'Exc 40.3\_Pivot\_WBS' in the amount of $176,761.00, plus 2.0% Major Construction Overhead.

replies.text: Credit denied. Each of the WBS codes on this exception are Major Construction AFEs (as noted by the auditor in the exception summary), however, they are not part of the IPT. The auditor is referencing Exhibit “G” (Integrated Project Team and Technology Sharing) as the basis for defining employee. Exhibit “G” is for the Integrated Project Team and is not applicable to all Major Construction projects. The 8-hour monthly limitation for Major Construction projects does not apply to Employees or Affiliates. The Addendum to Exhibit C for Section III Overhead 2.B points out the distinction between services rendered by a. Employees of Participants and b. Affiliate and Drafting Services. Neither Paragraph “a” for employees nor paragraph 'b" for affiliates reference of at least one full day during a given month. See screen shots below. Accounting Procedure Section III Overhead 2.B:

052.short_description: SIEP Contractors – Less Than 8 Hours Billed in a Month
052.description: The Addendum to Exhibit "C", Accounting Procedure Statement of Clarification and Intent provides in its clarification to Section III, Paragraph 2.B.a "Services Rendered by Operator's Employees": "Salaries will be charged to the Joint Account based upon actual days worked only when such time totals at least one day or more per month that is devoted to the Major Construction project." Exhibit "G" attached to, and made part of the Prospect Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement provides in its Section 1.6 Employees: "Employees shall mean any individual under the employment of any party to this Operating Agreement including any Affiliate or contractor which may represent any Party hereunder." As Shell properly recognizes, the definition of "Employees" contained in Exhibit G of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement (Integrated Project Team and Technology Sharing) expressly defines "Employees" to include any individual under the employment of any Affiliate of any Party to the Operating Agreement. Therefore, any Employee of a Shell Affiliate that is a member of the Integrated Project Team, is considered an Employee of Shell. The Addendum to Exhibit C of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement expressly incorporates by reference the terms and conditions of Exhibit G (See Addendum to Exhibit C, p.1). Consequently, all wages paid to Shell Affiliates are chargeable in accordance with Section III, Paragraph 2.B. Moreover, Shell has noted that there is a prior course of dealing between CNOOC and Shell regarding audit exceptions for employee charges of less than one day per month, which further supports CNOOC's position. As Shell is aware, a prior course of dealing is "a sequence of previous conduct between the parties to the agreement," which can provide "a common basis of understanding for interpreting their expressions and other conduct" (RESTATEMENT (SECOND) OF CONTRACTS § 223, 1981). Given Shell's longstanding approval of CNOOC's interpretation requiring salaries of Shell's Affiliates to be subject to the time requirement of Section III, Paragraph 2.B(a), the parties have established a course of dealing regarding the interpretation of the Joint Operating Agreement concerning the subject audit exception. The audit worksheet 'Exc 52.2\_Pvt Hrs < 8 Hrs', provided herein, presents JADE analysis and identification of six SIEP employees charging a total of 61.0 hours to major construction projects during the service period of January through December 2022 with those hours reported totaling less than 1 full day (8 hours) in each month. The Operator is requested to credit the various WBS' identified in 'Exc 52.3\_Pivot\_WBS' in the amount of $12,510.00, plus 2.0% Major Construction Overhead.

replies.text: Credit denied. This claim is associated with IPT time for Affiliates working less than 8 hours in a given month. The Exhibit ‘G’ clause referenced by the auditor is only one of the sections that must be referenced. The Operator agrees the definition in section “1.6 Employees” does reference Affiliates, however, the Addendum to Exhibit C for Section III Overhead 2.C points out the distinction between services rendered by Employees of Participants and b. Affiliate and Drafting Services. Paragraph “a” for employees has the reference of at least one full day during a given month, but the Affiliate paragraph does not. So even though Affiliate is mentioned under the definition of Employees under Exhibit G, the clarification and distinction in the Accounting procedure gives the direction of how to charge for each. The “one full day per a given month is applicable to Employees only, and not Affiliates. Screen shot below is an excerpt from Exhibit “G” regarding IPT. It defines Employees, but it also lists in Section 2.0 the distinction of Employee Staff contributing 2.1.1 and Affiliate and Contract Staff 2.1.2. The ‘less than 8 hours’ provision is only applicable to "SERVICES RENDERED BY OPERATOR'S EMPLOYEES" on IPT WBS codes. Accounting Procedure Section III Overhead 2.C:

attachments: Exc 52_SIEP Contractors - Less Than 8 Hours Billed in a Month.xlsx

065.short_description: Charges not for the Joint Account – TCJA Rebills
065.description: maintains the position that Transocean’s estimated charges referencing the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (TCJA) should not be charged to the Joint Account. The estimated charges do not specify the tax provision in the TCJA or provide any detailed calculations. CNOOC’s position remains that the TCJA tax provisions such as the Base Erosion Anti-Abuse Tax (BEAT) relate to the federal tax level for all US business and do not directly increase the cost of performing drilling services. If BEAT is interpreted as a “Change in Tax Law” applicable to the contract provision (see contract excerpt below), the decrease in tax costs resulting from greatly reduced income tax rates and bonus depreciation would also be applicable. The allocation of BEAT only considers the increased cost of a change in tax law and ignores a significant reduction to costs from lower corporate income tax rates and bonus depreciation. The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 not only created the BEAT tax, but also decreased the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21%, and at its highest allowed 100% first year depreciation on tangible assets for 2017-2022). If corporate level taxes are deemed applicable, it is inconsistent to recover tax costs associated with BEAT, but not also adjust for other tax law changes that reduce costs for the contractor, Transocean. For example, the income tax rate decreases from 35% to 21% was not adjusted in favor of Shell (i.e., reduced day rate). The contract provision (excerpt below) does not appear to be consistently applied over time. Assuming the rebill is related to BEAT as it was in 2019, it is calculated at a federal level, additional support is needed to evaluate the reasonableness of the allocation of the tax. Many tax assumptions and variables are examined to arrive at taxable income (the starting point of the BEAT calculation) and relying on an estimate at mid-year is not accurate. At a minimum, a true-up from the estimate to the actual tax rebill incurred related to Proteus in 2022 is required. Additionally, per the 2022 Annual Report (Form 10k) filed by Transocean Ltd and Subsidiaries, no taxes related to BEAT were paid in 2022. We request credit in the amount of $582,228.00 plus 2.5% Development overhead for these incorrectly billed charges

0004.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $306,177.22 in TRACK related charges during both audit years. In Information Request 002 the Operator was requested to provide copies of the Track Reports for examination. In their response, the Operator provided a PDF dump for all vendors for the whole Gulf of Mexico for both years in question.

The Operator was subsequently requested to provide the reports in a more usable format; i.e. only charges relevant to the current audit, or reports in excel format that are able to be analyzed using automated processes. The Operator did not provide these by the end of fieldwork.

The Operator is again requested to provide the TRACK reports corresponding to only these specific charges for the Auditor's review (i.e. not the whole GoM or multiple other assets), or in an analyzable format such as excel. If the Operator is not able to support the charges with usable data, they are requested to credit the Joint Account $306,177.22 plus OH for the unsupported charges.

replies.text:
Instructions were provided to filter the JADE by vendor and use materiality and statistical sampling to review the charges of Information Request 002. The Operator followed these instructions and completed the review process in about 2 hours. If materials were selected, an invoice can be pulled from the Track system, which the auditor has access to and instructions for. For maintenance labor, samples from the initial Track report can be reconciled with the JADE. Names can also be verified against the POB report/flight log to ensure the person was on the platform and used the correct charge code for their time. Please see the attached file for details.

Therefore, the credit claim of $306,177.22 plus OH for the unsupported charges has been denied.

replies.text:
Credit denied.

The charges of $1,882,421.00 in question are for the second and final milestone payments for the XT, XT CAP, and Hanger Refurbishment paid to TechnipFMC for their Deepwater Subsea Engineering Services.

As explained during the audit fieldwork, the Operator optimizes resources and reduces costs through the following process: 1) Farming Subsea Hardware: Hardware from non-producing wells, such as chokes, valves, and other subsea equipment, is retrieved.

- 2) Refurbishment and Reinstallation: The retrieved hardware is refurbished or repaired and then reinstalled on other wells that require functioning equipment.

The Crosby CA-7 well project is utilizing a refurbished tree system originally from the Europa A6 well. According to the process, XTs are refurbished under the name of the well from which they came and are not renamed until reinstalled on a new well, in this case, the Crosby CA-7 Side-tracked well. Therefore, Crosby CA-7 received the necessary hardware in time to meet the installation schedule and is charged for the subsea engineering services related to the XT refurbishment from Europa A6 for Europa A3.

The project was completed in 2023. The refurbished equipment has been installed in the Crosby CA-7 well and assigned new serial and equipment numbers associated with the Crosby CA-7

0011.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $64,766.02 for Storage costs on 4 FMC Technip invoices according to the attached JADE lines. According to the Feb 19 2019 Letter Agreement, Staging and Warehouse (storage) facilities are chargeable for approved project.

In Information Request 26 the Operator was requested to provide evidence (signed AFE, etc.) that the project these costs have been charged to was approved by BP, in accordance with the aforementioned letter agreement.

- Third Party Staging, Warehouse Facilities – For approved projects, the labor and facilities costs directly incurred for preservation, maintenance, and staging for jointly owned equipment or materials for Joint Operations may be charged by the Operator to the Joint Account as a direct charge consistent with COPAS Model Form Interpretation #21. The chargeable amounts are limited to periods of six (6) months or less occurring prior to execution of the project. After use of the material or equipment for the Joint Operation is completed, the equipment or material storage costs will no longer be charged to the Joint Account unless the Parties have agreed in writing that the material or equipment is a critical spare.

The Operator was not able to provide evidence of these costs being part of an approved project and therefore the Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $64,766.02 plus 13% OH for these storage costs.

The charges in question are for High Performance Computing (HPC) services, which are calculated based on the cost of leased HPC hardware in the Shell MegaCenter, support staff, power, real estate lease, and other factors. These costs are recovered on a project-by-project basis according to the objectives and compute needs of seismic processing projects. Seismic processing costs are divided between staff and HPC based on project objectives, technology requirements to address geophysical problems, and previous analogous projects. replies.text:
Charges totaling $382,996.20 are associated with journal entries under SAP document numbers 130052082 and 131232804. These entries pertain to the rig NGT2's accumulator costs for mobilization, upgrade, and demobilization.

The $239,426.39 posted under SAP document no. 130052082 represents the trueup of the NGT2 rig's accumulator costs related to mobilization and upgrade.

The non-operator used 1705 days from January 1, 2019, to September 1, 2023, from the Noble Fleet status report for day rate calculations. This is incorrect because it fails to recognize that 1) The rig was not mobilized to GoM until July 2019, 2) The rig had incurred a number of days between 26th July and 10 October 2019 for intake and upgrades before it could begin work in the GoM and 3) It began drilling for the first well on 11th October 2019,

It is correct to use 477 days from the first well drilled on October 11, 2019, to January 29, 2021, as a basis to calculate the day rate on budget before actuals were available. Since the NGT2 rig was released on January 25, 2021, which was four days earlier than the budget, the allocation period has been adjusted down to 473 days for true up entries.

The $143,569.81 posted under SAP document no. 131232804 pertains to the NGT2 rig's demobilization accumulator. Theallocation period from September 9, 2013, to November 4, 2023 (totaling 3709 days) was used to calculate the day rate of$2,022.11 for amortization.

The true up entries for accumulator costs (mobilization, upgrade and demobilization) have been correctly calculated. The creditclaims of $382,996.20 plus overhead (OH) are denied.

The Non-Operator specifically did not include any Noble rigs in the 2019 Settlement Agreement with regards to the Accumulator beginning or ending date. The intent of the parties during settlement was that the accumulator accounts would be unwound over the full rig term (1705 days) vs what was done here. This is in accordance with MFI-56 Section VIII Mobilization and XVI Demobilization which state that the costs "...benefit all the properties utilizing the Rig during the term of the Rig Contract ". All properties includes a broader group than just a particular basin (i.e. Gulf of Mexico) as any other property drilled by the rig benefits, regardless of location.

## VIII. MOBILIZATION

Mobilization costs are those costs incurred to move a Rig to an initial location agreed upon by the Company and drilling contractor at the commencement of a Rig Contract; for example, moving a deepwater Rig from a shipyard located in Korea to a lease located in the Gulf of Mexico or moving an onshore Rig to the initial Area of Operation. Common deepwater Mobilization costs include, but are not limited to, preparing for Mobilization, the Rig rate, towing costs, assisting tug costs, staffing/training costs and insurance costs. Onshore Mobilization costs include, but are not limited to, the Rig rate, trucking and insurance costs.

Under some Rig Contracts, the Company is required to pay a Mobilization fee at the time the Rig Contract is executed to compensate the drilling contractor for moving the Rig to the agreed-upon location. Under other Rig Contracts, the Company is charged for the actual Mobilization costs incurred by the drilling contractor, or pays the Rig moving costs directly to the vendors that carry out specific Mobilization tasks. The Mobilization fee or costs are part of the overall compensation due the drilling contractor or other vendors, as applicable, and the Mobilization benefits all the properties utilizing the Rig during the term of the Rig Contract.

## XVI. DEMOBILIZATION

Demobilization costs are those costs to move a Rig to an agreed upon location at the conclusion of a Rig Contract and, in some cases, remove equipment from the Rig. Demobilization costs may include, but are not limited to, costs to prepare for a move, towing costs, including assist tug costs, trucking and labor to dismantle equipment and stack the Rig. Some Rig Contracts require the Company to pay the drilling contractor a pre-determined Demobilization fee at the end of the contract. At other times, the Operator may be charged for the actual Demobilization costs incurred by the drilling contractor. If another Company operating in the same area hires the Rig immediately following the end of the Rig Contract, there might not be a Demobilization cost or fee because the next Company hiring the Rig pays to move the Rig to its property.

## Demobilization Costs Paid for by the Drilling Contractor

Demobilization costs are part of the overall compensation due the drilling contractor and benefit all properties utilizing the Rig during the term of the contract, barring any unusual or extraordinary circumstances. When the drilling contractor pays such costs, it includes them in the total value of the Rig and the rate(s) it bills to the Company. In this case, the drilling contractor's rate is chargeable to the joint account under the Services provisions.

The Operator is requested to correct the allocation days and issue credit as initially requested.

02.description: The Operator charged the Vito Joint Account $42,841,984.27 in company labor provided by the Operator’s affiliate Shell International Exploration & Production’s Projects and Technology group. In addition, the Operator has applied 2% to 2.5% overhead fees to these affiliate services amounting to $865,149.93. The addendum to Vito’s 1986 Accounting Procedure (non-PTAP) states the following under provision d., (ii) in short: *"The Major Construction rates provided in Exhibit "C", Section III, Paragraph 2.C [If the Operator forms an Integrated Project Team and charges its costs directly to the Joint Account] shall provide compensation to the Operator for all personnel...and other support services provided by the Operator. Such rate [2%] shall be applied to the total cost (gross) incurred by the Joint Account* *excluding Affiliate charges* *."* The purpose of the last sentence in the above statement is to prevent the Operator from billing the Joint Account an additional layer of overhead because overhead components are already rolled into SIEP’s flat hourly rates hence the word “all-inclusive”. Nevertheless, and regardless of where the SIEP affiliate charges land, e.g., Major Construction project, Development project, Operating project, etc. a percentage overhead fee should not be applied to these affiliate services. The legal definition of an all-inclusive hourly rate is defined as follows: *“An hourly rate comprised of all direct and indirect costs including, but not limited to,* *overhead* *, fee or profit, clerical support, travel expenses, per diem, safety equipment, materials, supplies, managerial support, and all documents, forms, and reproductions thereof, portal-to-portal expenses and per diem expenses such as food.”* The partner should not incur overhead fees from both the parent company and SIEP. 03.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged $17,473,350.64 from Shell EP Wells Equipment Services, B.V. (Shell EPWells) in August 2021 to rebill rig costs and allocate to all eight wells drilled. Of that amount, $16,882,310.02 rebilled for the services of the Deepwater Poseidon Rig. A review of the invoices revealed that Shell EP Wells marked up the invoices totaling $15,319,922.49 received from Transocean Poseidon Opco, Inc. The Vito Accounting Procedure and Addendum do not explicitly allow the Operator to charge costs from Affiliates for 3rd party rig services in excess of actual costs. There are no provisions in the agreements allowing markup on pass through vendor charges. MFI 18 addresses charges to affiliates in its Interpretation: "The purpose of the Labor, Materials and “Equipment and Facilities” provisions in the COPAS Accounting Procedure forms is to assure the Operator’s employees, material purchased from outside sources and any equipment or facilities which are owned by the Operator and serve the Joint Property are charged to the Joint Account at actual cost, without a mark-up. ....1. The Related Entity must either historically or currently have conducted a substantial amount of its business with companies other than the Operator or other Related Entities. ...The Related Entity should not merely serve as a vehicle for rebilling services or products provided by unrelated companies." The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account a total of $1,601,447.22 ($1,562,387.53 plus 2.5% Drilling overhead of $39,059.69) for 3rd party invoice mark-up not allowed. Amount Claimed: $1,601,447.22

replies.text: Credit denied. The invoices in question are from 2018, reclassed in 2021 as part of the "Reclass Batch Set Costs to Vito Wells". Note that a similar exception was taken on the 2019 audit (Ex #04), with the Operator's reply from that audit provided again below: To leverage its market position and negotiating capability, Shell Exploration and Production Wells Equipment Services B.V. (SEPWES), contracts for drilling rigs on a global basis. SEPWES contracted with Transocean for the use of the Deepwater Poseidon drilling rig in September 2012. When a Shell operating company, such as Shell Offshore Inc. (SOI), needs a drilling rig, the operating company can then look to procure a rig through SEPWES. Article 5.1 of the Vito UOA gives SOI, as Operator, the exclusive right to conduct all operations (including execution of drilling contracts) in the Contract Area. Article 5.3 of the UOA allows SOI, as Operator, to have all drilling operations conducted by a qualified and responsible independent contractor (such as Transocean) employed under a competitive contract. In April 2014, SOI contracted with SEPWES to use of the Deepwater Poseidon in the U.S. GOM. In order to comply with arm’s length pricing for intragroup charges as required by the U.S. transfer pricing provisions in Section 482 of the Internal Revenue Code and Chapters 1 and 7 of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (“OECD”) Transfer Pricing Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises, SEPWES’s assignment to SOI had to be an “arm’s length” transaction based on prevailing market rates at the time of the assignment. As a result of the timing difference and normal market fluctuations between the Transocean/SEPWES contract and the SEPWES/SOI assignment, the dayrate in the SEPWES/Transocean contract ($477,168 per day) is different than the dayrate in the SOI/SEPWES contract ($533,169 per day). Significantly, SOI, as Vito Operator, is charging the Vito Joint Account the exact same rate ($533,169 per day) that SOI pays for use of the rig. The market rate for the Deepwater Poseidon rig assignment from SEPWES to SOI was determined using independent benchmarking data, which is attached hereto as Appendix A, for similar drilling rigs in the U.S. GOM at the time of the assignment. Therefore, the SEPWES/SOI assignment complies with the competitiveness requirement set forth in Section 5.3 of the Vito UOA. Equinor’s audit exception focuses almost entirely on COPAS MFI 18, which addresses “markups” charged by affiliated companies. An example of a markup would be if ABC 1 Oil procured a vessel from XYZ Boat for $100 a day, but then invoiced its affiliate, ABC 2 Oil, for $100 a day plus a 10% overlay/upcharge charge for the use of the vessel. The dayrate that SEPWES charged to SOI was based on market dayrates at the time of the SEPWES / SOI contract. The rate that SEPWES charged to SOI does not include an overlay or upcharge. It is not a markup. The SEPWES / SOI contract was not a “vehicle for rebilling.” For those reasons, the rig charges comply with the provisions of Vito UOA and the guidance provided by MFI 18. Additionally, it is important to note that SEPWES bears the risk of market fluctuation. While the prevailing market rate at the time of the SEPWES/SOI assignment (April 2014) was higher than the market rate when the SEPWES/Transocean contract was executed (September 2012), it could have been the other way around with a lower transfer price resulting from downward market fluctuations. This risk is highlighted by the recent Blacktip appraisal well AFE that SOI sent to Equinor on February 18, 2020. SOI, as Blacktip Operator, is using the Noble Globetrotter II rig (NGT II) to drill the Blacktip well. The NGT II is also on assignment from SEPWES to SOI, however, during the period between the SEPWES / Noble contract and the SEPWES / SOI assignment for the NGT II, the rig rates moved downward. As a result, the SEPWES / SOI assignment has a lower rate than the SEPWES / Noble contract. In that instance, in compliance with transfer pricing laws and the Blacktip operating agreement, SOI is charging Equinor the lower day rate contained in the SEPWES / SOI assignment for the NGT II. SOI’s decision to contract for a drilling rig through SEPWES in no way harmed Equinor. Had SOI elected to go to market to procure a rig, rather than looking to SEPWES, SOI would have obtained a rig for a similar base dayrate (see the market rate information attached hereto as Appendix A). Equinor was not damaged by the SOI/SEPWES arrangement because the dayrate under the SOI/SEPWES assignment was consistent with prevailing market rates at the time of the assignment. In any event, SOI, as Vito Operator, is charging the Vito Joint Account the exact same rate ($533,169 per day) that SOI pays for use of the rig in full compliance with the Vito UOA. 19.short_description: P&T Contractors charged at Affiliate Rate
19.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged $9,751,434.61 P&T labor for 24 contractors from 12 suppliers at the affiliate flat rate. The affiliate labor charges were manually adjusted from the SIEP invoices to replace the original invoice rates with the escalated affiliate rate of $367 per hour. These contractors are not on the consolidated P&T staff listing but on the contractor listing. Their services were billed at the affiliate flat rates instead of the actual cost as listed on the affiliate invoices. The total amount charged to the Joint Account from these contractors is $9,740,891.97 for 26,513.5 hours. The actual costs based on the SIEP invoices is $5,061,735.00, resulted in an overcharge of $4,679,156.97 at the higher flat rates. Information request No. 71 was submitted requesting the Operator to provide contracts with the suppliers and contractor job descriptions and timesheet. The information request remains open at the end of the field work. These personnel are contractors from various vendors including GATE, NES Global, RISK bytes, Global Edge, Worley Group, EDG, Intertek, SGS North America and Nextsource. The Accounting Procedure, section 5. Services, allows “the cost of contract services, equipment, and utilities used in the conduct of Joint Operations” to be a direct cost. There is no place in the Unit Operating Agreement that allows a vendor’s contractor to be up charged. The flat rate was intended as a way for the Operator to easily recover its employee costs without the requirement to calculate and provide support for salary, benefit, and burden. It was not intended to circumvent vendor costs being billed at the actual cost paid by the Operator. In addition, charging vendor employees through the P&T labor also creates the risk of duplicate costs by directly charging the vendor invoice and also billing that contractor on the monthly P&T Labor entry. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account a total of $4,772,740.11 for over charge of contractors' costs at the affiliate flat labor. Amount Claimed: $4,772,740.11

replies.text: Credit denied. The auditor points out the fact that the charges are from the Affiliate and therefore sections of the JOA/Accounting Procedure addressing Affiliate charges should be reviewed. All projects are Major Construction or IPT and per the applicable JOA/Accounting Procedure sections the charges are correct as billed, ie. at a flat rate. The auditor is incorrect when stating the following: "The affiliate labor charges were manually adjusted from the SIEP invoices to replace the original invoice rates with the escalated affiliate rate of $367 per hour." The timewriting charges were not "manually adjusted", but were billed according to the JOA terms at a flat rate escalated annually. Per Exhibit "G" Integrated Project Team and Technology Sharing of the Vito JOA allows for Affiliate charges. As further clarified for Section III per the Addendum to Exhibit “C” (Statement of Clarification and Intent). Screenshots below:

20.description: The Operator charged $1,048,325.59 overhead on Shell International Exploration & Petroleum (SIEP) P&T Non-labor costs in 2021 and 2022. Affiliate costs include both P&T labor and P&T Non-labor costs. The Addendum to the JOA Section III.d.ii, stipulates, overhead for IPT AFEs should be applied to the total cost excluding any affiliate charges. Specifically, Joint Operating Agreement, Exhibit C, section III, paragraph 2.C, states the major construction overhead rate is 2%. And the Addendum to the Exhibit C, Addendum, section III, paragraph d.ii. states, "The Major Construction rates provided in Exhibit "C", Section III, Paragraph 2.C shall provide compensation to the Operator for all personnel above the Project Manager level and all other administrative functions and associated cost indirectly serving the project including, but not limited to, cost for accounting, personnel services, treasury, administrative, senior management and other support services provided by the Operator. 38.description: The Operator charged the Vito Joint Account a total of $70,596,759.40 P&T affiliate labor costs in 2021 and 2022. The P&T labor costs are calculated based on actual hours worked times the escalated affiliate flat rates. The Operator charged the Joint Account affiliate cost using the escalated flat rates based on Exhibit "A" of Joint Operating Agreement (JOA) dated July 1, 2008. However, a Unit Operating Agreement (UOA) was signed with an effective date of January 1, 2012. Article 1. of the UOA stated: "the Unit Area and all operations conducted thereon shall be governed by this "UOA". Article 2. e) stated "all references to "Joint Operating Agreement" or "JOA" shall be deleted and replaced with "Unit Operating Agreement" or "UOA". 2.f) stated: "The effective date shall be January 1, 2012. All references to July 1, 2008 shall be deleted and replaced with January 1, 2012 . The Accounting Procedure in Exhibit "A" shows the effective date is January 1, 2012. In addition, the JOA dated July 1, 2008 was amended replaced with the new effective date of February 13, 2012. Per the above mentioned "UOA", the Operator should use the Accounting Procedure attached and made part of Unit Operating Agreement dated January 1, 2012 not the JOA dated July 1, 2008. Even though the initial rates are the same for both agreements, due to COPAS yearly percentages increases/decreases the chargeable rate varies which created a difference on the escalated affiliate rates. A recalculated of the affiliate costs based on the January 1, 2012 effective date shows the Joint Account was over-charged P&T labor in the amount of $2,245,897.52 in 2021 and $3,264,478.81 in 2022 for a total over-charge of $5,510,376.31. Credit is requested for the Joint Account in the amount of $5,621,094.64 ($5,510,376.33 + $110,718.34 overhead) for overcharge of P&T affiliate labor costs based on incorrect escalated flat rates. 012.short_description: Globetrotter 1 BOP Repairs & Maintenance Charged 100% to Europa- November 2021 Costs (IR-024)
012.description:
Pursuant to Journal Entry No. 130778596 dated 1/31/2022, the Europa Joint Account was charged $3,931,426.44 to transfer costs from a suspense account to the Europa Joint Account for Globetrotter 1 BOP repairs & maintenance applicable for the period November 12, 2021, through November 30, 2021. According to the Operator's Daily Operating Reports for the period November 12, 2021 through January 4, 2022, the Globetrotter 1 rig was either at South Timbalier Blk 89 or Mississippi Canyon Blk 506 (where the Globetrotter II was located) and not at MC935 Europa. During one stretch of time, November 19, 2021 and November 29, 2021, it appears the Globetrotter 1 was at MC Blk 506 where the Globetrotter 2 was located, and members of both rig crews were working on the BOP repairs & maintenance.

Section XI Suspended Operations Handling of Rig Costs and Rig Related Costs During Long-Term Suspension of MFI- 56 Rig Related Costs (Page 11) states in part:

A suspension lasting more than 30 days is a long-term suspension. It is unfair for the Company to bear all Rig costs and Rig-Related Costs incurred during a long-term suspension because the suspension is beyond the Company's/Operator's control. The Company should record all Rig costs and Rig -Related Costs incurred during long-term suspensions into appropriate allocation pools. Such costs are directly chargeable to the joint account under the Labor, Transportation, Services or other pertinent provisions of the applicable accounting procedures except the DWAP, where such costs are directly chargeable to the joint account under the Equipment and Facilities Furnished by Parties, Affiliates provisions and allocated to all subsequent wells served by the Rig during the remaining term of the Rig Contract.

Since, there were BOP repairs, maintenance, and testing going on for the whole time period of November 12, 2021, through January 4, 2022 (when the Globetrotter 1 rig arrived on location from ST089 to MC935 Europa), these rig cost repairs were clearly over 30 days and should have been allocated to subsequent wells that used the Globetrotter 1 over the remaining life of the drilling contract.

Also, the term of the contract should include any extensions made to the drilling contract. Based on the Operator's rig modification costs amortization schedules, the original life of the contract was July 15, 2012 through July 14, 2022. Please note that after the original life of the contract, it appears the contract may have been extended by Shell and subleased to CNOOC and Petronas for the Globetrotter 1 to drill some wells in Mexico for the period August 2022 through February 2023. Section XVIII Sub-Leasing (Page 17) states in part:

The sub-lease account should bear its share of Rig-Related Costs allocation pools and receive an appropriate allocated share of the cost, regardless of whether or not these costs are passed along to the party that is subleasing the Rig.

Finally, reference is again made to MFI-56, specifically Section XX Rig Contract Extensions (p. 18).

When a Rig Contract is extended as a direct result of a Long-Term Suspension, the Rig Contract extension term should be included along with the remainder of the original Rig Contract term when allocating the accumulated costs of the Long-Term Suspension. This will more equitably allocate the Long-Term Suspension costs over the term which benefits.

When material Rig Modifications, Rig Repairs or Program Moves are performed near the end of a Rig Contract term and are directly linked to the Company's decision to extend the Rig Contract, the extension term should be included along with the remainder of the original contract term when allocating the accumulated costs of those activities. In general, if the Company has decided to incur certain Rig-Related Costs for the benefit of an extended contract, the extended contract should bear its proportional share of the allocation.

023.short_description: Globetrotter 1 BOP Repairs & Maintenance Charged 100% to Europa- December 2021 Costs
023.description:
Noble invoice nos. 90020806A and 90020919C dated January 7, 2022 and April 18, 2022, totaling $873,404.28 and $179,104.12 respectively, charged the Europa Joint Account for daywork for the Globetrotter 1 for the period December 4, 5, 18-20, 2022 applicable to BOP repairs and maintenance.

Section XI Suspended Operations Handling of Rig Costs and Rig Related Costs During Long-Term Suspension of MFI- 56 Rig Related Costs (Page 11) states in part:

A suspension lasting more than 30 days is a long-term suspension. It is unfair for the Company to bear all Rig costs and Rig-Related Costs incurred during a long-term suspension because the suspension is beyond the Company's/Operator's control. The Company should record all Rig costs and Rig -Related Costs incurred during long-term suspensions into appropriate allocation pools. Such costs are directly chargeable to the joint account under the Labor, Transportation, Services or other pertinent provisions of the applicable accounting procedures except the DWAP, where such costs are directly chargeable to the joint account under the Equipment and Facilities Furnished by Parties, Affiliates provisions and allocated to all subsequent wells served by the Rig during the remaining term of the Rig Contract.

Since, there were BOP repairs, maintenance, and testing going on for the whole time period of November 12, 2021, through January 4, 2022 (when the Globetrotter 1 rig arrived on location from ST089 to MC935 Europa), these rig cost repairs were clearly over 30 days and should have been allocated to subsequent wells that used the Globetrotter 1 over the remaining life of the drilling contract.

Also, the term of the contract should include any extensions made to the drilling contract. Based on the Operator's rig modification costs amortization schedules, the original life of the contract was July 15, 2012 through July 14, 2022. Please note that after the original life of the contract, it appears the contract may have been extended by Shell and subleased to CNOOC and Petronas for the Globetrotter 1 to drill some wells in Mexico for the period August 2022 through February 2023. Section XVIII Sub-Leasing (Page 17) states in part:

The sub-lease account should bear its share of Rig-Related Costs allocation pools and receive an appropriate allocated share of the cost, regardless of whether or not these costs are passed along to the party that is subleasing the Rig.

Finally, reference is again made to MFI-56, specifically Section XX Rig Contract Extensions (p. 18).

When a Rig Contract is extended as a direct result of a Long-Term Suspension, the Rig Contract extension term should be included along with the remainder of the original Rig Contract term when allocating the accumulated costs of the Long-Term Suspension. This will more equitably allocate the Long-Term Suspension costs over the term which benefits.

When material Rig Modifications, Rig Repairs or Program Moves are performed near the end of a Rig Contract term and are directly linked to the Company's decision to extend the Rig Contract, the extension term should be included along with the remainder of the original contract term when allocating the accumulated costs of those activities. In general, if the Company has decided to incur certain Rig-Related Costs for the benefit of an extended contract, the extended contract should bear its proportional share of the allocation.

Exhibit 'C' Section III Overhead of the Unit Operating Agreement states: "As compensation for administrative, supervision, office services and warehousing costs, Operator shall charge the Joint Account in accordance with this Section III.'

Additionally, AG 19, Section IV.3.C states 'Actual costs may include costs of (I) Material, (2) making it suitable for use, a nd (3) transportation from the point of acquisition to the Joint Property including loading and unloading. Not included are storage or carrying costs."

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

The Sumitomo Corporation of Americas has been contracted to provide OCTG, casing, tubing, well, and accessories for drilling and completion projects. The Operator does not own any goods/ products or inventory at the vendor's facility and is not charged for the material until is ready for immediate use and shipped out for installation (thus avoiding an accumulation of surplus stock), or for any items not used or returned, a credit is provided to the Joint Operation. This Supply Chain Management (SCM) fee is an ancillary cost related to Sumitomo project management that is charged as part of the overall cost for provision of goods and services.

Therefore, the contract provision described in Exhibit 'C' Section III Overhead of the Unit Operating Agreement (UOA) stated is for warehousing costs incurred for warehouses owned and operated by the Operator is not applicable here.

According to BP-SOI February 2019 letter agreement, Attachment I, Section 3 Billing Disputes Paragraph l. Third-Party Project Management - Ancillary costs related to third party project management that are charged as part of the overall cost for provision of goods and services by such third party associated with a third party's provision of goods and services may be charged to the Joint Account as a component cost of the underlying goods and services and shall not be qualified as OTL or as administrative costs covered under Overhead. Sumitomo SCM fee is a component cost of the underlying goods and services, and it does not qualify as OTL, administrative, or warehousing costs covered under Overhead.

This Supply Chain Management (SCM) fee is an ancillary cost related to Sumitomo project management that is charged as part of the overall cost for provision of goods and services.

Therefore, the contract provision described in Exhibit 'C' Section III Overhead of the Unit Operating Agreement (UOA) stated is for warehousing costs incurred for warehouses owned and operated by the Operator is not applicable here.
