066.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $556,848.41 for EDG charges via the TRACK system per the attached JADE lines. Included in the charges are $545,672.79 for Cost Specialist(s), Document Controller, and Project Scheduler(s).

Project Schedulers are covered by overhead per the URSA JOA, Exhibit C, Section III "As compensation for administrative, supervision, office services and warehousing costs, Operator shall charge the Joint Account in accordance with this Section III (Overhead)....The cost and expense of services from outside sources in connection with matters of taxation, traffic, accounting or matters before or involving governmental agencies shall be considered as included in the overhead rates". Furthermore, these costs are not chargeable per the Settlement Agreement, effective date December 19,2018, Exhibit C, Section 2 which states that to be directly chargeable to the joint account, scheduler(s), planners (s) and execution supporters must be working on "...facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities". The Scheduler in question was working on major construction, development projects and general Opex, per the charging WBS codes. Absent of supporting documentation evidencing that the Scheduler was working specifically on a facility maintenance, well maintenance and/or turnaround activity, they do not meet the definition of "Technical Employee" per Section 2 of the Agreement, and instead reverts to being an administrative function covered by overhead.

Cost Specialists and Document Controllers are accounting and administrative functions covered by overhead per the JOA, Exhibit C, Section III ""As compensation for administrative, supervision, office services and warehousing costs, Operator shall charge the Joint Account in accordance with this Section III (Overhead)....The cost and expense of services from outside sources in connection with matters of taxation, traffic, accounting or matters before or involving governmental agencies shall be considered as included in the overhead rates". The Settlement Agreement, effective date December 19, 2018, Exhibit C, Section 2 also states "Technical Employees do not include procurement, administration, accounting and auditing, pipeline nominations and scheduling, human resources, management, supervision, ... Overhead charges are compensation for all costs and expenses associated with these functions."

The Operator is therefore requested to credit the joint Account $545,672.79 plus overhead of $12,295.41 for a total credit due of $557,968.20.

In order to clarify "engineering, design and drafting costsⁿ chargeable under Section III, Paragraph ž.B. of this Exhibit C, the following shall apply:

- a. SERVICES RENDERED BY OPERATOR'S 1 EMPLOYEES All salaries, wages, payroll burden and Personal Expenses of personnel performing technical services for the benefit of the Joint Account in connection with the design, construction, and installation of the Major Construction project shall be charged direct regardless of location. Such personnel shall be comprised of Operator's Producing and Exploration Department employees including engineers, environmentalists, techñologists, e engineering assistants, technicians, draftsmen, construction representatives, and other personnel performing technical services.

However, note that only Technical employees are chargeable per the above agreement. Technical employees are defined as follows in the 2018 Settlement Agreement.

## 2. Definition of "Technical Employees"

"Technical Employees" shall mean those employees, having special and specific engineering, geological, geophysical technical or 'operational skills (including planners, schedulers and execution support for facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities), and whose function in Joint Operations (as defined in the relevant Applicable Operating Agreement) is providing services for the benefit of the Joint Property (as defined in the Applicable Operating Agreement).

For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employees do not include procurement, administration, accounting and auditing, pipeline nominations and scheduling, human resources, management, supervision (excluding first level supervision of operational staff which is billable), legal services, handling taxation matters, permitting/regulatory work, land and division order services. Overhead charges are compensation for all costs and expenses associated with such functions, including the salaries or wages plus applicable payroll burdens, benefits, and personal expenses of personnel performing such functions, as well as their office and other support costs.

Thus, if an employee's role/function is not technical in nature (ie, administrative in nature), then their cost is considered overhead even if they are working in a Major Construction Project.

Note that in this exception, there are only 9 contractors in question, as follows:

[table 1]

Hector Perez and Rhett Vicknair are Project Schedulers and as such are considered Technical employees per definition noted above. The Operator is requested to demonstrate that Mr. Perez and Mr. Vicknair's job responsibilities in the non-Major Construction projects are in accordance with what is chargeable per the 2018 Settlement Agreement.

However, the rest of the EDG contractors are cost specialists and document controllers. These roles are administrative in nature. 075.short_description: NGT2 Rig Settlement for Hurricane Ida
075.description:
Noble invoice 90021225A, in the amount of $9,952,525, is for the settlement of a dispute as to the applicable day rate for the Noble Globetrotter 2 rig during the Repair Period due to Hurricane Ida. The Repair Period is a period of 116 days commencing on August 29, 2021, and ending on December 23, 2021. Shell and Noble agreed that Shell would transfer $9,952,525 to Noble in settlement of this dispute. Simultaneously with execution of this Agreement, Noble and Shell agreed to extend the term of the Drilling Contract by 56 days.

The NGT2 was on the URSA Princess P12 at the time that Hurricane Ida hit and returned to Princess P12 on December 26, 2021, and was there for 14 days until it was released on January 8, 2022. From there it went on to other non-URSA properties. Shell issued Emergency AFE P.US.AOP.EO.21.024.26 for the cost associated with this Settlement Agreement and charged 100% of the cost to URSA.

We believe that COPAS Model Form Interpretation 56 supports having these rig charges related to Hurricane Ida placed into a pool and charged out to all subsequent wells served by the rig during the remaining term of the Rig Contract. We believe there are three parts of MFI-56 that supports this position.

First, Section XI. Suspended Operations refers to when an Operator must suspend Rig operations for a reason outside of its reasonable control, such as a hurricane. For a long-term suspension, which is defined as a suspension over 30 days, it recommends that rig and rig-related costs should be placed in allocation pools and allocated to all subsequent wells served by the Rig during the remaining term of the Rig Contract. Hurricane Ida caused damaged to the rig which resulted in a suspension of activities for 116 days, so it falls into this category.

Second, Section XIII. Rig Repairs states that costs for repairs not caused by operations on a specific property are a part of the overall compensation due the drilling contractor and are directly chargeable to all wells using the repaired equipment over the remaining life of the Rig Contract. The day rate for the rig during the rig repair period should be considered as a part of rig repairs and since these damages were caused by Hurricane Ida and not by operations on Princess P12, they should be placed in allocation pools and allocated to all subsequent wells served by the Rig during the remaining term of the Rig Contract.

Third, XX. Rig Contract Extensions. Since this agreement also includes an extension of the Drilling Contract by 56 days, it is clear that this settlement agreement benefits properties serviced by the NGT2 rig after it was released from the Princess P12 well. MFI-56 states that when the Rig Contract is extended as a direct result of a Long-Term Suspension, the Rig Contract extension term should be included along with the remainder of the original Rig Contract term when allocating the accumulated costs of the Long-Term Suspension. This will more equitably allocate the Long-Term Suspension costs over the term which benefits.

For all of the above reasons, we feel the costs associated to the NGT2 rig during the repair period should be placed in an allocation pool and allocated to all subsequent wells served by the Rig during the remaining term of the Rig Contract, including the additional 56 days, which would make the contract expire on December 30, 2023. This includes Noble Invoice 90021225A, in the amount of $9,952,525 and the NGT2 Demob allocation charges of $208,277.33 and NGT2 Blind Shear Ram allocation charges of $200,234.06 for the respective unwind charges during the repair period of the NGT2. We have excluded the $18,804.67 for the adjusted NGT2 Blind Shear Ram allocation charges, as we are taking exception to that in a different exception.

Credit to the URSA Joint Account is requested in the amount of $10,163,683.32, which is the net of the $10,361,036.39 charged to the Joint Account less the $197,353.07 that should be allocated to URSA for the December 26, 2021 to January 8, 2022 time period.

084.short_description: NGT2 BSR Upgrade Adj Coding Error
084.description:
The URSA Joint Venture was charged $40,895.11 for an adjustment made to the NGT2Blind Shear Rams Upgrade Accumulator for time the NGT2 rig was undergoing a 5-year BOP Recertification from January to March 2022. The NGT2 Blind Shear Rams Upgrade Accumulator Unwind charged $104,977.50 during this time frame to Network 30335722, which was created to accumulate the NGT2 5-year Recertification Rig Idle costs. However, instead of transferring these charges to the 5-year BOP Recertification Accumulator (WBS P.US.RTD.EB.22.012.1510A) it transferred these charges back to the NGT2 Blind Shear Rams Upgrade Accumulator (WBSP.US.RTD.EB.20.001.1510B) and allocated the charges retroactively back to the start of the Unwind. Therefore, it charged the URSA properties for charges associated with the NGT2 rig that occurred after the rig was released from the URSA properties. The Major Maintenance section of COPAS Model Form Interpretation 56 addresses this issue and states that properties using the equipment prior to the major maintenance should not share in any of the cost.

In an email attached to SAP Document Number 131266474, which is the entry where Shell transferred the charges from the NGT2 5-year Recertification Rig Idle network back to the NGT2 Blind Shear Rams Upgrade Accumulator, the reason for this entry was because 'we should not be allocating accumulators to other accumulators.' The auditors are not sure of the Accounting Principle that supports this, but basically, this is just a two-level allocation which happens in the Oil Industry all the time. Shell went on to break their own rule because they ended up transferring these charges from the NGT2 Blind Shear Rams Upgrade Accumulator back to this same Accumulator, so they still did an accumulator-to-accumulator allocation. Furthermore, a result of this reallocation is that Shell ended up allocating $9,858.76 back to Network 30335722 (NGT2 5-year Recertification Rig Idle costs), which would then have been transferred to the 5-year BOP Recertification Accumulator (WBS P.US.R TD.EB.22.012.1510A). Therefore, Shell didn't stop this Accumulator -to-Accumulator transfer, they just inappropriately reduced the amount being transferred.

Bottom line is the $104,977.50 should have been transferred to the 5-year BOP Recertification Accumulator (WBS P.US.RTD.EB.22.012.1510A) instead of the NGT2 Blind Shear Rams Upgrade Accumulator (WBS P.US.RTD.EB.20.001.1510B), just like all the other NGT2 rig costs during this time period were allocated.

Please credit the URSA Joint Account $40,895.11 for this coding error.

It also appears the rig contract end date should be used as the end date for the basis of the allocation charges instead of November 24, 2022.

For purposes of this exception, we are seeking credit for all the charges to URSA from the NGT2 Blind Shear Rams Upgrade Accumulator prior to August 25, 2021, which amounts to $182,737.88. Once documentation is provided for the correct start and end date of this accumulator, we can calculate the exact amount due the URSA Joint Account.

In this particular instance, the invoicing for these Blind Shear Ram upgrades were not charged initially to the correct coding and it was not until October 2022 before this was all rectified and allocated. By this time a number of rig contract extensions had been executed with SEPWES, and given these extensions are now established it makes sense to allocate from the completion of the upgrade through the current contract at the time of the allocation which is 24 November 2022.

In its response, the Operator has not provided the actual start and end date of their contract with Noble for the NGT2. Instead the Operator notes that the period used in the accumulator is based on their internal contract with Shell E&P Wells Services (SEPWES).

Since the Operator did not provide the requested contract, we relied on the published Noble Fleet Status report dated October 3, 2022 to obtain an end date for Noble's contract with Shell. Based on the Fleet Status report dated Oct 2022, the NGT2 is shown to be under contract with Shell until November, 2023. Then, the Fleet Status report dated Oct, 2023, the NGT2 is shown to have extended its contract with Shell to March, 2024. Thus, the accumulator should be adjusted to reflect this contract end date (March 2024). Even as of Oct 2022, there was already an agreement between the Operator and Noble to extend the rig contract to November 2023 as evidenced by the Fleet Status report. While we are still waiting for a response to this request, we noted two items that should be corrected on the NGT2 Rig Demobilization unwind.

First, as a result of damages due to Hurricane Ida, the rig contract for NGT2 was extended by 56 days. In accordance with COPAS Model Form Interpretation 56, the NGT2 Rig Demobilization Accumulator unwind should be extended by these 56 days upon its return to duty from the hurricane. As a result, the URSA Joint Venture should only be charged $26,152.60 instead of $28,309.52 for the December 26, 2021 to January 8, 2022 timeframe, resulting in a credit of $2,156.92 due the URSA Joint Account.

Second, SAP Document 131266474 charges $109,193.94 to the NGT2 Rig Demobilization accumulator (WBSP.US.RTD.EB.22.007.1510A). As pointed out in Audit Exception 084, this charge should be to the NGT2 BOP Recertification accumulator (WBS P.US.RTD.EB.22.012.1510A). Although Shell has not yet included this amount in the worksheet for the NGT2 Rig Demobilization accumulator, this coding error should be corrected to prevent future erroneous charges to the NGT2 Rig Demobilization accumulator.

We request the Operator provide the requested data from IR66, along with making the two adjustments mentioned above, resulting in a credit of $2,210.84 ($2,156.92 plus 2.5% overhead) to the URSA Joint Account.

Please note any additional exception amount due URSA will be determined upon the receipt of data from IR66.

As discussed in our rebuttal on exception 85, we noted that the NGT2 contract with Noble was extended to March 2024 by Shell. Thus, this accumulator should also be calculated using an end date of March 2024.

In its response, the Operator asserts that it "recovers mobilization and demobilization cost through the original contract period. There is no presumption that a contract extension will be executed from the start, and therefore the operator must recover these costs in the initial contract period." The Operator claims that this is consistent with section XX of COPAS MFI 56 guidance. However, the Operator left off the 2 situations where rig contract extensions should be included in the calculation. (see highlighted portions below).

## XX. RIG CONTRACT EXTENSIONS

If the Company extends the Rig Contract term, the recommended practice is to treat the Rig Contract extension period as a new Rig Contract rather than reallocating the Rig-Related Costs from the inception of the original Rig Contract to the termination date of the Rig Contract extension period. This is because the Rig-Related Costs incurred for the initial Rig Contract term were incurred with a presumption that only the initial Rig Contract term would exist. Accordingly, the Rig Contract extension is a separate and independent decision. However, two specific situations warrant including the Rig Contract extension period in the prospective allocation term:

- When a Rig Contract is extended as a direct result of a Long-Term Suspension, the Rig Contract extension term should be included along with the remainder of the original Rig Contract term when allocating the accumulated costs of the Long-Term Suspension. This will more equitably allocate the Long-Term Suspension costs over the term which benefits. There must be a reasonably clear link between the existence of a Long-Term Suspension and the decision to extend the Rig Contract in order to warrant including the extension term in the allocation of the Long-Term Suspension costs.
- When material Rig Modifications, Rig Repairs or Program Moves are performed near the end of a Rig Contract term and are directly linked to the Company's decision to extend the Rig Contract, the extension term should be included along with the remainder of the original contract term when allocating the accumulated costs of those activities. In general, if the Company has decided to incur certain Rig-Related Costs for the benefit of an extended contract, the extended contract should bear its proportional share of the allocation. There must be a reasonably clear link between the decision to incur costs for these categories (Rig Modifications, Rig Repairs or Program Moves) and the decision to extend the Rig Contract in order to warrant including the extension term in the allocation of the costs
- related to those activities.

In this case, there was a long term suspension related to the hurricane which caused a 56-day extension.

Lastly, the dayrate calculation is based on a budgeted figure of $7.5m. We request the Operator to provide an updated accumulator using actual costs.

## Operator's Reply on 31 October, 2025

Credit Denied

NGT2 rig was on a 6-month contract assignment with SEPWES and these expenditures were all incurred during the operations of P12 (inclusive of the storm event). The 6-month assignment ended at the completion of P12, and therefore would have all been allocated to this well had a rig accumulator been created.

For context, the Shell rig accumulators only allocate cost across the current rig contract assignment of a rig, because there is no guarantee Shell will be re-assigning the rig to the GoM after its current assignment. Shell treats any new rig contract assignment as a new contract and thus do not extend these expenditures and accumulators into any new assignment contract. This is consistent with all rig accumulators in the GoM and is aligned with COPAS guidelines.

In its response, the Operator did not address our concerns, as reiterated below:

a. timing of the delivery of the ADCP System (1/8/2022) coincided with timing of when NGT2 left Princess P12 per the rig summary provided by Operator below (also 1/8/2022). Therefore, our assertion is that this item could not have benefitted the Joint Property given that it was delivered as the NGT2 left the property.

[table 1]

b. ownership of the item: Since the ADCP System is an item that stayed on the NGT2 after installation, we believe that even if it was used on URSA part of the time ( to be determined per a above), the cost should have been placed on an accumulator and allocated to all the wells served by the NGT2 after its installation and not wholly charged to URSA. The Operator contends that this cost would have all been wholly charged to Ursa anyway even if an accumulator was used because the Joint Property's "contract" with SEPWES was only 6 months and would have ended with the work at Princess P12. We reiterate that the relevant contract term for the accumulator should be the one with Noble (until March 2024) and not the one with SEPWES.

No further supporting documentation available.

While we understand the Operator's explanation, we are unable to determine that this $460k allocation/reclassification made to Ursa is valid and/or equitable. As noted on the original exception write-up, a spreadsheet is not adequate supporting documentation for charges.

Credit remains due.

094.description:
SAP Doc 131713873 credits the Leopard Appraisal 1 Side Track network in the amount of $2,812,131,11 and charges $2,442,610.90 of this amount to the Ursa Yellow Drilling network with the remainder charged to a Leopard Appraisal WBS element and another Leopard network.

There is a NGT2 Rig fuelworking file attached to the SAP document with calculations tying into this amount but we can't understand the reasoning for this entry or the calculations behind it.

There is also a Globetrotter 2\_Rig Fuel Sheet attached to the SAP document that shows the Rig Fuel Usage on the NGT2 and the transfer of the Fuel Oil remaining on the rig from property to property. This spreadsheet makes more sense to us but does not tie to the $2,442,610.90 charged to URSA. It shows 459,977 gallons valued at $1,223,538.82 transferred from Leopard (30336101) to URSA (30350402). It also shows 421,724 gallons valued at $1,121,785.84 remaining on the NGT2 rig after the URSA operations. The URSA well only used 38,252 gallons of Fuel valued at $101,750.32.

We are having trouble understanding why the URSA well would be charged $2,442,610.90 in Rig Fuel Trueup when it only used $101,750.32 worth of fuel. It appears the URSA well was overcharged $2,340,857.92 for rig fuel usage.

Please credit $2,340,857.92 to the URSA Joint Account or provide explanation and documentation for the Rig Fuel Trueup charge as requested on IR-84.

## Summary

This table tracks fuel balance reconciliation across five SAP network codes (30353385, 30344241, 30336101, 30350470, and 30350402), comparing existing SAP quantities and amounts against actual consumption with the resulting differences. Key values include a large fuel balance credit of **2,812,131.10** for network 30344241 (where SAP balance exceeded consumption), a debit of **231,744.52** for network 30336101 (where consumption exceeded SAP balance), and a new debit of **137,775.68** for network 30353385 (which had no prior fuel balance). A remaining fuel balance of **2,442,610.90** is temporarily parked in network 30350402 after all allocations are reconciled.

0053.short_description: Noble Globetrotter II BOP Unwind Charges
0053.description:
The Operator charged the Whale and Silvertip drilling wells $848,659.85 for drilling rig Noble Globetrotter II unwind costs relating to NGT2 5 Yr BOP Recert ($733,824.00) and NGT Blind Shear Rams ($114,835.85). Per the daily operations reports and rig reports, the Noble Globetrotter II was only used for top drilling during 2022. Blowout Preventers (BOPs) are not used for the top drilling of wells; therefore, these costs should not have been allocated to the Whale and Silvertip drilling wells.

Reference the Joint Operating Agreement Exhibit C, Accounting Procedures, Section II-6 Direct Charges-Equipment and Facilities Owned by Parties, Affiliates. The first sentence state

'Operator shall charge the Joint Account for use of equipment and facilities which are owned in whole or in part by a Party or its Affiliates and used in the conduct of Joint Operations…' (underline added for emphasis only).

Reference the COPAS Model Form Interpretation 56 Rig Related Costs, Section VI Rig Modifications, sub-section Allocation for Rig Modification Costs, states

'…However, if some Rig Modifications benefit only specific wells or conditions while other Rig Modifications benefit all wells, then separate allocation pools might be necessary.'

'Benefit or service provided is the key consideration when determining the appropriate group of wells to include in an allocation pool'

Because blowout preventers are not used in conduct of Joint Operations for Top Drilling, the recertification and upgraded blind shear rams do not provide any benefit to the Whale and Silvertip wells.

The Operator is requested to credit Chevron in the amount of $880,142.53 ($848,659.85 plus overhead $31,482.68) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
In the MFI 56 Rig Related Costs, Section VI Rig Modifications, sub-section Allocation for Rig Modification Costs, states "Some Rig Modifications benefit all the wells even though the modifications might not have been required. For example, an upgraded Blowout Preventer (BOP) may be used on all the wells, although it is over-specification for some of them. Likewise, additional risers may be required in only some water depths; however, they serve as back-up equipment and can be rotated with the riser stock furnished by the drilling contractor. In this example, all wells would benefit from this arrangement because they prolong the life of the riser stock, reducing the chances of equipment failure and eliminating downtime that would occur if the drilling cont ractor's riser stock failed. Thus, the wells using the Rig generally receive the benefit of these modifications, either through actual use, improved operations and/or improved contract terms."

In this instance, the BOP on the NGT2 served as available equipment in ALL well activities if it were needed. The wells in question could have elected to complete the drilling and the BOP would have been deployed. The 'benefit' is having a working and BSEE certified BOP available at any time to safely execute all well activities.

The Operator charged the Whale and Silvertip drilling wells $145,591.92 for estimated demobilization charges relating to drilling rig Noble Globetrotter II using the contract dates 9/9/2013 through 11/4/2023. According to the Noble Fleet Status Report dated May 6, 2024, the Noble Globetrotter II was on contract from November/2023 through May/2024, thus extending the original contract dates. Therefore, there should not have been any demobilization costs allocated to the Whale and Silvertip drilling wells.

Reference the COPAS Model Form Interpretation 56 Rig Related Costs, Section XX Rig Contract Extensions, states

'If the Company extends the Rig Contract term, the recommended practice is to treat the Rig Contract extension period as a new Rig Contract rather than reallocating the Rig-Related Costs from the inception of the original Rig Contract to the termination date of the Rig Contract extension period.'

Given that the initial mobilization and Rig-Related expenses are not apportioned to the extension period, it stands to reason that the extension period should be solely accountable for any demobilization costs incurred.

The Operator is requested to credit chevron $151,011.17 ($145,591.92 plus overhead $5,419.25) with a reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text: Shell recovers mobilization and demobilization cost through the original contract period. There is no presumption that a contract extension will be executed from the start, and therefore the operator must recover these costs in the initial contract period. This is consistent with COPAS MFI 56 guidance

0061-A.description:
The Operator reclassed $19,513,125 from the Whale Joint Venture to the Whale 815 lease joint venture. The examination of the relevant documentation indicated it pertained to three purchase orders from FMC Technologies, Sumitomo Corporation of the Americas, and McDermott Inc., which were charged entirely to the Whale Joint Venture. While it is anticipated that some costs may be tied to Drill Center 815, there was no evidence provided to justify the allocation to DC 815.

On July 25, 2024, information request number 53 was issued to Shell. Shell replied on August 7, 2024, stating that the cost allocation was based on the value of work done; however, no details were provided justifying the percentage that pertains to DC 815 nor the method used for determining that percentage. To confirm the fair distribution of cost between the Whale and Whale-Silvertip Joint Accounts, the operator is asked to supply the grounds on which these costs are allocated.

The overhead and working interest percentages are different between the two wells causing an increased net-billing to Chevron in the amount of $3,824,572.50. Exceptions 0061-A and 0061-B have been created for each JV in order to calculate the correct gross and net impact. Both exceptions must be addressed together.

| JV     | JVName            | Gross Amt before OH   | OH   | Total Gross Amt   | CVXWI   | Net to CVX      |
|--------|-------------------|-----------------------|------|-------------------|---------|-----------------|
| J1140H | Whale 815 lease   | (19,513,125.00)       |      | 2%(19,903,387.50) | 60%     | (11,942,032.50) |
| J114H8 | Whale and special | 19,513,125.00         | 4%   | 20,293,650.00     | 40%     | 8,117,460.00    |
|        |                   |                       |      | 390,262.50        |         | (3,824,572.50)  |

The Operator is requested to provide the detailed support justifying the allocation to the Silvertip JV or credit the WhaleSilvertip Joint Venture $19,903,387.50 ($19,513,125.00 plus 2% overhead $390,262.50) and charge Whale Joint Venture $20,293,650.00 ($19,513,125.00 plus 4% overhead of $780,525.00) resulting in a net credit to Chevron of $3,824,572.50 with reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing. Partner reserves the right to issue additional exceptions, if warranted, after reviewing the documentation once it is made available.

replies.text:
Under SURF, specific line items within the PO were allocated to 815, covering the pipe scope and the tree scope. Several other SURF scopes had 815 costs calculated using a percentage due to shared/common execution within both 815 and non-815, which were not split between PO line items. Therefore, the line items in the SURF POs are itemized and segregated between 815, non-815 lease lands, and common (used for both 815 and non-815). Note: the portion of cost allocated as a common cost is fully charged to the Whale asset.

The percentage was determined at the beginning of 2021:

- Subsea Hardware scope (TFMC): 11.5%
- Aftermarket Services (TFMC): 11.5%
- Tools and Equipment: 12%
- ·
- URF Contractor: 13.4%
- ·
- Jumper Scope: 8.9%

The overall VOWD for each scope is calculated from the leads and the assigned percentage is used to determine the overall VOWD for 815 (per scope).

The 815 cumulative VOWD is then compared to the previous quarter's 815 VOWD, and the delta is added to the accrual for 815 VOWD for that quarter.

0062.description:
The Operator charged $2,167,193.49 to the Whale joint venture, WBS C.US.WHL.PD.21.004.1230J, for RTTC Rental Whale Team. Reviewing the JADE line-item text these charges appear to be monthly rentals of the RTTC facility from Jan/2022 through October/2023. Information Request 66 was submitted to Shell on July 26 seeking additional information and documentation to support RTTC facility costs billed to the Joint Account. No response was received from Shell.

Referencing COPAS Accounting Guideline 19, Expenditure Audit Protocols, Section III-B-17, Charges for use of Operator's Equipment/Facilities, exposure areas that an auditor may choose to examine include

- a. Actual cost versus competitive rates
- b. Actual costs
- (1) Depreciation calculation, including gross and net book value and anticipated salvage value
- (2) Return on investment (imputed interest) calculation

For the RTTC Rental referenced in IR 66, please provide

1. A description of the facility, (location, square footage, space used)
2. Actual Cost, salvage value, estimated life, yearly depreciation, and interest rate

The Operator is requested to provide documentation listed above or credit the Whale joint account $2,253,881.23 ($2,167,193.49 plus 4% overhead of $86,687.74). Partner reserves the right to issue additional exceptions, if warranted, after reviewing the documentation once it is made available.

replies.text:
Accounting Guideline 19 serves as an audit protocol, and the section III-B-17 cited by the auditor pertains specifically to charges associated with the use of equipment and facilities. In this instance, the charge relates to training sessions and classes conducted for the Whale Integrated Project Team and associated personnel at the Robert Training Center, in support of joint operations. Hence, section III does not apply.

No credit is due.

The Operator charged the Whale Joint Account $26,265,911.33 for 2022 SIEP Affiliate Labor costs. $11,867,866.86 are excluded from this exception as they are covered by various other exceptions.

Section I.5.C (Expenditure Audits) also states that "If Affiliate charges are billed using the Cost Basis, upon request from another Party, the Party providing an Affiliate will provide an annual report from a nationally recognized independent public accounting firm attesting that the charges billed from such Affiliate represent a complete and accurate allocation of its costs, and exclude any element of profit."

7.short_description: SIEP Employees - Less than 8 hours billed in a month
7.description:
The Addendum to Exhibit "C", Accounting Procedure Statement of Clarification and Intent provides in its clarification to Section III, Paragraph 2.B.a "Services Rendered by Operator's Employees":

"Salaries will be charged to the Joint Account based upon actual days worked only when such time totals at least one day or more per month that is devoted to the Major Construction project."

Exhibit "G" attached to, and made part of the Prospect Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement provides in its Section 1.6 Employees:

"Employees shall mean any individual under the employment of any party to this Operating Agreement including any Affiliate or contractor which may represent any Party hereunder."

As Shell properly recognizes, the definition of "Employees" contained in Exhibit G of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement (Integrated Project Team and Technology Sharing) expressly defines "Employees" to include any individual under the employment of any Affiliate of any Party to the Operating Agreement. Therefore, any Employee of a Shell Affiliate that is a member of the Integrated Project Team, is considered an Employee of Shell. The Addendum to Exhibit C of the Appomattox Joint Operating Agreement expressly incorporates by reference the terms and conditions of Exhibit G (See Addendum to Exhibit C, p.1). Consequently, all wages paid to Shell Affiliates are chargeable in accordance with Section III, Paragraph 2.B.

Moreover, Shell has noted that there is a prior course of dealing between CNOOC and Shell regarding this exact audit exception, which further supports CNOOC's position. As Shell is aware, a prior course of dealing is "a sequence of previous conduct between the parties to the agreement," which can provide "a common basis of understanding for interpreting their expressions and other conduct" (RESTATEMENT (SECOND) OF CONTRACTS § 223, 1981). Given Shell's longstanding approval of CNOOC's interpretation requiring salaries of Shell's Affiliates to be subject to the time requirement of Section III, Paragraph 2.B(a), the parties have established a course of dealing regarding the interpretation of the Joint Operating Agreement concerning the subject audit exception.

The audit worksheet 'Exc. 7.2\_Pvt Hrs. < 8 Hrs.', provided herein, presents JADE analysis and identification of 41 SIEP employees charging a total of 546 hours to major construction projects during the service period of August 2022 through December 2023 with those hours reported totaling less than 1 full day (8 hours) in each month.

25.short_description: Charges Not for the Joint Account - TCJA Rebills
25.description:
CNOOC maintains the position that Transocean's estimated charges referencing the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (TCJA) should not be charged to the Joint Account. The estimated charges do not specify the tax provision in the TCJA or provide any detailed calculations. CNOOC's position remains that the TCJA tax provisions such as the Base Erosion Anti-Abuse Tax (BEAT) relate to the federal tax level for all US business and do not directly increase the cost of performing drilling services. If BEAT is interpreted as a 'Change in Tax Law' applicable to the contract provision (see contract excerpt below), the decrease in tax costs resulting from greatly reduced income tax rates and bonus depreciation would also be applicable. The allocation of BEAT only considers the increased cost of a change in tax law and ignores a significant reduction to costs from lower corporate income tax rates and bonus depreciation.

The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 not only created the BEAT tax, but also decreased the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21%, and at its highest allowed 100% first year depreciation on tangible assets for 2017-2022). If corporate level taxes are deemed applicable, it is inconsistent to recover tax costs associated with BEAT, but not also adjust for other tax law changes that reduce costs for the contractor, Transocean. For example, the income tax rate decreases from 35% to 21% was not adjusted in favor of Shell (i.e., reduced day rate). The contract provision (excerpt below) does not appear to be consistently applied over time.

Assuming the rebill is related to BEAT as it was in 2019, it is calculated at a federal level, additional support is needed to evaluate the reasonableness of the allocation of the tax. Many tax assumptions and variables are examined to arrive at taxable income (the starting point of the BEAT calculation) and relying on an estimate at mid-year is not accurate. At a minimum, a true-up from the estimate to the actual tax rebill incurred related to Proteus in 2023 is required. Additionally, per the 2023 Annual Report (Form 10K) filed by Transocean Ltd and Subsidiaries, no taxes related to BEAT were paid in 2023.

01.description: The Sparta Joint Account was charged $4,114,876.62 across various journal entries including two direct fuel transfers for a total of 1,123,643 gallons used by the Poseidon rig during the period of 1/30/2023 through 4/30/2023. The unsupported price per gallon (PPG) for fuel charged in this audit period calculates out to $3.66/gallon. However, a direct fuel purchase/transfer made during the Sparta drilling campaign on Shell affiliate inv. 13292007 calculates out to a much lower $3.19/gallon. In response to IR56, the Operator did explain the nature of some fuel entries, however the end result still equates to an overcharge of ~.23 per gallon during the current audit period. The question is, where and how was fuel PPG obtained by the Operator? The Sparta UOA does not allow markup of products and services from the Operator's receiving business entity. In addition, the direct fuel transfer on Shell Trading invoice 12688060 delivered on 11/25/2022 should have been charged to the Abilene project (co-owner's lower WI%) not Sparta. Since the Operator's fuel methodology is based on usage, the PPG should be calculated using the actual/direct PPG as invoiced/charged as calculated on the attached schedule. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $269,287.38 ($258,930.17 plus $10,357.21 Project overhead) for rig fuel calculated in error.

replies.text: Sparta is the only 20K project on the Shell rig schedule. The rig upgrade only benefits Sparta as no other wells on the rig schedule require a 20K rig upgrade. It was previously agreed with Equinor that the Sparta JV would cover the 20K rig upgrade and was part of the Fabrication AFE that has been signed by Equinor. AFE is attached.

Shell charged the Joint Account for the first milestone payment of the 20K rig upgrade with the intent to charge the entire amount of the 20K rig upgrade to Sparta without regard for future drilling activity under their Stena Drilling Evolution drillship contract. Stena stated through the media that their Stena Evolution drilling contract with Shell started in second quarter of 2024 and extends for five years, with an option to extend the contract upon completion of the primary term. Even though Shell has several years left on their Stena Drilling Evolution drilling contracts, only the Sparta Joint Account is being charged. The Operator’s charge of this rig modification is not consistent with COPAS Model Form Interpretation 56 ( *Rig-Related Costs* ). Methods of allocating Rig Modification costs include a daily or monthly rate or a flat rate per well. The ultimate goal of any allocation methodology is to share the costs based on the benefit derived. Achieving this goal can become complicated because the properties benefiting may vary with each Rig Modification and may change over time. Companies may find it necessary to establish multiple allocation pools for the same Rig. For example, if Rig Modifications were made midway through the drilling program, only the wells using the Rig subsequent to the date the modifications were placed in service would share in the allocation pool for those Rig Modifications… Benefit or service provided is the key consideration when determining the appropriate group of wells to include in an allocation pool. Some Rig Modifications benefit all the wells even though the modifications might not have been required. For example, an upgraded Blowout Preventer (BOP) may be used on all the wells, although it is over-specification for some of them. Likewise, additional risers may be required in only some water depths; however, they serve as back-up equipment and can be rotated with the riser stock furnished by the drilling contractor. In this example, all wells would benefit from this arrangement because they prolong the life of the riser stock, reducing the chances of equipment failure and eliminating downtime that would occur if the drilling contractor’s riser stock failed. Thus, the wells using the Rig generally receive the benefit of these modifications, either through actual use, improved operations and/or improved contract terms. Shell provided an AFE for the 20K rig upgrade and stated the upgrade was necessary only for Sparta operations. Shell’s 20K rig upgrade charge does not match the operations dynamics because all wells drilled under the contract term will benefit from the 20K rig upgrade. Additionally, Shell did not provide information about the Stena Drilling Evolution drillship contract dates, or provide a rig schedule, so the Non-Operator could not validate any type of potential allocation basis for the upgrade charges. Furthermore, the studies are performed on the physical Joint Property as they are studies on samples from the reservoir, which are “real and personal property subject to the Agreement” as defined in Exhibit C, Section I, Paragraph 1 of the UOA. The primary purpose of these studies is to guide reservoir management and future development at Vito, and not future exploration. The samples from the VA02 well and VA04 wells are used to understand the mixture of reservoir fluids being produced from the complex fluid system at Vito, and to provide a baseline for analysis of future changes of the production from those wells. The sample analyses from the VA11 well are used to understand the fluid variations in the saddle area of the Vito field, and to understand asphaltene deposition risk from downhole fluid mixing. We are currently relying on these analyses to evaluate reservoir management opportunities in the existing Vito wells, as well as for the planning of an upcoming infill campaign at Vito.

27.description: The Operator charged the Vito Joint Account $29,205,086.00 P&T Labor. SIEP P&T labor was billed out at an escalated “all-inclusive” flat hourly rate to various AFE’s throughout 2023. In addition, the Operator has applied 2% to 13% overhead fees to these affiliate services amounting to $626,783.89. The addendum to Vito’s 1986 Accounting Procedure (non-PTAP) states the following under provision d., (ii) in short: "The Major Construction rates provided in Exhibit "C", Section III, Paragraph 2.C [If the Operator forms an Integrated Project Team and charges its costs directly to the Joint Account] shall provide compensation to the Operator for all personnel...and other support services provided by the Operator. Such rate [2%] shall be applied to the total cost (gross) incurred by the Joint Account excluding Affiliate charges." The purpose of the last sentence in the above statement is to prevent the Operator from billing the Joint Account an additional layer of overhead because overhead components are already rolled into SIEP’s flat hourly rates hence the word “all-inclusive”. Nevertheless, and regardless of where the SIEP affiliate charges land, e.g., Major Construction project, Development project, Operating project, etc. a percentage overhead fee should not be applied to these affiliate services. The legal definition of an all-inclusive hourly rate is defined as follows: “an hourly rate comprised of all direct and indirect costs including, but not limited to, overhead, fee or profit, clerical support, travel expenses, per diem, safety equipment, materials, supplies, managerial support, and all documents, forms, and reproductions thereof, portal-to-portal expenses and per diem expenses such as food.” The partner should not incur overhead fees from both the parent company and SIEP. The Operator is requested to credit the Vito Joint Account $626,783.89 for overhead applied to affiliate services in error.

replies.text: Claim is under Operator review

41.short_description: Incorrect Transfer Pricing - Seawater Source Pumps
41.description: The Vito Joint Account, Topside Procurement AFE was charged $2,528,080.00 for (2) Seawater Source Pump units (serial nos. 619339 PBE-2165 & 619338 PBE-2160) at 100% "A" condition value on transfer document no. 131419962 from Whale's inventory to Vito. Email communication was obtained during the audit that indicated these 2 pumps were needed as replacements to the original 2 out of 3 Vito pumps that failed while being used in the field. The 2 replacement pumps were installed on the Vito production facility in March 2023. In addition to these 2 pumps being transferred from Whale to Vito at their 100% original value, Vito was also charged for the reconditioning of these same pump units on Worley third-party passthrough provided by Sulzer on invoice no. 90664027 & 90665823. In response to IR37, the Operator did not acknowledge the third party repair/reconditioning cost. In the absence of an inspection report detailing the condition of the pump units before leaving Whale's inventory in Singapore, the true assessment of this equipment remains unclear at this time. Based on Sulzer Repair Quotations (to the right), these pumps required dismantling, inspection, engineering & redesign work, component sourcing, testing and reassembly to return this equipment back to its original sound and suitable function. As such, this material no longer qualifies as "A" or "B" condition. Section IV.2. (Transfers and Dispositions) of the Vito Accounting Procedure states the following under subsection C: Since reconditioning cost was billed to the Joint Account to return these pumps back to their original condition for Vito operations, these pumps should have been transferred to Vito at 50% of their original value in accordance with Section IV.2.C(1). The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $1,289,320.80 ($1,264,040.00 plus 2% major construction overhead) for material. T.B.D. portion of exception: According to email communication between Shell's Contracts & Finance Management Team, Vito had 3 failed Seawater Source Pump (SSP) units within a 6-month timeframe. Based on the cost of these units, co-owner has concerns regarding the financial impact to Vito and whether warranty terms under the supplier/manufacturers Master Service Agreement have been reviewed and evaluated. Co-owner is requesting answers the following questions regarding the failed SSP's: • What was the root cause of failure for Vito's original & spare SSP units (serial numbers 592097, 592098, 619577), e.g. defective or faulty components such as gaskets, seals, excessive heat, power supply anomalies? • Does the supplier/manufacturer offer discounts or replacement warranties on these SSP units if it was determined failure was caused by a defective or faulty components? • A considerable amount of quality control and assurance cost has been billed during the Vito FPU construction phase. Has a post failure inspection analysis been performed by the supplier or third-party detailing the cause of failure for these units?

replies.text: Credit Denied. The operator has already provided an explanation on the Condition aspects of the Seawater source pump in information request 37. (i.e) these pumps were brand new and uninstalled on Whale, thus they qualify for the 100% A condition as per COPAS. Providing these pumps from Whale saved Vito and subsequently Equinor millions of dollars of revenue which they would not have received had the pumps not been provided as this would have resulted in additional downtime on Vito. Whale had to replace the pumps provided and thus Whale and its co-owners would have been harmed had the pumps not been transferred at 100% of their value as they were 100% new pumps and were required by Whale for the completion of the Whale project. Also, the inspection of the equipment is standard before it is sent offshore. Also, the below snippet demonstrates that Equinor was informed and involved in the seawater pump solution at the time. By providing the materials Whale saved the day and that if Whale hadn’t had these pumps available, Vito’s ramp-up would likely have been materially set back. So this was a big “win” for Vito from a value perspective. The operator considered the TBD portion of the exception is not related to chargeability and will not be replied in the audit trail. The technical aspects of the questions should be managed through normal co-owner engagements and not through audit trail.

53.description: The Operator charged the Vito Joint Account, VA010 & VA011 wells a total of $5,357,376.00 from several Enhanced Drilling (EDI) milestone invoices for CML pump and seal upgrades for the Deepwater Pontus drillship. Based on EDI's work scope, the upgrades consist of replacing of 2 existing subsea pumps on the SPM with more powerful pump motors and seals, including an upgrade to the subsea interface and control system to handle the power demands from the upgraded pumps. IR19 was submitted to the Operator questioning the sole benefit of these cost charged to Vito. In response, only copies of the Vito Waterflood VA010 & VA011 Drilling AFE's were provided. The scope and language provided in the Vito Waterflood VA010 & VA011 Drilling AFE's do not sufficiently address all capital cost elements associated with these rig upgrades, such as non-productive rig time and other ancillary cost supporting these upgrades. In addition, the 2023 Annual Operating Plan does not provide the co-owner information regarding upgrades. Article 6.7.3.1 (Capital Budget) to the Vito Unit Operating Agreement states, in part: "...The Annual Operating Plan shall contain an estimated capital budget that includes the following:... ...c) other capital projects requiring a gross expenditure greater than three million dollars ($3,000,000). The term "capital project" shall include addition of new equipment, expansion or upgrades of existing equipment..." The rig upgrades provided by EDI have exceeded the $3M threshold as set forth in Article 6.7.3.1. The approval of these AFE's does not imply that the co-owner should subsidize upgrades that could potentially benefit other properties. Any capital cost associated with the commissioning, installation, and testing of upgrades to the drilling contractors MODU substructure and/or base drilling equipment inventory should be amortized throughout the rigs contract term under guidelines set forth in COPAS MFI-56 (Rig Related Cost) Web sources indicate Deepwater Pontus end contract date with Shell is set for Oct-2027. At this time Co-owner is of the opinion that these rig upgrades and associated marine vessel cost could benefit other ventures utilizing the Pontus on future operations. This exception will remain as To Be Determined pending future evaluation and final disposition the CML equipment. Status: T.B.D. (To Be Determined)

replies.text: Credit Denied The purpose of the rig upgrade was to drill the two wells associated with the Vito asset, irrespective of its applicability to future assets. After obtaining the approval from the co-owner via the AFE C.US.VTO.PD.21.006.0942A, C.US.VTO.PD.21.008.0942A the full cost was charged to the Vito asset. Regarding the contract period it is inappropriate for the auditor to use the report obtained from the Transocean website and to ignore the facts presented by the rig schedule and contract provided to the auditor.

54.short_description: AE54 - Affiliate Contract Labor charged at Flat Rate
54.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged $5,360,410.00 P&T labor for 32 contractors from 17 suppliers at the affiliate flat rate. The affiliate labor charges were manually adjusted from the SIEP invoices to replace the original invoice rates with the escalated affiliate rate of $366 to $399 per hour. These contractors are not on the consolidated P&T staff listing but on the contractor listing. Their services were billed at the affiliate flat rates instead of the actual cost as listed on the affiliate invoices. The total amount charged to the Joint Account from these contractors is $5,360,410.00 for 14,170 hours. The actual costs based on the SIEP invoices is $2,639,042.00, resulted in an overcharge of $2,721,368.00 at the higher flat rates. These personnel are contractors from various vendors including GATE, NES Global, RISK bytes, Global Edge, Worley Group, EDG, Intertek, SGS North America and Nextsource. The Accounting Procedure, section 5. Services, allows “the cost of contract services, equipment, and utilities used in the conduct of Joint Operations” to be a direct cost. There is no place in the Unit Operating Agreement that allows a vendor’s contractor to be up charged. The flat rate was intended as a way for the Operator to easily recover its employee costs without the requirement to calculate and provide support for salary, benefit, and burden. It was not intended to circumvent vendor costs being billed at the actual cost paid by the Operator. In addition, charging vendor employees through the P&T labor also creates the risk of duplicate costs by directly charging the vendor invoice and also billing that contractor on the monthly P&T Labor entry. The auditor also noticed that the Operator added a lot more vendors to the contractor listing and included a lot more contractors to the P&T labor costs billed at flat rate instead of actual costs. For example, in 2022, the P&T labor costs is about 70% of the total affiliate costs. In 2023, the P&T labor costs is about 90% of the affiliate costs. In 2022, only 24 contractors are billed at flat rate and 32 contractors are billed at flat in 2023. No details were provided as to what services being performed by these contractors. The Operator is requested to provide vendor contract with the contractors to show that they were hired by the Affiliate as their contractors to perform IPT work as directed by the project manager. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $2,775,795.36 ($2,721,368.00 plus $54,427.36 overhead) for over-charge of contractors' costs at all-inclusive flat rates instead of the actual costs.

replies.text: Claim is under Operator review

replies.text:

The contractors Logos and Eric have time-written to Great White WBS's using cost center 286694, &442016 respectively, however for these cost center's Labor Over-under has been enabled in the SAP system.

For the over & under process to happen monthly a corresponding charge (i.e salary of the contractor) to the cost center should have been made.

However, in case of Franklin and Eric no charge in the Salaries GL account was made to the cost center because only employees' salaries are charged here, the Over/Under program will reverse the excess time writing as part of the month-end process. So, there is no duplication of charge.

Through Over/Under process whatever charges were booked for these contractors have been reversed.

Therefore, no cost was charged to the co-owners and no credit remains due.

001.description:
The Operator charged the Great White Joint Account $159,570.70 on various Sumitomo Corporation of Americas invoices for SCM Fee Consignment charges. This is a material management fee and is not a direct cost of the material but an additional fee to house the material and ensure it is available when needed.

Exhibit 'C' Section III Overhead of the Unit Operating Agreement states: As compensation for administrative, supervision, office services and warehousing costs, Operator shall charge the Joint Account i n accordance with this Section III.'

Additionally, AG 19, Section IV.3.C states 'Actual costs may include costs of (I) Material, (2) making it suitable for use, and (3) transportation from the point of acquisition to the Joint Property including loading and unloading. Not included are storage or carrying costs."

And according to MFI-19, Section IV, interpretative section, carrying costs are not chargeable. This SCM Fee is a form of carrying cost and therefore considered covered by Overhead (not allowed to be charged) as stated in MFI-19:

replies.text:
The operator maintains its position that the SCM fee is chargeable in accordance with the BP-SOI Settlement Agreement, effective February 1, 2022, and Section 3, paragraph 3.12 of the Billing Standards. Following the face-to-face meeting in February 2025 with SOI\_BP, both parties agreed to escalate this issue to the commercial departments of both companies. The operator's position remains unchanged.

001.description:
The Operator charged the Great White Joint Account $168,581.54 ($328,902.14 including burden and benefits, and overhead) for CATS Payroll costs which are not chargeable under Exhibit C, Section 3 C of the terms of the Chevron Settlement Agreement.

This was the subject of Silvertip IR-018 which the Operator responded, "Based on previous audits and weekly meeting discussions, it has been determined that the operator is not required to provide proof for activities or functions performed offshore or on-site previously."

Per Section III, Paragraph 2.C of the Addendum to Exhibit 'C' of the JOA, 'Each participant shall maintain auditable records to support any charges made by it to the Joint Account and shall be subject to the audit requirements provided in Section I Paragra ph 5 of this Exhibit 'C" as to such charges. The Partner does not agree with the Operators position that proof of activities performed offshore or on-site previously is not required to be provided.

Additionally, the Settlement Agreement specific to Chevron and Shell has additional language indicating the function must have been previously performed offshore/onsite but have been relocated onshore in order to be chargeable. The Operator has not provided documentation to verify the original location of these roles.

The Operator is requested to provide supporting documentation or credit the Great White Joint Account $328,902.14 ($168,581.54 plus burden and benefits of $122,482.30 plus overhead of $37,838.30) with reference to Chevron's audit number and exception number on the Joint Interest Billing.

replies.text:
Credit Denied

Planners, schedulers, plan execution supporters, and other roles working on drilling, completions, facility maintenance, well maintenance operations, and turnaround activities were previously performed offshore. However, industry practices have relocated these roles onshore, focusing on the function rather than the location of the individual. Therefore, these activities, although performed onshore, are directly chargeable to the joint account for the operation of the asset.

The 2019 Settlement Agreement between Shell and Chevron clarifies that these technical roles, are defined by their function rather than their location. The Settlement Agreement does not require the Operator to demonstrate that the roles were previously performed onsite/offshore.

It has been concluded in the Face-to-face meeting that both parties will escalate to their respective commercial teams.

This is the Statement of Clarification and Intent as it relates to Major Construction projects:

This section is applicable to technical labor/services. The personnel taken exception to by the auditor does not qualify for this section. Auditor did not provide Staff listing showing what position or function that each of the Operating personnel fulfills. Operator is providing here.

## SECTION III, PARAGRAPH 2.B.:

In order to clarify "engineering, design and drafting costs" chargeable under Section II, Paragraph 2.B of this Exhibit C, the following shall apply:

## a. SERVICES RENDERED BY OPERATOR'S EMPLOYEES

All salaries, wages, payroll burden and Personal Expenses of personnel performing technical services for the benefit of the Joint Account in connection with the design, construction, and installation of the Major Construction project shall be charged direct regardless of location. Such personnel shall be comprised of Operator's Producing and Exploration Department employees including engineers, environmentalists, technologists, engineering assistants, technicians, draftsmen, construction representatives, and other personnel performing technical services.

Salaries will be charged to the Joint Account based on actual days worked only when such time totals at least one day or more per month that is devoted to

the Major Construction project. Payroll burden and Personal Expenses associated with this labor will be charged to the Joint Account consistent with the provisions of Section II, Paragraph 2, Direct Charges - Labor and Paragraph 3, Direct Charges- Employee Benefits.

Personal Expenses include travel, accommodation, per-diem, meals, entertainment, and other reimbursable costs incurred by personnel whose salaries are chargeable to the Joint Account. Relocation costs may be chargeable only if the transfer is primarily for the benefit of the Joint Account and the employee is assigned to the Integrated Project Team for a minimum of twelve (12) months.

0006.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account for various material charges (material master types 1 and 7) on various projects. Information Request 001 was submitted requesting the WBS status which is required to complete reconciliations. The Operator replied to Information Request 001 that the WBS's are in release (REL)status. The WBS must be TECO'd before the reconciliation process can be performed.

0010.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $648,250.48 in Rig Direct Surcharge fees on multiple Tenaris invoices per the attached JADE. In IR 12, issued during the fieldwork, the Operator was requested to provide a copy of the contract relating to these fees. According to the vendor contract, these fees cover "Demand Sync, Logistics to Patterson, Storage + Maint. + WK, and Pipe Management Services".

Upon review of the Mars JOA, Exhibit C, Section III- "Demand Sync" is an administrative and management fee. "Storage + Maint. + WK" are various warehousing and inventory carrying costs, as is "Pipe Management Fee" all of which are included in the Overhead rate already reimbursed to the Operator and not directly changeable here. Exhibit 'C' Section III Overhead of the Unit Operating Agreement states: "As compensation for administrative, supervision, office services and warehousing costs, Operator shall charge the Joint Account in accordance with this Section III.'

Additionally, AG 19, Section IV.3.C states 'Actual costs may include costs of (I) Material, (2) making it suitable for use, and (3) transportation from the point of acquisition to the Joint Property including loading and unloading. Not included are storage or carrying costs."

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account for $648,250.48 plus overhead of 2.5%. for the fee which is not chargeable.

replies.text:
Credit denied.

Tenaris provides pipe management services, which include in-yard movement, inspection, tally, and preparation of pipes for running. They also provide technical services to reduce operational risk and optimize running times by ensuring the right practices are followed and products are installed at the rig site. Tenaris's fee is a component cost of the underlying goods and services, and it does not qualify as administrative costs covered under Overhead.

The chargeable amounts are limited to periods of six (6) months or less occurring prior to execution of the project. After use of the material or equipment for the Joint Operation is complcted, the equipment or material storage costs will no longer be charged to the Joint Account unless the Parties have agreed in writing that the material or equipment is a critical spare.

0020.description:
The Operator charged the Mars Joint Account $603,251.21 on various Sumitomo Corporation Of Americas invoices for SCM Fee Consignment charges. This is a management fee and is not a direct cost of the material but an additional fee to house the material and ensure it is available when needed.

Exhibit 'C' Section III Overhead of the Unit Operating Agreement states: As compensation for administrative, supervision, office services and warehousing costs, Operator shall charge the Joint Account in accordance with this Section III.'

Additionally, AG 19, Section IV.3.C states 'Actual costs may include costs of (I) Material, (2) making it suitable for use, and (3) transportation from the point of acquisition to the Joint Property including loading and unloading. Not included are storage or carrying costs."

The Operator is requested to credit the joint account for $603,251.21 plus overhead of 2.5%.

replies.text:
Credit denied.

Sumitomo Supply Chain Management (SCM) fee is the Ancillary costs related to Sumitomo project management that is charged as part of the overall cost for provision of goods and services.

Per the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement, Section 3 Billing Disputes Paragraph l, third-party project management costs by such third party associated with a third party's provision of goods and services may be charged to the Joint Account as a component cost of the underlying goods and services and shall not be qualified as OTL, or as administrative costs covered under Overhead.

The Joint Account was charged $361,946.45 per the attached JADE lines.

We noted the individuals who were charged by Keystone were not on the Joint Property during the time for which they were charged. We summarized these individuals in question on the tabs called "OTL Labor--Track" and "OTL--invoices" on the attached file called "IR#21 Keystone Track updated" and requested the Operator to explain why these labor costs are chargeable per the Mars UOP and the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement.

After further examination, we also excluded personnel related to Track 7050947 and 7063807 since these are TAR related and Track 7063808 because these costs were related to Major Construction.

In its response to this request, the Operator simply notes that "Based on the confirmation from the Facility Team Lead", the costs are chargeable per Exhibit C, section 3, #2 (Feasibility and Project Studies) and #3 (Planners & schedulers, maintenance and TAR, rig administration) of the February 2019 Letter Agreement. However, the Operator did not provide any documentation to support such claims.

replies.text:
Based on the confirmation from Facility Team Lead, the labor costs from Keystone engineering in the invoices pertain to the below two activities that are permissible to be chargeable activities per the February 2019 Letter, page 9 'OTL-Chargeable Activities'.

## 2. Feasibility and Project Studies

OTL associated with approved field improvement or facility improvement projects and for feasibility studies undertaken to progress future projects is chargeable by the Operator.

## 3. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration

OTL is chargeable by the Operator to the joint account for planners, schedulers, and plan execution supporters working on facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities.

Simply making a statement and not providing any evidence is not sufficient documentation.

The Operator is requested to provide the following:

- a. Which individuals were working on Feasibility and Project Studies and what are these studies.
- b. We see the following administrative personnel who are not chargeable: Please explain why their costs are being charged when they are not technical labor.

Michelle Hartel, -- Sr. Planner/Scheduler. Susan Boudreaux-- Project Controls William Peyton-- Scheduler

The Operator is requested to provide the above information, or to credit the Joint Account $109,662.70 plus 13% OH for labor costs not chargeable per the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement or the JOA or any other Agreement.

Credit denied.

- (a). To further substantiate the nature of the work performed, we have provided the job descriptions for the respective individuals in the attached spreadsheet, which clearly demonstrate their direct involvement in engineering, project execution, and control activities supporting approved facility improvement projects.
- (b). All designers and engineers directly contributed technical input to the projects they supported, including the preparation and review of engineering calculations, piping models, and technical drawings required to execute approved facility improvement scopes. Their work involved applying engineering judgment, resolving design challenges, and incorporating multidiscipline technical inputs to ensure that deliverables met applicable technical and safety requirements.

Document Control and Project Controls provided essential project support through revision control of engineering deliverables, management of drawing updates, cost tracking, and coordination of drafting activities. This support was particularly critical during the review and issuance of piping isometric drawings, where multiple sources of technical feedback were received, consolidated, tracked, and resolved to ensure accuracy, traceability, and proper approval prior to final issue.

Project Managers integrated the efforts of all disciplines, led assurance activities including Management of Change (MOC), coordinated third-party engineering and construction vendors, and supported technical troubleshooting required to progress the work safely and efficiently. Their role ensured that project scope, cost, schedule, and technical requirements were aligned with approved objectives and that all assurance and governance requirements were satisfied.

Collectively, these activities directly supported facility improvement projects that were reviewed and approved by the asset FIMP budget holder and executed in accordance with the AFE work process. The work performed represents direct project execution and assurance support for approved capital and facility improvement activities, rather than general overhead or administrative functions.

These activities are project-specific, technically driven, and directly attributable to approved facility improvements as per the February 2019 Letter, 3. OTL-Chargeable Activities.

## 3. Planners & Schedulers, maintenance and turnaround, rig administration

execution supporters working on facility maintenance, well maintenance and turnaround activities.

0028.description:
The Operator charged the Joint Account $126,324.66 according to the attached JADE lines for various SIEP invoices. Upon review of the invoices, the following discrepancies and issues were noted:

6706082871 ($48,679.52): The Invoice reflects a charge code of ZZPT/044495/012904 however none of the timesheets or supporting invoices have cost charged to this code.

67706082880 ($22,202.67): The invoice does not have any timesheets or other documents to verify the hours charged. There are only some EDI invoices that do not tie in any way to the main SIEP invoice

6706082155 ($12,981.45): The charge code on this invoice is ZZPT/044495/016704 yet no timesheets or other documents like expense reports reflect this charge code.

6706082867 ($24,269.70): The charge code on this invoice is ZZPT/0444495/016404. Upon review of the timesheets for this invoice they reflect activities such as "Travel to Lafayette to perform supplier audit". Per the Mars UOA Section III Overhead, Auditing is covered by Overhead and not allowed as a direct charge.

670682884 ($8,447.99): No timesheets or other documents were provided to account for the labor costs. The only documents provided were some EDI invoices that do not match the SIEP invoices.

6706082868 ($6,969.35): The Charge code on this invoice is ZZPT/044495/015504. Upon review of the timesheets this is for audit work: "Travel to Broussard, LA to perform audit.". Auditing is not chargeable to the Joint Account per the Mars UOA exhibit "C" Section III Overhead.

6706082833 ($2,000.25): There were no timesheets provided to account for the labor, just some EDI invoices which do not relate to the charges.

6706082712 ($773.73): This is for audit work which is not chargeable to the Joint Account per Mars UOA Section III Overhead:

This was the subject of IR 28 issued during the fieldwork, to which the Operator responded:

replies.text:
05/08/2025

These costs are not auditing charges rather these are Quality assurance check charges done with respect to efficient well execution and maintaining the operation of the tool and minimize risk of downtime due to tool failures. :-Swami

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $126,324.66 plus OH for vendor auditing not chargeable.

Credit denied.

The Auditor asserts that certain invoices lack adequate timesheet support and rely on EDI documentation. This position ignores standard Shell vendor billing practices where EDI invoices are the primary system-generated source document, timesheets are not always produced at the individual invoice line level, labor is billed under master service agreements with embedded scope definitions.

The absence of standalone timesheets does not invalidate the charge where the invoice ties to a valid service order, the work scope aligns with operational execution, the costs are consistent with similar charges historically accepted on the asset.

The operator noted that there were some typos on the invoices

6706082871 - the charge code 12904 should be 12903.

6706082867 - the charge code 16404 should be 16403

6706082155 - the charge code 16704 should be 16703

The timesheet attached to the invoice supplied the supporting information.

The Auditor characterizes the challenged costs as 'vendor auditing' and therefore non-chargeable under Mars UOA Exhibit C, Section III (Overhead). This characterization is factually and contractually incorrect.

The invoices cited relate to supplier quality assurance, tool readiness verification, and field-level execution support activities, not internal or financial audit functions.

These activities are operational in nature, performed to:

-  Verify tool condition and readiness prior to deployment
-  Minimize non-productive time (NPT)
-  Reduce operational risk and well execution failure

They are not corporate audit, compliance audit, or vendor financial audit activities.

Mars UOA Exhibit C, Section III excludes auditing from direct chargeability. However, this exclusion applies to Internal audits, financial audits, Compliance audits, Management or governance oversight. It does not apply to field-level quality assurance and operational verification activities that are integral to drilling and completion execution.

Under COPAS principles, cost allowability is determined by the nature of the work performed, not the terminology used in an expense description.

These costs are not auditing charges rather these are Quality assurance check charges done with respect to efficient well execution and maintaining the operation of the tool and minimize risk of downtime due to tool failures.

The Operator has inferred that the costs here are QA/QC related, however the cost for those types of inspections is coded as such, and not "supplier audit" as has been done here. Additionally, auditing is contrary to the Feb 2019 Letter Agreement, snipped below, which states that auditing is specifically covered by the Overhead rate.

For the avoidance of doubt Technical Employces do not includeprocurement, administration, accountingand auditing, pipeline nominations and scheduling, human resources, management, sup ( cnl o l ces handling taxation matters, permitting/regulatory work, land and division order services. Overhead charges are compensation for all costs and expenses associated with such functions, including the salaries or wages plus applicable payroll burdens, benefits, and personal expenses of personnel performing such functions, as well as their office and other support costs.

The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $126,324.66 plus OH for supplier (vendor) auditing not chargeable.

The Joint Account was charged $1,152,971.53 in Crane costs per the attached JADE lines. We can see that for these JADE lines, the 5 events that were allocated to were as follows:

|                  | UTS | MMH 4600 AM 315/4359.AM 41.00         |                |
