01.description: The Operator charged the Sparta Joint Account $2,000.00 on Grand Isle Shipyard work ticket no. 10123-4756-0001 for centralizer fabrication services. 02.description: The Operator charged the Sparta Joint Account $326,216.00 for P&T labor related to Senior Reservoir Engineer Daniel Weber for the period from January 1, 2024, to June 27, 2024. Additionally, the Joint Account was charged $208,930.98 for the same employee during the same period, which includes $121,827.08 for company labor and an associated payroll burden of $87,103.90. The SAP timesheet for Daniel Weber indicates that he is part of the Sparta subsurface SEPCO employee time reporting to the Sparta execution WBS from January 2, 2024, through March 26, 2025. It appears that the P&T labor charges for Daniel Weber are duplicate charges, as his time has already been accounted for in the Joint Account through company payroll and burden. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $339,264.64 ($326,216.00 plus 4% Project Rate overhead) for these duplicate charges.

03.description: The Operator charged the Sparta Joint Account $33,533.10 from Cenergy International Services. The Track System timesheet documentation provided by the Operator indicates that the services rendered by Don Sutton pertained to GOM ONS SAP Master Data 3. Activities involving the maintenance of SAP master data are administrative and accounting in nature, and as such, should be classified as overhead rather than direct charges to the joint account. According to Section III of the Accounting Procedure Exhibit "C", which addresses Overhead, the following applies: *"As compensation for costs not specifically identified as chargeable to the Joint Account pursuant* *to Section II (Direct Charges), the Operator shall charge the Joint Account in accordance with this* *Section III. The Parties specifically recognize that functions described in this Section III shall be* *directly chargeable when performed by personnel assigned to a feasibility team or an Integrated* *Project Team and within a scope of work, as approved by the Parties under the Agreement.* *Functions compensated by the overhead rates regardless of whether they are performed by the* *Operator, Operator’s Affiliates or third parties and regardless of location, include, but are not* *limited to, the following:"* • administration • accounting and auditing The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $34,874.42 ($33,533.10 plus 4% Project Rate overhead) for charges covered by overhead.

04.short_description: Cost Covered by Overhead - Shell India Marketing
04.description: The Operator charged the Sparta Joint Account $149,237.00 from Shell India Marketing for procurement services. The Operator provided the names of the four CP Specialists in response to IR16. These specialists are not listed on the IPT project team organizational chart. Procurement services are considered indirect costs covered by overhead. According to Section III of the Accounting Procedure Exhibit "C", which addresses Overhead, the following applies: *"As compensation for costs not specifically identified as chargeable to the Joint Account pursuant* *to Section II (Direct Charges), the Operator shall charge the Joint Account in accordance with this* *Section III. The Parties specifically recognize that functions described in this Section III shall be* *directly chargeable when performed by personnel assigned to a feasibility team or an Integrated* *Project Team and within a scope of work, as approved by the Parties under the Agreement.* *Functions compensated by the overhead rates regardless of whether they are performed by the* *Operator, Operator’s Affiliates or third parties and regardless of location, include, but are not* *limited to, the following:"* • procurement services, and land and division order services, in support of Joint Operations The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $155,206.48 ($149,237.00 plus 4% Project Rate overhead) for charges covered by overhead.

05.description: The Operator charged the Sparta Joint Account a total of $104,613,768.47 from the vendors Stena Drilling and NOV for milestone payments associated with 20K rig upgrades to the Stena Evolution drilling unit. These capital costs include, but are not limited to, the procurement of engineering, design, testing, materials, and fabrication of drilling equipment and pressure control systems specifically BOP's and associated riser equipment all designed to significantly enhance the unit’s operational capabilities. This exception is a continuation of Audit Exception No. 14 (2024SOV\_E116) submitted in 2024. While the Operator has indicated that Sparta is currently the only 20K project on Shell’s rig schedule, the absence of a definitive long-term drilling program leaves open the possibility that Stena Evolution, along with its substantial 20K upgrades, could be utilized on future HPHT joint ventures. Based on the Operator’s response to IR01, the upgrade of the Stena Evolution’s dynamic positioning system suggests that the rig is being configured for long-term, multi-project deployment within Shell’s drilling program. COPAS MFI-56 emphasizes that when modifications are made to enhance a rig’s capabilities, particularly when those enhancements extend the rig’s utility beyond a single project, costs should be shared proportionally among all benefiting properties over the life of the rig contract. This principle is especially relevant if the Operator exercises a contract extension or reassigns the upgraded rig to other joint ventures. Additionally, under the Sparta JOA, capital/controllable equipment such as advanced drilling and pressure control systems are subject to salvage and disposal provisions. If such equipment is deemed surplus at the end of Sparta operations, the Operator is required to notify the parties and obtain approval for its disposal. Until the Operator can definitively demonstrate that the Stena Evolution and the associated upgrades will be used exclusively for Sparta, the non-operator reserves the right to challenge the handling of these costs to the Sparta Joint Account. This exception will remain classified as T.B.D. (To Be Determined) pending further review and evaluation by the non-operator.

06.short_description: Rig Modifications - Enhanced Drilling MPD System
06.description: The Operator charged the Sparta Joint Account a total of $318,704.00 from the vendor Enhanced Drilling on various invoices for FEED studies associated with a Dual Subsea Pump Module (SPM) system. These capital costs include the procurement of engineering, design, and assessment of pressure management equipment designed to significantly enhance a rig's operational capabilities. Based on Enhanced Drilling’s scope of work provided in response to IR04, the FEED studies include a comprehensive engineering and operational evaluation for the integrating of a second EC-Drill Pump Module into the existing EC-Drill system onboard the Stena Evolution drilling unit. In the absence of a definitive long-term drilling plan, there remains a possibility that the Stena Evolution, along with its MPD upgrades, could be deployed on future Shell joint ventures. As such, it is uncertain at this time whether these enhancements will exclusively benefit the Sparta project. COPAS MFI-56 emphasizes that when modifications are made to enhance a rig’s capabilities, particularly when those enhancements extend the rig’s utility beyond a single project, costs should be shared proportionally among all benefiting properties over the life of the rig contract. This principle is especially relevant if the Operator exercises a contract extension or reassigns the upgraded rig to other joint ventures. Additionally, under the Sparta JOA, capital/controllable equipment such as advanced pressure management systems are subject to salvage and disposal provisions. If such equipment is deemed surplus at the end of operations, the Operator is required to notify the Parties and obtain approval for its disposal. Until the Operator can definitively demonstrate that the Stena Evolution and its MPD upgrades will be used exclusively for Sparta, the non-operator reserves the right to challenge the handling of these costs to the Sparta Joint Account. This exception will remain classified as T.B.D. (To Be Determined) pending further review and evaluation by the non-operator.

07.description: The Operator charged the Sparta Joint Account $7,500.000.00 from the vendor Trendsetter Engineering on invoice no. SI06682 for cost related to 20K Open Water Intervention Riser System (OWIRS). In response to IR17, which requested a more detailed breakdown of the scope of services included in the invoice, the Operator stated only that the OWIRS was designed to provide well access to subsea wells for the purpose of well workover and intervention operations without providing any cost component detail. While the cost may not be directly related to a rig modification, it aligns with the category of “Intervention Units” as defined in COPAS MFI-56. According to Section XVII, such costs are to be treated and allocated in the same manner as Rig-Related costs. Given the absence of a detailed cost breakdown and the possibility that the OWIRS equipment and services may be utilized on other properties beyond Sparta, we request the Operator provide additional details as to the future handling of these cost. Additionally, under the Sparta JOA, capital/controllable equipment such as advanced intervention equipment is subject to salvage and disposal provisions. If such equipment is deemed surplus at the end of operations, the Operator is required to notify the Parties and obtain approval for its disposal. Until the Operator can definitively demonstrate that the OWIRS cost will be used exclusively for Sparta, the non-operator reserves the right to challenge the handling of these costs to the Sparta Joint Account. This exception will remain classified as T.B.D. (To Be Determined) pending further review and evaluation by the non-operator.

08.short_description: Sales Tax Not Chargeable - NOV Invoice No. 22099
08.description: The Sparta Joint Account was charged $993,922.80 from the vendor National Oilwell on milestone invoice no. 22099 for a CDX-2030 Wellhead Connector. A review of the invoice revealed the vendor applied a 9.85% sales tax. State and local tax regulations prohibit the application of sales tax to oil and gas equipment and services delivered or used in offshore federal waters. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $92,687.71 ($89,122.80 plus $3,564.91 Project overhead) for sales tax charged in error.

09.description: The Operator charged the Sparta Joint Account $4,396,665.32 for 1,123,643 gallons of rig fuel consumed by the Deepwater Poseidon during the period January 30, 2023, through April 30, 2023. This amount includes two direct fuel purchases from Shell Trading (invoice nos. 13292007 and 12688060) as well as multiple fuel true-up entries posted throughout 2023 and 2024. This exception replaces Audit Exception No. 01 (2024SOV\_E116), originally submitted in 2024. Since rig fuel is charged on a usage-based methodology, several concerns have been identified regarding the pricing and handling of rig fuel during the Sparta campaign: 1. Lack of Formal Procedures There are no documented rig fuel pricing procedures in place to govern the handling, allocation, or reconciliation of fuel costs. 2. Inconsistent Pricing The final 2024 true-up rate charged to Sparta was $3.91 per gallon. However, two direct STUSCO fuel deliveries reflected lower market rates of $3.81 and $3.19 per gallon, respectively, raising concerns about pricing consistency and transparency. 3. Miscoded Fuel Transfer The fuel delivery associated with Shell Trading Invoice 12688060, dated November 25, 2022, should have been charged to the Abilene project, not Sparta. 4. Overstated Fuel Volumes Rig Fuel Usage Reports show a total of 810,850 gallons of fuel was delivered on March 3–4, 2023, while the corresponding STUSCO invoice no. 13292007 reflects only 800,000 gallons, indicating a 10,850-gallon discrepancy recorded. In the absence of formal internal procedures, COPAS MFI-45 (Marine and Aircraft Offshore Transportation) provides relevant guidance, stating: *“Diesel should be charged to the Joint Account based on the weighted average price during the month... fuel cost for the month should be divided by the total number of gallons purchased during the month. The beginning inventory should be included in the calculation at the previous month’s calculated weighted average price.”* At the start of the Sparta campaign, the Deepwater Poseidon rig arrived with 1,189,435 gallons of fuel onboard, carried over from the Abilene project and priced at $3.84/gal. During the campaign, an additional 800,000 gallons was delivered on March 3–4, 2023 at $3.19/gal (STUSCO Invoice No. 13292007). Using the COPAS-recommended weighted average price (WAP) method, the appropriate rate for fuel charged to Sparta should have been: Instead, the Operator applied $3.91/gal, resulting in an overcharge of $0.32/gal, or approximately $359,565.76. Operator's Applied Rate vs. COPAS WAP Method The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $373,948.39 ($359,565.76 plus $14,382.63 Project overhead) for rig fuel calculated in error.

attachments: Poseidon - Rig Fuel Usage-Inventory Report by Project.xlsx

10.error_type: 22.0 Incomplete or Lack of Procedures and Controls
10.description: The Operator charged the Sparta Joint Account $96,878,204.40 for labor cost related to P&T employees and contract personnel provided by its affiliate, Shell International Exploration & Production (SIEP) in 2023 and 2024. These charges span multiple disciplines and international locations, representing a significant share of the total venture costs. Under Section 5.C of the Sparta Unit Operating Agreement (UOA), affiliate labor must be charged strictly on a cost basis, meaning the charges must reflect actual costs incurred without any profit component or duplication. To support this, the UOA requires the affiliate to provide an annual attestation report from an independent public accounting firm, confirming that the charges: • Represent a complete and accurate allocation of costs, • Do not contain a profit component, • Exclude any duplication of costs. During audit fieldwork, the Operator provided a 2023 attestation report prepared by an independent firm. However, the report contains redacted sections and omits critical confirmations required under the Sparta UOA, specifically: • The At Cost Statement and key cost allocation methodologies were intentionally blacked out. • The report does not explicitly affirm that the charges exclude profit or duplication. • No billing rates by role, discipline, are disclosed, despite such detail being standard in similar industry attestation/assurance reviews to support cost validation. • The procedures performed were limited to sample-based testing, without full transparency into allocation keys or reconciliation of actual costs. Additionally, the audit identified a specific instance of duplicate time writing for one P&T individual whose labor was billed through both the SIEP affiliate and SEPCO company labor during the same time period (See AE02). This directly contradicts the UOA’s requirement to exclude duplication and raises concerns about the integrity of the affiliate billing process. These omissions and findings materially impair the co-owners’ ability to verify that the affiliate charges are consistent with the cost basis principle. The lack of explicit language regarding profit exclusion and duplication, combined with evidence of actual duplicate billing, undermines the reliability of the attestation and the Operator’s compliance with contractual obligations. The co-owner acknowledges and continues to adhere to the confidentiality obligations set forth in the Sparta Unit Operating Agreement. In light of these obligations, the co-owner respectfully requests that the Operator provide unredacted copies of the 2023 and 2024 affiliate attestation reports or equivalent documentation and ensure that future affiliate assurance reports include the necessary disclosures referenced above to support audit verification. 04.short_description: Cost Covered by Overhead - Hydrocarbon Engineering
04.description: The Vito Joint Account, Production Operations - BI (AFE O.US.VTO.VTO.001.71300) was charged a total of $106,145.00 from various Hydrocarbon Engineering invoices for Measurement and Allocation and Multi Phase FlowMeter services. A review of helicopter manifests indicates these services were performed offsite. Because these charges were billed directly to a Vito operating AFE, they should be governed by Section III (Overhead) of the COPAS Model Form Accounting Procedure (1986 non-PTAP edition), which serves as the base accounting procedure for offshore joint operations. This procedure establishes that overhead recovery is intended to cover administrative and technical costs not directly chargeable under Section II. Section III of the 1986 Offshore Model Form provides: *“Except as otherwise provided in Paragraph 2 of this Section III, the salaries, wages, and Personal Expenses of Technical Employees and/or costs of professional consultant services and contract services of technical personnel either temporarily or permanently assigned to and directly employed in the operation of the Joint Property…* *(X) Shall be covered by the overhead rates.”* Paragraph 2.B. & C. (Overhead – Major Construction) expressly references the Addendum (Statement of Clarification & Intent), which is a supplemental provision to the 1986 Offshore Model Form. The Addendum expands direct chargeability for Major Construction and Project Team activities, but it does not override Section III for routine production operations. Its “regardless of location” language applies exclusively to Major Construction and Project Team activities under Section III.2.B and III.2.C. There is no language extending this exception to routine production technical personnel working remotely. Therefore, Section III (Overhead) of the 1986 Offshore Model Form governs these charges. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $119,943.85 ($106,145.00 plus 13% Operating overhead) for these technical services that are covered by overhead.

05.short_description: Costs Covered by Overhead - Petroleum Coordinators
05.description: The Vito Joint Account, drilling wells VA007–VA009 and VA012, were charged a total of $214,414.12 from various Petroleum Coordinators invoices for Equipment Integrity Analysts, Equipment Support Technicians, and other technical and administrative personnel. A review of invoice support indicates these services were performed offsite either from home or from Shell’s Woodcreek and Hancock Whitney office locations. Because these charges were billed directly to Vito drilling AFEs, they should be governed by Section III (Overhead) of the COPAS Model Form Accounting Procedure (1986 non-PTAP edition), which serves as the base accounting procedure for offshore joint operations. This procedure establishes that overhead recovery is intended to cover administrative and technical costs not directly chargeable under Section II. Section III of the 1986 Offshore Model Form provides: *“Except as otherwise provided in Paragraph 2 of this Section III, the salaries, wages, and Personal Expenses of Technical Employees and/or costs of professional consultant services and contract services of technical personnel either temporarily or permanently assigned to and directly employed in the operation of the Joint Property…* *(X) Shall be covered by the overhead rates.”* Paragraph 2.B. & C. (Overhead – Major Construction) expressly references the Addendum (Statement of Clarification & Intent), which is a supplemental provision to the 1986 Offshore Model Form. The Addendum expands direct chargeability for Major Construction and Project Team activities, but it does not override Section III for routine drilling operations. While the Addendum references Drilling Operations in its introductory scope, its “regardless of location” language applies exclusively to Major Construction and Project Team activities under Section III.2.B and III.2.C. There is no language extending this exception to routine drilling technical personnel working remotely. Therefore, Section III (Overhead) of the 1986 Offshore Model Form accounting procedure governs these charges. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $219,774.47 ($214,414.12 plus 2.5% Development Rate overhead) for these technical and administrative costs that are covered by overhead.

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

The auditor's position is based on a misapplication of Section III of the 1986 COPAS Offshore Model Form as Section III applies to Operator labor and embedded technical overhead, not third-party services contracted for drilling execution.

The costs charged for Equipment Integrity Analysts, Equipment Support Technicians, and related services were third-party expenditures contracted directly by the Operator for the direct and primary benefit of Drilling Operations on Vito wells VA007 - VA009 and VA012.

In accordance with the Vito Joint Operating Agreement, Exhibit 'C' Addendum, Section III(c) (Third -Party Costs Contracted by Operator), third-party expenditures incurred for the direct and primary benefit of Drilling Operations are directly chargeable to the Joint Account regardless of the location from which the services are performed. The services supported active drilling activities and were necessary to maintain equipment integrity and operational reliability during drilling.

These costs represent third-party contractor services, not Operator employee labor or administrative overhead, and therefore are appropriately charged direct under the Vito Accounting Procedure.

## c. THIRD-PARTY COSTS CONTRACTED BY OPERATOR

All third-party expenditures, resulting from agreements made directly with the Operator, for the direct and primary benefit of the design, construction and installation of the Major Construction projects or Drilling Operations,regardless of location, will bedirect charged by the Operator to the Joint Account Third-party expenditures shall include but not be limited to

- Contractors, consultants and service companies
- Fabrication, construction installation and commissioning activities and associated Ct
- Specialized equipment, materials, testing or other services (including software and specialized computer applications)
- Research and development, prototype studies, design and development work
- Conceptual work/studies
- On-site construction representatives and inspectors and associated cost
- Real Time Operations Center (RTOC), or any successor facılity, providing similar services The net daily cost for the RTOC is allocated to the rigs using the facılity based on the number and operation types of rigs using the facility

22.short_description: Improper Coding of Deepwater Pontus MPD/CML Rig Upgrades
22.description: The Operator charged the Vito Joint Account (VA010 and VA011 wells) $5,357,376.00 from multiple Enhanced Drilling (EDI) milestone invoices for CML pump and seal upgrades on the Deepwater Pontus drillship. These upgrades included installing higher-capacity motors and CaBr2 and ZnBr2 seal upgrades to SPM-63 and SPM-64, and modifying the subsea interface and control system for increased power. This exception is a continuation of Exception No. 53 from last year’s audit (Shell File No. 2024SOV\_E117). During fieldwork, IR59 was submitted requesting confirmation on whether the upgraded SPMs were deployed on Frio GD011 or demobilized after Deepwater Pontus left Vito. In response the Operator stated: *“Shell and Equinor jointly determined that the upgrade was necessary for the Vito project. Both companies agreed to invest in this upgrade solely for Vito, and at the time, there was no other operational justification for Shell to initiate the enhancement. As such, the full cost of the equipment was appropriately charged to Vito’s Joint Account, irrespective of any subsequent or potential use on other assets. Shell’s position remains unchanged and does not support any reallocation or modification in the cost treatment.”* As stated in last year’s audit exception, the Annual Operating Plan did not provide co-owner visibility into these rig upgrades, despite their classification as a capital project exceeding the $3 million threshold outlined in the UOA. This requirement remains unchanged, and the lack of disclosure continues to raise concerns regarding compliance with Article 6.7.3.1, which explicitly mandates that significant capital projects, including equipment additions, expansions, or upgrades be identified in the Annual Operating Plan. The omission of these details limits transparency and prevents co-owners from fully assessing the financial impact and potential cross-venture benefits of such upgrades. While AFE approval provides a basis for charging Vito, it does not override the UOA’s requirement for proportional cost allocation when equipment benefits multiple properties. Article 6.7.3.1 obligates disclosure of major upgrades and equitable sharing of costs for joint operations. The MPD/CML Letter of Agreement and EDI’s SPM upgrade proposal confirm these enhancements were designed for multi-well and multi-rig use across Shell’s broader program, making full allocation to Vito inconsistent with UOA principles. COPAS MFI-56 emphasizes that when modifications are made to enhance a rig’s capabilities, particularly when those enhancements extend the rig’s utility beyond a single project cost should be shared proportionally among all benefiting properties over the life of the rig contract. This principle is especially relevant if the Operator exercises a contract extension or reassigns the upgraded rig to other joint ventures. The non-operator has confirmed that one of two of the upgraded Subsea Pump Module (SPM), specifically SPM-64, was commissioned and placed into service on July 4, 2024, as identified on the Daily Operations Reports. This date marks the start of amortization consistent with the Operator’s rig-related cost allocation methodology. As a result, 1,054 days associated with this upgrade should have been proportionately allocated to other non-Vito properties for the duration of the drilling contract, as detailed in the attached "Motor & Seal Upgrade Schedule.” The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $4,560,229.81 ($4,449,004.69 plus 2.5% Development Rate overhead) for upgrades that should have been proportionally allocated across all benefiting wells.

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

The MPD/CML motor and seal upgrades were undertaken to meet the specific pressure regime, well design, and drilling requirements of the Vito development wells. At the time the decision was made, there was no approved drilling program, commitment, or obligation to deploy the Deepwater Pontus to other projects requiring these enhancements.

The UOA and Accounting Procedure do not require the Operator to retrospectively re-allocate costs based on speculative or potential future use of equipment following completion of a project. Costs are chargeable based on the purpose and necessity at the time incurred, which in this case was exclusively Vito.

Pursuant to UOA Article 6.3 (Authorizations for Expenditures), the Operator issued an AFE that explicitly included the MPD/CML upgrades. The AFE was reviewed and approved by the co-owners prior to execution, thereby authorizing the Operator to incur and charge the associated costs to the Vito Joint Account.

Once approved, the AFE constitutes the contractual mechanism by which expenditures are authorized and charged. The audit process is not intended to retroactively reopen or recharacterize approved AFEs absent a clear violation of the UOA or Accounting Procedure, neither of which exists here.

UOA Article 6.7.3.1 requires that the AOP identify material activities, including significant capital projects, for planning and transparency purposes.

However, UOA Article 6.7.4 explicitly states that the AOP is informational only and 'shall not obligate any Party to expend f unds nor limit expenditures otherwise authorized under an approved AFE.'

- 6.7.4 Effect of the Annual Operating Plan: The Annual Operating Plan shall be primarily for informational and planning purposes and shall not obligate any Party to any expenditures or constitute an Election to participate in any specific operation. However, the Annual Oet o d p e ind ies during the year while providing for input from the Non-Operators. Pursuant to the terms amons s ons s s s s s t os iceh were not included in the Annual Operating Plan. Approval of any such operation, under the terms provided in Article 8 (Voting and Elections), shall be deemed a modification to the Annual Operating Plan.

The auditor's reliance on COPAS MFI -56 is misplaced. MFI-56 addresses circumstances where equipment modifications are intentionally made to enhance a rig's capabilities for use across multiple properties as part of a broader drilling program. That is not the fact pattern here. The MPD/CML upgrades were justified, approved, and executed to enable Vito drilling, not to enhance the rig for general fleet or multi-venture use.

26.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged $4,158,032.00 for Waterflood CAR insurance covering the period from July 1, 2024, to May 31, 2027. The operator charged the full insurance premium to the Joint Account and billed the non-operator for its share of this amount. The operator should not have expensed the entire insurance amount or billed the JV partner the full premium upfront, as the insurance coverage spans 35 months. Instead, the operator should have billed the JV partner only for the portion of the insurance applicable to the current accounting period. Given that the insurance covers the period from July 1, 2024, to May 31, 2027, the operator should calculate the pro-rata share of the insurance cost for the portion of 2024 for which the JV partner is responsible. The monthly CAR insurance cost is $118,800.91, leading to total costs for 2024 of $1,425,610.97. Consequently, the operator over-billed the Joint Account by $2,732,421.03 for CAR insurance costs in 2024. In response to IR29, the operator stated that quarterly amortization is performed only for Shell Share. This practice does not align with the general accounting principles for the treatment of prepaid expenses. Additionally, although the operator recognized the appropriate accounting treatment for handling this prepayment, it failed to apply the same treatment to its partner, inconsistent with its own accounting practices. Therefore, the operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $2,732,421.03 for the overcharge of the prepaid insurance premium.

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

The Waterflood (CAR) insurance premium totaling USD 4.15 million was remitted in full to the insurance provider (Marsh) to secure coverage for the entire policy period from 1 July 2024 to 31 May 2027, in accordance with the insurance contract requirements. The full payment was necessary to bind and maintain uninterrupted insurance coverage over the full construction period.

With respect to accounting treatment, the Operator has applied its standard and established practice for CAR insurance across Operator-operated assets. Under this practice, the full Waterflood CAR insurance invoice is initially paid to the vendor and recorded in the insurance cost account, following which the Shell share is reclassified from the insurance expense account (A8386060) to the Shell prepaid insurance account. The Shell prepaid balance is then amortized on a quarterly basis over the coverage period, in line with Shell's internal accounting policies.

In this specific instance, Equinor's share was processed through the standard JV cutback mechanism. COPAS governs where a cost is properly chargeable to the Joint Account based on incurrence and operational relevance. It does not impose any requirement to defer or amortize prepaid costs for Joint Interest Billing purposes. The auditor's position improperly imports financial reporting concepts (matching principle and amortization) into a contractual cost recovery framework, which COPAS does not support. The Operator billed exactly what it paid for the benefit of the Joint Account.

Therefore, the full premium was correctly paid to the insurer to obtain coverage for the entire policy period, and Equinor's share was processed in line with the Operator's established JV accounting and cutback practices. As such, the billing reflect s the invoiced and paid insurance premium rather than a pro-rata amortized amount for the non-operator share.

28.short_description: Affiliate Contract Labor Billed at Flat Rate
28.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged $2,468,991.00 for P&T labor associated with 19 contractors from 11 suppliers at the affiliate flat rate. The affiliate labor charges were manually adjusted from the SIEP invoices to replace the original invoice rates with the escalated affiliate rates. These contractors are not on the consolidated P&T staff listing but on the contractor listing. Their services were billed at the affiliate flat rates instead of the actual cost as listed on the affiliate invoices. The total amount charged to the Joint Account from these contractors is $2,468,991.00 for 6,378.50 hours. The actual costs based on the SIEP invoices is $1,275,987, resulted in a overcharge of $1,193,004.00 at the higher flat rates. These personnel are contractors from various vendors including GATE, NES Global, Risktec, Turner & Townsend, Worley Group, Wood Group, Total System, EDG, Intertek, SGS North America and Nextsource. The Accounting Procedure, section 5. Services, allows “the cost of contract services, equipment, and utilities used in the conduct of Joint Operations” to be a direct cost. There is no place in the Unit Operating Agreement that allows a vendor’s contractor to be up charged. The flat rate was intended as a way for the Operator to easily recover its employee costs without the requirement to calculate and provide support for salary, benefit, and burden. It was not intended to circumvent vendor costs being billed at the actual cost paid by the Operator. In addition, charging vendor employees through the P&T labor also creates the risk of duplicate costs by directly charging the vendor invoice and also billing that contractor on the monthly P&T Labor entry. The Operator is requested to provide vendor contract with the contractors to show that they were hired by the Affiliate as their contractors to perform IPT work as directed by the project manager. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $1,216,864.08 ($1,193,004.00 plus $23,860.08 overhead) for over-charge of contractors costs at all-inclusive flat rates instead of the actual costs.

The above Gulf of Mexico all-inclusive standard rate shall be adjusted on the first day of April each year following the effective date of the Agreement. The adjustment shall be computed by applying the adjustment factor most recently published by COPAS in accordance with MFI 50 or its subsequent replacement pronouncement as accepted by COPAS. The adjusted rate shall be the rate specified above, as annually amended, increased or decreased by the adjustment factor described herein, for each year from the effective date of such rates in accordance with COPAS MFI-47 or its replacement pronouncement as accepted by COPAS. The adjusted rates shall be effective April 1 and shall continue to be effective through March 31 of the subsequent calendar year.

29.short_description: Improper Coding of DPN BOP Shear Ram Upgrade
29.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged a total of $1,696,728.46 (100%) for high-pressure shear ram upgrades for two Transocean-owned BOP stacks utilized aboard the Deepwater Pontus drillship. These upgrades were billed through a combination of accumulator entries unwound solely to Vito wells during the period of April 1, 2024, and October 20, 2024 for the first BOP stack and a direct charge on TOI invoice no. 9253 for the second. In response to IR66, the Operator provided the following methodology regarding accumulator costs: *"For accumulators, the start date is when the upgrade is confirmed by the business as ready for use, marking the beginning of cost unwinding. The end date aligns with the contract termination between SOI and SEPWES. Since SEPWES may allocate the rig to SOI or other affiliates, the contract with SOI is limited to one year. The contract end date for Pontus with SOI is 20th oct 2024..."* The non-operator is unable to independently verify the exact commissioning date of the BOP upgrades on the provided Daily Operations Reports. However, consistent with the Operator’s stated methodology, the commencement of cost unwinding for the upgrades are assumed to have begun on April 1, 2024, as indicated on the attached Accumulator Allocation worksheet. That said, the non-operator disagrees with the Operator’s position that the end date for cost unwinding should be determined by an internal agreement between its affiliates (SOI and SEPWES), particularly given that all rig-related charges were invoiced directly by Transocean. Instead, the non-operator maintains that the appropriate end date should be governed by Paragraph 15 of the HP Shear Upgrade Letter of Agreement dated April 5, 2023 executed between Shell (Company) and Transocean (Contractor), which states: *“COMPANY and CONTRACTOR agree that the HP Shear Upgrade shall remain installed on board the DRILLING UNIT up to and until the end of the CONTRACT DURATION…”* The BOP stacks, owned and provided by Transocean, are part of the rig’s standard well control & subsea equipment package included in the daily operating rate. As such, any upgrades to these components should be equitably allocated among all properties utilizing the rig throughout the contract term. Based on publicly available information, the underlying contract SEP-C-12-004 is scheduled to expire in October 2027. COPAS MFI-56 emphasizes that when modifications are made to enhance a rig’s capabilities, particularly when those enhancements extend the rig’s utility beyond a single project, costs should be shared proportionally among all benefiting properties over the life of the rig contract. This principle is especially relevant if the Operator exercises a contract extension or reassigns the upgraded rig to other joint ventures. The drilling contractor's BOP stack will be used on all properties served during the drilling campaign, therefore, the HP Shear Ram upgrade cost should be unwound from April 1, 2024, through the projected contract expiration in October 2027. As a result, 1,054 days associated with this upgrade should have been proportionately allocated to other non-Vito properties for the duration of the drilling contract, as detailed in the attached “Shear Ram Upgrade Schedule” tab. The Operator is requested to credit the Joint Account $1,359,119.99 ($1,325,970.72 plus 2.5% Development Rate overhead) for upgrades that should have been proportionally allocated across all benefiting wells.

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

To leverage Shell's market position and negotiating capability, Shell Exploration and Production Wells Equipment Services ('SEPWES') contracted for drilling rigs on a global basis, such as the Transocean -build Pontus rig used to drill Vito. When a Shell operating company, such as SOI, needs a drilling rig, the operating company looks to procure a rig through SEPWES. As such, SOI enters into a contract with SEPWES. Shell recovers mobilization and demobilization cost through the original contract period between SEPWES and SOI. There is no presumption that a contract extension will be executed, and therefore the operator must recover these costs in the contract period entered between SOI and SEPWES. This is consistent with COPAS MFI 56 guidance.

34.short_description: Overhead Incorrectly Assessed on P&T Labor
34.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged $14,582,897.00 for P&T labor related to IPT projects. The Operator applied a 2% overhead fee to these affiliate services, totaling $291,657.94. According to the addendum to Vito’s 1986 Accounting Procedure (non-PTAP), provision d., (ii) states: "The Major Construction rates provided in Exhibit 'C', Section III, Paragraph 2.C [If the Operator forms an Integrated Project Team and charges its costs directly to the Joint Account] shall provide compensation to the Operator for all personnel...and other support services provided by the Operator. Such rate [2%] shall be applied to the total cost (gross) incurred by the Joint Account excluding Affiliate charges." This provision indicates that the 2% overhead should not be applied to affiliate charges. Therefore, the Operator is requested to credit the Vito Joint Account $291,657.94 for the overhead incorrectly applied to P&T labor costs.

35.short_description: Overhead Incorrectly Assessed on P&T Non-Labor
35.description: The Operator charged the Vito Joint Account a total of $875,149.16 for P&T non-Labor costs associated with IPT projects. An overhead fee of 2%, amounting to $17,502.98, has been applied to these affiliate services. According to the addendum to Vito’s 1986 Accounting Procedure (non-PTAP), provision d., (ii) states: "The Major Construction rates provided in Exhibit 'C', Section III, Paragraph 2.C [If the Operator forms an Integrated Project Team and charges its costs directly to the Joint Account] shall provide compensation to the Operator for all personnel...and other support services provided by the Operator. Such rate [2%] shall be applied to the total cost (gross) incurred by the Joint Account excluding Affiliate charges." This addendum clarifies that the IPT overhead excludes charges related to affiliates. It does not specifically limit this exclusion to only P&T labor costs. Since P&T non-labor costs fall under affiliate charges, no overhead should be applied to these costs. The Operator is requested to credit the Vito Joint Account $17,502.98 for the overhead incorrectly applied to P&T non-Labor costs.

replies.text:
Credit Denied.

The addendum language cited is intended solely to prevent double recovery of affiliate labor and related support services that already embed overhead or compensation, not to exclude pass-through, non-labor project costs. The P&T non-labor costs in question are direct project expenditures and do not include affiliate labor, overhead, or profit. Therefore, they do not meet the definition of affiliate charges contemplated by the exclusion. Application of the 2% IPT overhead to these costs is fully consistent with the Accounting Procedure, and no credit is due.

36.description: The Vito Joint Account was charged a total of $1,785,614.91 for company labor costs associated with production operation projects, which includes a 13% overhead applied to these company labor services. This amount also includes $1,644,780.68 for employees who were offsite during production operations. Section III. (Overhead) of the Accounting Procedure indicates the parties choice for offsite technical services. ( x ) shall be covered by the overhead rates" The Addendum to Exhibit "C" further elucidates the chargeability of labor costs as outlined in Section III. In order to clarify the provisions of Exhibit "C", Section III, Overhead, Paragraph ii. and Paragraph 2. Overhead-Major Construction, the following shall apply: a. SERVICES RENDERED BY EMPLOYEES OF PARTICIPANTS (i) Exhibit "C", Section III, Paragraph 2B The rates provided in Exhibit "C", Section III, Paragraph 2B shall not provide for the following, and the following shall be directly billable to the Joint Account for services rendered by Operator's employees: (ii) Exhibit "C", Section III, Paragraph 2C The rates provided in Exhibit "C", Section III, Paragraph 2C shall not provide for the following, and the following shall be directly billable to the Joint Account for services rendered by participant's employees: Historically, the Operator has denied audit claims for offsite technical labor involved in production and drilling operations, citing the aforementioned Addendum.
